sources.title: Login for AWS local development using console credentials
supports: `aws login` needs AWS CLI 2.32.0 or later
Works for root, IAM user, and IAM federation sign-in; IAM Identity Center uses `aws configure sso` instead
Non-root identities need the SignInLocalDevelopmentAccess managed policy
Credentials refresh every 15 minutes; the session lasts up to the principal's session duration, 12 hours at most
Cache lives in ~/.aws/login/cache; `aws logout` deletes it

sources.title: Managing your costs with AWS Budgets
supports: Budget data is updated up to three times a day, typically 8-12 hours apart
A notification can arrive after spending has already passed the threshold

sources.title: AWS Free Tier
supports: New accounts receive USD 100 in credits and can earn up to USD 100 more
A Free plan account closes after 6 months or when credits run out, whichever is first, unless upgraded
Always-free offers apply on both Free and Paid plans
sources.note: The page does not state the account-creation date from which this model applies.

sources.title: Amazon CloudFront pricing (flat-rate plans)
supports: Flat-rate plans exist: Free USD 0, Pro USD 15, Business USD 200, Premium USD 1,000 per month
Flat-rate plans cannot be combined with other offers or discounts
sources.note: Which features and origins each plan allows, and CloudFormation/CDK support for selecting a plan, were not verified. The book's examples use pay-as-you-go.

supports: cdkd describes itself as for dev/test workflows and recommends the AWS CDK CLI for production

Pages are written as <path>/index.html; internal links end in /index.html
i18n uses a locale-prefixed file tree; ssg.localeSwitcher adds the language switcher
search-index.json is written to the output root; files under assets/ carry a content hash
codeImports enables `<<< @/path{region}` snippet imports

supports: run.tasks keys: command, cwd, dependsOn, cache
Tasks are cached by default and package.json scripts are not; `cache: false` cannot be overridden from the CLI
A task with `cache: false` receives the caller's full environment
`vp install --frozen-lockfile` runs the pinned package manager with that flag
Bundles vite 8.3.3, vitest 5.0.3, oxlint 1.87.0, oxfmt 0.72.0
`vp check`'s type check does not cover Vue single-file components

supports: `@vizejs/vite-plugin` default export is a Vite plugin that compiles Vue single-file components
`vize check` type-checks .vue and .ts files using the tsconfig include list
`vize lint` lints Vue templates; `--preset essential` selects the essential rules
Adding `@vizejs/vite-plugin` to compilerOptions.types lets TypeScript resolve .vue imports without a shim

There is no vite-plus attribute; `vp` is an unrelated package

sources.title: Restrict access to an Amazon S3 origin
supports: AWS recommends origin access control over origin access identity
The bucket policy allows the cloudfront.amazonaws.com service principal with an AWS:SourceArn condition naming the distribution
An S3 website endpoint is a custom origin and cannot use OAC
With signing behavior `always`, CloudFront always uses HTTPS to S3

sources.title: Choose between REST APIs and HTTP APIs
supports: HTTP APIs are designed with minimal features so that they can be offered at a lower price
REST API only: AWS WAF, API keys, per-client throttling, request validation, caching, private endpoints, X-Ray tracing, response streaming
HTTP API only: JWT authorizers, automatic deployments

sources.title: Cloudflare Workers: Local development
supports: Local development runs Workers in workerd through Miniflare, started by wrangler dev or the Cloudflare Vite plugin
Bindings connect to local simulations by default; `remote: true` on a binding sends its operations to the deployed resource
Workers AI has no local simulation: AI models always run remotely

sources.title: Cloudflare D1: Local development
supports: `wrangler dev` uses a local-only D1 by default and persists its data across runs
Local and remote data are separate; `--local` targets the local database for `wrangler d1 execute` and `wrangler d1 migrations apply`

sources.title: Quotas for HTTP APIs in API Gateway
supports: Maximum integration timeout is 30 seconds and cannot be increased
Payload size is 10 MB
300 routes per API by default

sources.title: Create AWS Lambda proxy integrations for HTTP APIs in API Gateway
supports: In payload format 2.0, duplicate headers are combined with commas and included in the headers field; there is no multiValueHeaders field
Format 2.0 has a cookies field for the request's cookies, and in the response each entry of cookies becomes a set-cookie header
All header names in the event are lowercased
The 2.0 event carries rawPath, rawQueryString, requestContext.domainName, requestContext.http.method, body, and isBase64Encoded
A customized 2.0 response has cookies, isBase64Encoded, statusCode, headers, and body

sources.title: Lambda quotas
supports: Function timeout is at most 900 seconds
Memory is 128 MB to 10,240 MB
Synchronous invocation payload is 6 MB for request and for response
Default concurrent executions quota is 1,000 per Region; new accounts start with a reduced quota
Environment variables total at most 4 KB

sources.title: Amazon S3 API: GetObject
supports: For a missing object S3 returns 404 when the caller has s3:ListBucket and 403 when it does not

sources.title: DynamoDB read consistency
supports: A write that returned HTTP 200 has been durably persisted
Eventually consistent reads are the default, may not reflect a recently completed write, and cost half of strongly consistent reads
ConsistentRead is available on GetItem, Query, and Scan for tables and local secondary indexes, not for global secondary indexes or streams
Global tables have two modes: multi-Region eventual consistency (default, typically replicated within a second) and multi-Region strong consistency (synchronous replication before the write returns)

sources.title: DynamoDB condition expression CLI example
supports: PutItem overwrites an item with the same primary key unless a condition prevents it
attribute_not_exists on a key attribute is true only when no item with that full key exists
A write whose condition evaluates to false is rejected with "The conditional request failed"

sources.title: Paginating table query results in DynamoDB
supports: A Query returns at most 1 MB per call
LastEvaluatedKey becomes the next ExclusiveStartKey; its absence is the only sign that the result set is finished
A non-empty LastEvaluatedKey does not guarantee that more items remain

sources.title: DynamoDB on-demand capacity mode
supports: On-demand tables are billed per read and write request, with no throughput charge at zero traffic
One read request unit is one strongly consistent read, or two eventually consistent reads, of an item up to 4 KB; one write request unit is one write of an item up to 1 KB
New on-demand tables sustain up to 4,000 writes and 12,000 reads per second and can be throttled when traffic more than doubles within 30 minutes
A maximum read or write throughput can be configured per on-demand table

sources.title: Constraints in Amazon DynamoDB
supports: Maximum item size is 400 KB
A transaction can contain at most 100 unique items and 4 MB
Sort key values are at most 1024 bytes and partition key values 2048 bytes

sources.title: AWS Price List bulk API: DynamoDB, ap-northeast-1
supports: Unit prices in data/pricing/unit-prices.json with offerCode AmazonDynamoDB
The storage price has a USD 0 tier for the first 25 GB-month

supports: Tag 3.3.1 exists for amd64 and arm64 and was the image `latest` pointed at

sources.title: Control access to HTTP APIs with JWT authorizers in API Gateway
supports: The authorizer checks signature (RSA-based algorithms only), iss, aud or client_id, exp, nbf, iat, and route scopes; a failure denies the request
client_id is evaluated only when aud is absent
Public keys are cached for up to two hours
Verified claims reach a Lambda integration at requestContext.authorizer.jwt.claims
There is no standard way to tell access tokens from ID tokens; requiring scopes on routes is recommended
For Cognito the issuer is https://cognito-idp.{region}.amazonaws.com/{userPoolId}

sources.title: Cognito: the redirect and authorization endpoint
supports: /oauth2/authorize accepts response_type, client_id, redirect_uri, state, scope, code_challenge, and code_challenge_method
Only S256 is supported for PKCE
The redirect URI must be pre-registered and HTTPS, except http://localhost
An implicit grant is described as less secure because it exposes tokens
An authorization code is valid for five minutes
An ID token is returned only when the openid scope is requested

sources.title: Cognito: understanding the access token
supports: Access tokens are signed with RS256 and carry sub, client_id, token_use = access, and scope
sub is the recommended way to identify a user
Access token validity is configurable from 5 minutes to 1 day
Managed login sets a browser cookie valid for one hour; token durations under an hour are discouraged with managed login

sources.title: Cognito: ending user sessions with token revocation
supports: Revoked tokens cannot be used with Cognito API calls, but are still valid to any JWT library that verifies only signature and expiration
Token revocation is enabled by default on new app clients

sources.title: Cognito: the managed login sign-out endpoint
supports: GET /logout with client_id and logout_uri signs the user out of managed login and redirects to an allowed sign-out URL

sources.title: Amazon Cognito pricing
supports: Essentials is the default feature plan for new user pools
Lite and Essentials include 10,000 free MAUs per month per account or organization, and that allowance does not expire
A user counts as a MAU when an identity operation occurs for them in the month
SMS and email are charged separately
sources.note: Whether managed login is available on the Lite plan is not clearly stated on the page.

sources.title: AWS Price List bulk API: Cognito, ap-northeast-1
supports: Unit prices in data/pricing/unit-prices.json with offerCode AmazonCognito

sources.title: What is Amazon IVS Low-Latency Streaming?
supports: IVS channels can deliver video with latency under 5 seconds; IVS stages under 300 ms
Ingest protocols are RTMP, RTMPS, and SRT
The data plane (ingest and viewing) is global; the control plane (API, channels, stream keys) is regional
Observed latency varies between users with location, network, and the components in the chain

sources.title: What is Amazon IVS Real-Time Streaming?
supports: Real-time streaming delivers latency that can be under 300 milliseconds from host to viewer
Up to 12 hosts on a stage; the resource is a stage, not a channel

sources.title: Amazon Interactive Video Service endpoints and quotas
supports: ap-northeast-1 has endpoints for IVS low-latency streaming, real-time streaming, and chat
One stream key per channel, not adjustable
Default quotas per Region: 100 concurrent streams and 15,000 concurrent views
BASIC ingest bitrate: 1.5 Mbps at 480p or less, 3.5 Mbps above 480p; STANDARD and ADVANCED: 8.5 Mbps; ingest resolution up to 1080p
PutMetadata: 1 KB payload, 5 transactions per second per channel
Real-time stages: 12 publishers and 10,000 subscribers per stage by default

sources.title: Amazon IVS Streaming Configuration
supports: Four channel types; STANDARD is the default; BASIC is transmuxed into a single rendition, STANDARD and ADVANCED are transcoded into several
Exceeding the allowed input resolution or bitrate probably disconnects the stream immediately
The RTMPS ingest URL form rtmps://<ingest endpoint>:443/app/<stream key>
Keyframe interval of 2 seconds is recommended; values above 5 seconds are to be avoided; a 2-second interval gives a stream-start latency of roughly 6 to 7 seconds
For the lowest latency the IVS player is required; H.264 video and AAC audio; CBR is recommended

sources.title: Getting started with IVS: Set Up Streaming Software
supports: OBS Studio 30.2 or later has an Amazon IVS service entry that takes the stream key
A stream lasts 48 hours at most; a reconnect starts a new stream
IVS disconnects after 30 seconds without data from the encoder
The FFmpeg example for RTMPS

sources.title: Amazon IVS Pricing
supports: All streams sent to IVS incur video input costs, even if they are not viewed; input is rounded up to the minute, output to the second
Input per hour: Basic 0.20, Standard 2.00, Advanced SD 0.50, Advanced HD 0.85 USD
Output is billed per hour delivered, by resolution (SD up to 480, HD up to 720, Full HD up to 1080) and by where viewers are served from
Japan is in the output group 'Japan, Hong Kong, and South East Asia'
Free tier for new customers, first 12 months: 5 hours of basic input and 100 hours of SD output a month
Real-time streaming is billed per participant hour
sources.note: The page describes no charge for a channel that exists but is not live.

sources.title: AWS Price List bulk API: IVS
supports: Unit prices in data/pricing/unit-prices.json with offerCode AmazonIVS
The offer contains only input-hour, output-hour, and real-time-hour products; none for an idle channel
sources.note: The offer has no per-Region file; region_index.json lists only aws-other. The usage types prefixed AP- are described in the file as 'Japan, Hong Kong, SEA'.

sources.title: IVS Costs: Low-Latency Streaming
supports: Auto-record to S3 has no IVS charge; S3 storage, the S3 API calls IVS makes, and serving the recordings are charged
As a rule of thumb, on average 50% of a stream is delivered to each viewer

sources.title: AWS::IVS::Channel
supports: The Channel resource does not create a stream key, unlike the CreateChannel API
Properties Type, LatencyMode (default LOW), Authorized, InsecureIngest, RecordingConfigurationArn, and their defaults
Attributes Arn, IngestEndpoint, PlaybackUrl; the playback URL contains the account ID

sources.title: AWS::IVS::StreamKey
supports: Attributes Arn and Value; Value is the stream key itself
Changing ChannelArn replaces the resource

sources.title: IVS API: GetStream
supports: An offline channel is reported as the ChannelNotBroadcasting error (HTTP 404), not as a response

sources.title: IVS API: Stream
supports: Do not rely on the OFFLINE state; the API may not return it
viewerCount of -1 means the request timed out; health is HEALTHY, STARVING, or UNKNOWN

sources.title: IVS API: StopStream
supports: StopStream disconnects the incoming stream; encoders often reconnect, so revoke the stream key to stop it for good

sources.title: IVS API: DeleteChannel
supports: Deleting a channel deletes its stream keys
Deleting a live channel fails with 409 ConflictException; stop the stream and wait for Stream End first

sources.title: Using Amazon EventBridge with IVS Low-Latency Streaming
supports: Events are best effort: they may be missing, hours late, or out of order (Stream Down before Stream Up)
Detail types, event names, and the example payloads used as test fixtures
Each time a channel goes live it gets a new stream_id
Session Ended may arrive before Stream End

sources.title: IVS Player SDK
supports: The IVS player is required for low latency; latency is under five seconds depending on location and settings
Browsers on iOS get normal-latency playback only; a service worker brings iOS Safari to about 6 to 8 seconds
Third-party players can be brought to about 10 seconds

sources.title: Getting Started with the IVS Web Player SDK
supports: The SDK is offered as a script tag and as an npm module; the page names 1.57.0 as the latest
playsinline is required for inline playback on iOS Safari
The WebAssembly binary must be served as application/wasm when self-hosted

sources.title: amazon-ivs-player 1.57.0 (npm tarball)
supports: create() takes wasmWorker and wasmBinary URLs; the files ship under dist/assets
ErrorType.NOT_AVAILABLE with code 404 means the stream does not exist or is offline, 429 that the viewer limit was reached
getLiveLatency() returns the latency from the server to the player in seconds; isLiveLowLatency() and TEXT_METADATA_CUE exist
The package is AWS Content under the AWS Customer Agreement, not an open-source license; peer dependencies are bowser and lodash
sources.note: Read from dist/index.d.ts and package.json of the installed tarball.

sources.title: Embedding Metadata within a Video Stream
supports: Timed metadata is embedded in the video segments, so every viewer receives it at the same point in the stream
PutMetadata works only on a live stream; there is no guarantee when the metadata is inserted
The web player delivers it as TEXT_METADATA_CUE

sources.title: IVS Auto-Record to Amazon S3
supports: Recordings are written under ivs/v1/<account>/<channel>/<date>/<recording id> as HLS media, thumbnails, and JSON metadata
Process a recording only after the Recording End event

sources.title: What Is MediaLive?
supports: MediaLive transforms live video from one format and package into others, for broadcast and streaming delivery

sources.title: MediaLive: Related Services
supports: MediaPackage is a just-in-time video packaging and origination service that can package content encoded by MediaLive

sources.title: AWS Elemental MediaLive Pricing
supports: A running channel is charged whether or not its inputs receive content; push inputs and channels are also charged while idle
Running time is rounded up to the minute above a 10-minute minimum

sources.title: Cloudflare Stream: Stream live video
supports: Ingest over RTMPS or SRT; playback in the Stream Player or any HLS or DASH player
Every live stream is recorded automatically
Priced per 1,000 minutes recorded and per 1,000 minutes delivered, with no separate encoding charge
sources.note: The page gives no latency figures.

supports: register-providers.ts registers no provider for any AWS::IVS type, so Channel and StreamKey go through Cloud Control API; AWS::Events::Rule, AWS::Lambda::*, AWS::IAM::*, and AWS::Logs::LogGroup have dedicated providers
The Cloud Control provider stores the resource model returned by a create as the resource's attributes in state
AWS::IVS::StreamKey Value is on cdkd's list of secret-valued attributes
sources.note: Read from the bundled dist of the tarball, which keeps the src/ region markers. No cdkd command was run against AWS, so what state.json holds for a stream key is not observed.

sources.title: Amazon VPC pricing
supports: A NAT gateway is billed per NAT gateway-hour while provisioned and available, plus per GB processed regardless of source or destination; a partial hour is billed as a full hour
Standard data transfer charges apply on top of NAT gateway data processing
Every public IPv4 address is billed by the hour, in use or idle, at the same rate; Elastic IP addresses attached to NAT gateways are named as an example
A Regional NAT gateway is billed per hour for each Availability Zone it is configured in
sources.note: The page renders its regional price tables with JavaScript. The numbers in the book come from the Price List bulk API, not from this page.

sources.title: What is Amazon VPC?
supports: There is no additional charge for using a VPC; some components such as NAT gateways are charged
Private IPv4 addresses are not charged
AWS Free Tier customers get 750 hours of public IPv4 address usage with the EC2 service

sources.title: Subnets for your VPC
supports: The subnet type is determined by its routing: a public subnet has a direct route to an internet gateway, a private subnet does not and needs a NAT device for internet access, an isolated subnet has no routes to destinations outside its VPC
Network ACLs allow or deny traffic at the subnet level

sources.title: Subnet CIDR blocks
supports: A subnet's IPv4 CIDR block is between /28 and /16
The first four addresses and the last address of every subnet are reserved

sources.title: VPC CIDR blocks
supports: A VPC's IPv4 CIDR block is between /16 and /28
Some AWS services use 172.17.0.0/16, so that range is best avoided

sources.title: Route table concepts
supports: The main route table controls routing for every subnet not explicitly associated with another route table
Every route table has a local route for communication within the VPC
A route has a destination CIDR and a target such as an internet gateway

sources.title: Control traffic to your AWS resources using security groups
supports: Security groups are stateful: responses to allowed traffic are allowed regardless of the rules in the other direction

sources.title: Control subnet traffic with network access control lists
supports: Network ACLs are stateless: responses to allowed traffic are not automatically allowed
Network ACL rules are evaluated when traffic enters and leaves the subnet, not as it is routed within a subnet
The default network ACL allows all inbound and outbound traffic
sources.note: The default rules were read on the linked page https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/default-network-acl.html.

sources.title: Infrastructure security in Amazon VPC
supports: Security groups work at the instance level with allow rules only; network ACLs work at the subnet level with allow and deny rules, evaluated in ascending order
You can secure your instances using only security groups

sources.title: Enable internet access for a VPC using an internet gateway
supports: There is no charge for an internet gateway itself

sources.title: NAT gateway basics
supports: A NAT gateway is created in one Availability Zone and is redundant within that zone
If zones share one NAT gateway and its zone is down, resources in the other zones lose internet access; one NAT gateway per zone avoids this
A public NAT gateway sits in a public subnet and needs an Elastic IP address
sources.note: The Elastic IP requirement was read on https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/vpc-nat-gateway.html.

sources.title: Gateway endpoints
supports: Gateway endpoints exist for Amazon S3 and DynamoDB only, and need no internet gateway or NAT device
There is no additional charge for using gateway endpoints
Creating one adds a route to each selected route table: destination the service's prefix list, target the endpoint
Prefix lists are specific to a Region, so traffic to the service in another Region does not use the endpoint

sources.title: Access an AWS service using an interface VPC endpoint
supports: An interface endpoint creates an endpoint network interface with a private IP address in each chosen subnet, one subnet per Availability Zone
Interface endpoints are billed for hourly usage and for data processing
Private DNS needs DNS hostnames and DNS resolution enabled on the VPC
The endpoint's security group must allow inbound HTTPS from the resources that call it

sources.title: AWS services that integrate with AWS PrivateLink
supports: Service names com.amazonaws.region.ecr.api, ecr.dkr, logs, secretsmanager, ssm, ssmmessages, and ec2messages

sources.title: AWS PrivateLink pricing
supports: An interface endpoint is billed for each hour it stays provisioned in each Availability Zone; a partial hour is billed as a full hour
Data processing is billed per GB regardless of the traffic's source or destination, in tiers over the Region's monthly total
sources.note: The hourly rate is rendered with JavaScript; the book's number comes from the Price List bulk API.

sources.title: AWS::EC2::VPCEndpoint
supports: Properties VpcEndpointType, ServiceName, VpcId, RouteTableIds, SubnetIds, SecurityGroupIds, and PrivateDnsEnabled

sources.title: Giving Lambda functions access to resources in an Amazon VPC
supports: By default a Lambda function can reach the public internet; attached to a VPC it can reach only what the VPC can
Connecting a function to a public subnet gives it neither internet access nor a public IP address

The execution role needs ec2:CreateNetworkInterface, DescribeNetworkInterfaces, DescribeSubnets, DeleteNetworkInterface, AssignPrivateIpAddresses, and UnassignPrivateIpAddresses on all resources, and the function's code is implicitly granted them too
A new function stays Pending while Lambda creates the Hyperplane ENI, which can take several minutes; functions with the same subnets and security groups share one
After 14 idle days Lambda reclaims unused Hyperplane ENIs and the function becomes Inactive

sources.title: Amazon ECR interface VPC endpoints (AWS PrivateLink)
supports: Fargate tasks on platform version 1.4.0 or later need both ECR endpoints (ecr.api, ecr.dkr) and the S3 gateway endpoint to pull images privately
Fargate tasks that use the awslogs driver in a VPC without an internet gateway need the com.amazonaws.region.logs interface endpoint

sources.title: Fargate task networking
supports: A Fargate task pulls its image over a public IP address in a public subnet, a NAT gateway from a private subnet, or ECR interface endpoints

sources.title: Improve the security of EC2 instances by using VPC endpoints for Systems Manager
supports: Systems Manager without internet access uses the ssm, ssmmessages, and ec2messages interface endpoints, and S3 for agent updates
ssmmessages is required for Session Manager

sources.title: AWS Availability Zones
supports: Each Region has at least three Availability Zones
An AZ ID such as apne1-az1 is the same physical location in every account; ap-northeast-1 has apne1-az1 to apne1-az4
AWS may restrict new resources in a constrained Availability Zone

sources.title: AZ IDs for your AWS resources
supports: In Asia Pacific (Tokyo), accounts created before November 2025 have Availability Zone names mapped independently per account
`aws ec2 describe-availability-zones` lists the zone names and IDs of an account

sources.title: AWS Fault Isolation Boundaries: Availability Zones
supports: An Availability Zone is one or more discrete data centers with separate power, networking, and connectivity inside one Region
Zones in a Region are up to about 100 km apart and designed not to fail together

sources.title: AWS Fault Isolation Boundaries: Regions
supports: Regions are isolated from each other, which limits a service failure to one Region
Resources and data in one Region do not exist in another unless you replicate them

sources.title: AWS Price List bulk API: EC2, ap-northeast-1
supports: Unit prices in data/pricing/unit-prices.json with offerCode AmazonEC2: NAT gateway hours and data processing
The offer also lists a Regional NAT gateway at the same hourly and per-GB rate, and regional data transfer at USD 0.01 per GB
sources.note: The file is about 445 MB. NAT gateway prices live in the EC2 offer, not the VPC offer.

sources.title: AWS Price List bulk API: VPC, ap-northeast-1
supports: Unit prices in data/pricing/unit-prices.json with offerCode AmazonVPC: interface endpoint hours and data processing, public IPv4 address hours
The offer has no SKU for a VPC, subnet, route table, internet gateway, or gateway endpoint

sources.title: cdkd v0.296.28 source: provider registry and property coverage
supports: register-providers.ts registers one EC2 provider for AWS::EC2::VPC, Subnet, InternetGateway, EIP, VPCGatewayAttachment, NatGateway, RouteTable, Route, SubnetRouteTableAssociation, SecurityGroup, SecurityGroupIngress, Instance, NetworkAcl, NetworkAclEntry, and SubnetNetworkAclAssociation
AWS::EC2::VPCEndpoint is not registered and is not in the unsupported list, so it goes through Cloud Control API
property-coverage.generated.ts lists the properties the EC2 provider writes; a resource using any other property is routed through Cloud Control API
The intrinsic resolver handles Fn::GetAZs
sources.note: Read from the source archive of the v0.296.28 tag. The npm tarball ships bundled JavaScript without the TypeScript sources. No cdkd command was run against AWS.

sources.title: cdkd v0.296.28: Cross-Stack References
supports: cdkd resolves Fn::ImportValue against the outputs other stacks recorded in its state, and falls back to CloudFormation ListExports when no cdkd stack exports the name
`cdkd destroy` of a stack whose exports are still imported is refused with StackHasActiveImportsError, and there is no flag to force it
cdkd also resolves Fn::GetStackOutput as a weak reference that does not block the producer's destroy; its documentation calls the intrinsic cdkd-specific
Outputs are stored in the state file; state version 9 records which output keys are Export names
sources.note: Read together with docs/stack-outputs.md and src/types/state.ts at the same tag. Not exercised against AWS. CloudFormation's own documentation also lists Fn::GetStackOutput (see cfn-stack-exports); how the two relate was not investigated.

sources.title: Default security groups for your VPCs
supports: Every VPC comes with a default security group, and a resource created without a security group is associated with it
AWS recommends creating security groups for specific resources instead of using the default one

sources.title: Get exported outputs from a deployed CloudFormation stack
supports: Export names must be unique within a Region for each AWS account
After another stack imports an output value, the exporting stack cannot be deleted and the exported value cannot be modified until every import is removed
CloudFormation documents Fn::GetStackOutput for references across accounts or Regions

sources.title: AWS::EC2::Subnet
supports: Updating a subnet's CidrBlock replaces the subnet: a new one is created and the old one deleted

sources.title: Amazon VPCs and ElastiCache security
supports: All node-based ElastiCache clusters are launched in a VPC; ElastiCache Serverless caches can also be configured with a public endpoint that needs no VPC configuration

sources.title: Request production access (Moving out of the Amazon SES sandbox)
supports: New accounts start in the SES sandbox, and the sandbox status is per Region
In the sandbox: mail only to verified addresses and domains or the mailbox simulator, at most 200 messages per 24 hours, at most 1 message per second
In the sandbox, bulk actions and SES API calls for suppression list management are disabled
After leaving the sandbox, From, Source, Sender and Return-Path identities still have to be verified
The console request asks for mail type (Marketing or Transactional), website URL, up to 4 additional contact addresses, preferred contact language (English or Japanese), and an acknowledgement
`aws sesv2 put-account-details --production-access-enabled --mail-type --website-url --additional-contact-email-addresses --contact-language` submits the same request
AWS Support gives an initial response within 24 hours; details cannot be edited while the review is open

sources.title: Using the Amazon SES account-level suppression list
supports: The account-level suppression list applies to one account in one Region
Accounts that started using SES after 2019-11-25 use it by default for bounces and complaints
A message to a suppressed address (with a matching reason) is accepted by SES but not sent
Such messages count toward the daily sending quota, and not toward the reputation bounce and complaint rates
Only hard bounces are added; addresses stay until removed
Gmail does not provide complaint data to SES
PutSuppressedDestination and CreateImportJob are unavailable in the sandbox
A configuration set can override the account-level suppression settings; with it, addresses are added only for mail sent with that configuration set
List entries are case-sensitive in the management API
`aws sesv2 put-account-suppression-attributes`, `list-suppressed-destinations`, and `delete-suppressed-destination`

sources.title: How email sending works in Amazon SES
supports: A successful request returns a message ID; delivery, bounce, and complaint happen afterwards
On rare occasions SES may accept an email for delivery even though the send request returns an error; a retry may then send a second email with a different message ID
SES recommends message tags, not only the message ID, to correlate event notifications with sending logic
Definitions of hard bounce and soft bounce; SES retries soft bounces for a period before reporting them

sources.title: SES API v2: SendEmail
supports: Request fields used: FromEmailAddress, Destination.ToAddresses, Content.Simple, ConfigurationSetName, EmailTags
The request has no idempotency or client token parameter
The response is a MessageId, and SES can accept a message without sending it

Errors: AccountSuspendedException, BadRequestException, LimitExceededException, MailFromDomainNotVerifiedException, MessageRejected, SendingPausedException (400), NotFoundException (404), TooManyRequestsException (429)

sources.title: SES API v2: MessageTag
supports: Tag names and values: ASCII letters, digits, underscore and dash only, at most 256 characters

sources.title: Monitor email sending using Amazon SES event publishing
supports: Events are published only for mail sent with a configuration set that has an event destination
Meaning of the Send, Delivery, Bounce, Complaint, Reject and DeliveryDelay events
Delivery means delivered to the recipient's mail server
Message tags and auto-tags are included in published events

sources.title: Contents of event data that Amazon SES publishes to Amazon SNS
supports: Top-level fields eventType, mail, bounce, complaint, delivery, and the possible eventType values
mail.messageId and mail.tags; bounce.bounceType, bounceSubType, bouncedRecipients[].emailAddress, timestamp, feedbackId
bounceType is Undetermined, Permanent or Transient; Permanent includes the OnAccountSuppressionList subtype
Only hard bounces, and soft bounces SES has stopped retrying, are published
Most ISPs redact the complainer's address, so complainedRecipients lists every recipient of the mail on the complaining domain

sources.title: Examples of event data that Amazon SES publishes to Amazon SNS
supports: The Bounce, Complaint and Delivery example records that examples/15-email/test/fixtures/ follow
sources.note: The fixtures are edited copies of the documented examples. No event was captured from a real account.

sources.title: Set up an Amazon SNS event destination for event publishing
supports: SES supports standard SNS topics only as an event destination, not FIFO
The topic policy must allow sns:Publish to ses.amazonaws.com, conditioned on AWS:SourceAccount and the configuration set's AWS:SourceArn

sources.title: Creating and verifying identities in Amazon SES
supports: An identity is a domain or an email address, verified separately in each Region
Verifying a domain covers its addresses and subdomains
An address verified only through its domain is limited to straightforward sending; advanced sending includes using the address with configuration sets
Email address identities are case-sensitive; the verification mail comes from no-reply-aws@amazon.com and its link expires after 24 hours
A domain identity is verified by publishing three Easy DKIM CNAME records, which can take up to 72 hours to be detected
The CNAME value is the token followed by the SigningHostedZone returned by CreateEmailIdentity and GetEmailIdentity
sources.note: What "using the address with configuration sets" excludes for an address that is verified only through its domain is not spelled out. The stack sets the configuration set as the identity's default as well as naming it on each send.

sources.title: Easy DKIM in Amazon SES
supports: With Easy DKIM, SES signs every mail from the identity with a 2048-bit key by default
The SES console can publish the records itself when Route 53 hosts the domain

sources.title: Using a custom MAIL FROM domain
supports: By default the MAIL FROM domain is a subdomain of amazonses.com, and SPF passes for that domain
A custom MAIL FROM domain must be a subdomain of the verified identity's domain, not used for sending or receiving
It needs exactly one MX record `10 feedback-smtp.<region>.amazonses.com` and a TXT record "v=spf1 include:amazonses.com ~all"
Behavior on MX failure is either falling back to the default MAIL FROM domain or rejecting the message
SES looks for the MX record for up to 72 hours

sources.title: Complying with DMARC authentication protocol in Amazon SES
supports: SPF checks the MAIL FROM domain, DKIM checks the signing domain, and DMARC requires one of them to align with the From domain
A message passes DMARC if either the SPF or the DKIM alignment check passes
The DMARC policy is a TXT record at _dmarc.<domain>; p=none, quarantine, and reject, rolled out in that order
SPF alignment through SES needs a custom MAIL FROM domain; DKIM alignment needs Easy DKIM on the From domain
`dig TXT _dmarc.<domain>` shows the published policy

sources.title: Sending test emails in Amazon SES with the simulator
supports: success@, bounce@, complaint@, ooto@ and suppressionlist@simulator.amazonses.com and what each simulates
The simulator works in the sandbox
Simulator mail does not count toward the daily quota or the bounce and complaint rates, and is billed like any other mail
bounce@simulator.amazonses.com is not placed on the suppression list

sources.title: SES API v2: GetAccount
supports: ProductionAccessEnabled false means the account is in the sandbox in that Region
SendQuota (Max24HourSend, MaxSendRate, SentLast24Hours), SendingEnabled, EnforcementStatus, SuppressionAttributes.SuppressedReasons

sources.title: SES API v2: GetEmailIdentity
supports: VerifiedForSendingStatus, VerificationStatus (PENDING, SUCCESS, FAILED, TEMPORARY_FAILURE, NOT_STARTED)
DkimAttributes (Status, Tokens, SigningHostedZone) and MailFromAttributes (MailFromDomain, MailFromDomainStatus)
Without an event destination or another mechanism, bounce and complaint notifications are sent by email

sources.title: AWS Service Reference: actions, resources and condition keys for SES
supports: ses:SendEmail is authorized against the resource types identity, configuration-set and template
ARN formats arn:aws:ses:<region>:<account>:identity/<name> and :configuration-set/<name>
ses:SendEmail supports the condition keys ses:FromAddress, ses:FromDisplayName, ses:Recipients, ses:FeedbackAddress and ses:ApiVersion
sources.note: The JSON does not mark which resource types are required. Whether a sandbox account also needs permission on the recipient's identity was not confirmed from a primary source.

sources.title: Amazon SES pricing
supports: Outbound email is USD 0.10 per 1,000 emails, charged per recipient, plus USD 0.12 per GB of attachments
The page describes Free Tier credits for new AWS customers (up to USD 200, a free plan available for 6 months, credits to be used within 12 months) and no monthly count of free messages
Dedicated IPs and Virtual Deliverability Manager are separate charges
sources.note: Read as rendered on 2026-10-11. The Free Tier terms depend on when and how an account was created; the calculation applies no allowance.

sources.title: AWS Price List bulk API: SES, ap-northeast-1
supports: Unit prices in data/pricing/unit-prices.json with offerCode AmazonSES
Mail to the mailbox simulator has its own SKU at the same USD 0.0001 per recipient

sources.title: AWS Price List bulk API: SNS, ap-northeast-1
supports: Unit prices in data/pricing/unit-prices.json with offerCode AmazonSNS
The first 1,000,000 SNS API requests a month are a USD 0 tier
Deliveries to Lambda are USD 0

sources.title: Invoking Lambda functions with Amazon SNS notifications
supports: SNS invokes the function asynchronously; only standard topics are supported
Asynchronous invocations process each event at least once, and duplicates can occur
The event shape: Records[].Sns.Message and MessageId

sources.title: How Lambda handles errors and retries with asynchronous invocation
supports: When the function returns an error, Lambda runs it two more times by default
A function can receive the same event more than once even without an error
An event that fails all attempts is discarded unless a dead-letter queue or an on-failure destination is configured

sources.title: Amazon SNS message delivery retries
supports: When SNS cannot reach a Lambda endpoint it makes up to 100,015 attempts over 23 days
When the delivery policy is exhausted the message is discarded unless the subscription has a dead-letter queue

sources.title: AWS SDKs and Tools: Retry behavior
supports: The default is 3 attempts in total; max attempts 1 disables retries
Timeouts, connection failures and HTTP 500, 502, 503, 504 are retried as transient errors; TooManyRequestsException as throttling

sources.title: Control access to HTTP APIs with IAM authorization in API Gateway
supports: With IAM authorization on a route, clients sign requests with SigV4, and API Gateway invokes the route only if the caller has execute-api permission
Resource policies are not supported for HTTP APIs

sources.title: Using time to live (TTL) in DynamoDB
supports: The TTL attribute is a Number holding Unix epoch seconds
Expired items are deleted typically within a few days of expiring, without consuming write throughput
Until then an expired item can still be read and updated

sources.title: Email settings for Amazon Cognito user pools
supports: The default email configuration limits the number of emails per day and is below typical production volume
With the SES configuration, the user pool sends through a verified identity in your account, under your SES limits
The account must be out of the SES sandbox before Cognito can mail users through your SES configuration
sources.note: The daily limit of the default configuration is on the Cognito quotas page, which was not read.

sources.title: Cloudflare Email Service
supports: Email Sending is in beta for outbound transactional email
A Worker sends through a send_email binding (env.EMAIL.send); a REST API and SMTP also exist
Email Sending requires the Workers Paid plan
sources.note: Only the overview page was read. Domain onboarding, DNS records, bounce handling, limits and prices were not checked.

sources.title: @go-to-k/cdkd 0.296.28: provider routing for the resource types of chapter 15 (npm tarball)
supports: No SDK provider is registered for AWS::SES::EmailIdentity, AWS::SES::ConfigurationSet or AWS::SES::ConfigurationSetEventDestination; types without one are routed to Cloud Control API

AWS::SNS::Topic, AWS::SNS::TopicPolicy, AWS::SNS::Subscription, AWS::DynamoDB::Table, AWS::Lambda::Function, AWS::Lambda::Permission, AWS::Logs::LogGroup, AWS::IAM::Role, AWS::IAM::Policy and the four AWS::ApiGatewayV2 types have registered SDK providers
sources.note: Read from dist/ of the published tarball (the bundled register calls and the provider registry). No cdkd command was run against AWS, so the Cloud Control path for the SES types is unexercised.

sources.title: aws-cdk-lib 2.273.0: aws-ses constructs (type definitions and compiled source)
supports: EmailIdentity exposes dkimRecords, and accepts configurationSet, mailFromDomain and mailFromBehaviorOnMxFailure
ConfigurationSet.addEventDestination with an SNS topic also adds a topic policy for ses.amazonaws.com conditioned on the configuration set's ARN
ConfigurationSet.suppressionReasons synthesizes SuppressionOptions.SuppressedReasons

sources.title: Restrictions on CloudFront Functions
supports: CloudFront Functions cannot read the request body
The runtime restricts network, file system, environment variable, and timer access
Execution time is limited and reported as compute utilization
Function logs are truncated at 10 KB
KeyValueStore requires JavaScript runtime 2.0
The KeyValueStore API uses SigV4A, which needs version 2 session tokens: use a Regional STS endpoint

sources.title: JavaScript runtime 2.0 features for CloudFront Functions
supports: The runtime is ES 5.1 compliant with selected ES 6 to 12 features; const, let, async, and await are supported in runtime 2.0
No eval or Function constructor, no setTimeout/setImmediate/clearTimeout, no file system, no process, no environment variables, no network calls
Date returns the function's start time for the whole run
console supports only log(), without comma-separated arguments
Built-in modules are buffer, querystring, and crypto
sources.note: The page lists supported features. Syntax it does not list (optional chaining, spread, destructuring, classes, for...of) is treated as unsupported in this book; that inference was not tested on the runtime.

sources.title: CloudFront Functions event structure
supports: A function can return a response with statusCode, headers, and a body given as { encoding, data }
A status of 400 or above returned by a function is not replaced by a custom error page

sources.title: Test functions
supports: CloudFront can run a function against an event object before it is live and report the result, logs, and compute utilization

sources.title: Amazon CloudFront KeyValueStore
supports: Read-only key-value data for CloudFront Functions
Values are strings, byte-encoded strings, or JSON
Intended uses include URL rewrites and redirects, A/B testing and feature flags, and access authorization

sources.title: Helper methods for key value stores
supports: A function starts with `import cf from 'cloudfront'` and `cf.kvs()`
get(key, { format }) rejects when the key does not exist; exists(key) and meta() are the other two methods
Awaiting reads one after another is recommended over promise combinators, which use more memory and are not faster
meta().lastUpdatedDateTime does not include the propagation time to the edge

sources.title: Work with key value data
supports: Pairs in an existing store are changed through the CloudFront KeyValueStore API, which is global and uses SigV4A
Write operations take the store's ETag as If-Match and return a new ETag
The ETags of the CloudFront API and the KeyValueStore API are not interchangeable
UpdateKeys is one all-or-nothing operation
Values are not changed during a function invocation; updates are processed between invocations

sources.title: Create a key value store
supports: A file of pairs can be imported only when the store is first created

sources.title: File format for key-value pairs
supports: Import file limits: 5 MB, 512-character keys, 1024-character values, no duplicate keys

sources.title: CloudFront KeyValueStore API: UpdateKeys
supports: UpdateKeys requires If-Match and returns the new ETag, ItemCount, and TotalSizeInBytes
Listed errors: AccessDenied 403, Conflict 409, InternalServer 500, ResourceNotFound 404, ServiceQuotaExceeded 402, Validation 400
sources.note: The page does not say which error a stale If-Match produces.

sources.title: CloudFront KeyValueStore API: ListKeys
supports: ListKeys returns at most 50 pairs per call (default 10) and a NextToken

sources.title: CloudFront quotas
supports: CloudFront Functions: 10 KB maximum function size (not adjustable), 2 MB maximum function memory, 100 functions per account
Key value stores: 512-byte key, 1 KB value, 5 MB per store, 50 keys or 3 MB per update request, one store per function, 100 functions per store, 200 stores per account
Lambda@Edge: 30-second function timeout, 50 MB compressed size, generated response up to 40 KB (viewer events) or 1 MB (origin events), 10,000 requests per second per Region

sources.title: Differences between CloudFront Functions and Lambda@Edge
supports: CloudFront Functions run on viewer request and viewer response only; Lambda@Edge also on origin request and origin response
CloudFront Functions: submillisecond duration, 2 MB memory, 10 KB code, no network, no file system, no request body
Lambda@Edge: Node.js and Python, up to 30 seconds, network and file system access, request body access, no KeyValueStore

sources.title: Restrictions on all edge functions
supports: One edge function per event type per cache behavior
CloudFront Functions and Lambda@Edge cannot be combined on viewer events; a CloudFront Function on a viewer event with Lambda@Edge on an origin event is allowed
Viewer response functions are not invoked when the origin returns 400 or higher

sources.title: Edge function logs
supports: CloudFront Functions log only console.log() lines, always to us-east-1, in /aws/cloudfront/function/<FunctionName>
Lambda@Edge logs to /aws/lambda/us-east-1.<FunctionName> in the Region where the function ran
Edge function logs are delivered on a best-effort basis

sources.title: Restrictions on Lambda@Edge
supports: The function must be in us-east-1 and must be referenced by a numbered version, not $LATEST or an alias
Not supported: environment variables (other than reserved ones), VPC access, layers, dead letter queues, X-Ray, provisioned concurrency, container images, arm64, more than 512 MB of ephemeral storage
With include body, the body is base64 encoded and truncated at 40 KB (viewer request) or 1 MB (origin request)
The execution role must be assumable by lambda.amazonaws.com and edgelambda.amazonaws.com

sources.title: Set up IAM permissions and roles for Lambda@Edge
supports: Associating a function needs lambda:GetFunction, lambda:EnableReplication*, lambda:DisableReplication*, and iam:CreateServiceLinkedRole
The service-linked roles AWSServiceRoleForLambdaReplicator and AWSServiceRoleForCloudFrontLogger are created automatically

sources.title: Delete Lambda@Edge functions and replicas
supports: A Lambda@Edge function can be deleted only after CloudFront has deleted its replicas, typically within a few hours of removing the last association

sources.title: AWS News Blog: Introducing Amazon CloudFront KeyValueStore
supports: Updates to a store are described as propagating to all edge locations in a few seconds
sources.note: A launch post, not a specification. The Developer Guide pages read for this chapter give no propagation time and no guarantee.

sources.title: Amazon CloudFront pay-as-you-go pricing
supports: Always-free each month: 1 TB data transfer out, 10,000,000 HTTP/HTTPS requests, 2,000,000 CloudFront Function invocations, 2,000,000 KeyValueStore reads
First 1,000 invalidation paths per month are free, then USD 0.005 per path
Origin fetches from AWS origins such as S3 are free of data-transfer charges
KeyValueStore reads from functions cost USD 0.03 per million; other KeyValueStore API actions cost USD 1 per 1,000 requests
Lambda@Edge costs USD 0.60 per million requests and USD 0.00005001 per GB-second, metered per millisecond, with no free tier

supports: Importing the package registers a JavaScript SigV4A signer that @aws-sdk/signature-v4-multi-region uses when no CRT signer is loaded
sources.note: Read from the installed package and from @aws-sdk/signature-v4-multi-region 3.996.48. The AWS documentation example imports @aws-sdk/signature-v4-crt instead.

sources.title: Cloudflare Workers: Limits
supports: CPU time per HTTP request: 10 ms on Workers Free, 30 seconds by default and up to 5 minutes on Workers Paid; waiting on fetch or KV does not count
128 MB of memory per isolate; Worker size up to 64 MiB uncompressed
Subrequests per invocation: 50 on Free, 10,000 by default on Paid
No hard duration limit for HTTP-triggered Workers while the client stays connected

sources.title: Cloudflare Workers: Pricing
supports: Workers Free: 100,000 requests per day
Workers Standard: 10 million requests and 30 million CPU milliseconds included per month, then USD 0.30 per million requests and USD 0.02 per million CPU milliseconds

sources.title: Cloudflare Workers KV: How KV works
supports: KV is eventually consistent: a change may take up to 60 seconds or more to be visible in other locations
Data is stored centrally and cached at locations after access

sources.title: Cloudflare Workers KV: Limits
supports: Key size 512 bytes, value size 25 MiB, 1 write per second to the same key
A Worker can write to KV; Free allows 1,000 writes per day

sources.title: @go-to-k/cdkd 0.296.28 (npm tarball and tagged source)
supports: Command list, flags, and exit codes used by tools/src/infra and tools/src/drift
`drift --json` output shape (StackDriftJson) and exit codes 0/1/2
`cdkd bootstrap` creates cdkd-state-{account}, cdkd-assets-{account}-{region}, and an ECR repository; it creates no IAM roles and no CDKToolkit stack
Without AWS_REGION cdkd uses us-east-1
A CloudFront distribution is waited for only with --full-wait
State is stored at s3://{bucket}/{prefix}/{stack}/{region}/state.json with an S3 conditional-write lock
AWS::CloudFront::Function is provisioned and read back through Cloud Control API, not a dedicated provider
A non-empty bucket without the CDK auto-delete tag makes destroy fail
AWS::CloudFront::KeyValueStore is in the list of stateful types, whose replacement needs --force-stateful-recreation
Asset publishing uses the stack's own region when the stack sets one (stack.region || base region)
`cdkd local start-cloudfront` serves a distribution locally with its viewer-request functions; --kvs-file backs cf.kvs().get() with a JSON file, and Lambda@Edge is skipped with a warning
sources.note: Read from the published tarball, --help output, and the v0.296.28 source tag. No cdkd command was run against AWS.

sources.title: What is Amazon Aurora DSQL?
supports: Aurora DSQL is available in Asia Pacific (Tokyo), ap-northeast-1
Serverless, with no instances to provision; data is replicated synchronously across three Availability Zones
Currently compatible with PostgreSQL version 16
ACID transactions with strong consistency and snapshot isolation
Multi-Region clusters must stay inside one Region set; Tokyo, Osaka, and Seoul are in the Asia Pacific set

sources.title: Migrating from PostgreSQL to Aurora DSQL
supports: The isolation level is fixed at PostgreSQL Repeatable Read
DDL and DML need separate transactions; a transaction holds one DDL statement; a transaction modifies at most 3,000 rows
Connections time out after 1 hour
One built-in database named postgres per cluster; UTF-8, C collation only, UTC
No temporary tables, no triggers, no PL/pgSQL (SQL functions only); DELETE FROM or DROP/CREATE instead of TRUNCATE; CREATE INDEX ASYNC instead of CREATE INDEX
Foreign keys are supported
Conflicts return a serialization error instead of waiting for a lock; AWS recommends idempotent transactions with retry, and random primary keys
Permissions are schema-level grants: admin manages objects in public, non-admin roles use user-created schemas

sources.title: Supported SQL for Aurora DSQL
supports: BEGIN accepts ISOLATION LEVEL REPEATABLE READ and READ WRITE | READ ONLY
INSERT supports ON CONFLICT; SELECT supports FOR UPDATE and FOR KEY SHARE, joins, CTEs, and window functions
CREATE SCHEMA, CREATE VIEW, CREATE SEQUENCE, CREATE FUNCTION ... LANGUAGE SQL, and CREATE [UNIQUE] INDEX ASYNC are supported
The page says the list is not exhaustive

sources.title: DDL and distributed transactions in Aurora DSQL
supports: A transaction can contain only one DDL statement and cannot mix DDL and DML
A schema change updates the catalog version; a session holding an older cached catalog can receive SQLSTATE 40001 with OCC code OC001, and a retry typically succeeds

sources.title: Concurrency control in Aurora DSQL
supports: Optimistic concurrency control: conflicts are evaluated at commit time, without locks
A conflict is returned as SQLSTATE 40001; OC000 is a data conflict, OC001 a schema conflict
Of two transactions that modified the same row, the one that commits first succeeds
SELECT ... FOR UPDATE is adjudicated at commit as if the transaction wrote the rows
AWS recommends retrying, with idempotent transactions, and random primary keys to avoid contention on a few keys

sources.title: Cluster quotas and database limits in Amazon Aurora DSQL
supports: 3,000 rows mutated per transaction, 10 MiB of data modified per write transaction, 5 minutes maximum transaction time, 60 minutes maximum connection duration
10,000 connections per cluster by default, 100 new connections per second with a burst of 1,000
1 database per cluster, 10 schemas per database, 1,000 tables per database, 24 indexes per table, 2 MiB per row
20 single-Region clusters per account per Region by default

sources.title: Aurora DSQL: CREATE TABLE
supports: CREATE TABLE supports IF NOT EXISTS, CHECK, DEFAULT, UNIQUE, PRIMARY KEY, REFERENCES / FOREIGN KEY with referential actions, and identity columns
CASCADE, SET NULL, and SET DEFAULT actions count toward the per-transaction row limit

sources.title: Aurora DSQL: ALTER TABLE
supports: ADD COLUMN takes a column name and a data type; the supported syntax lists no constraint or default on that form
CHECK and FOREIGN KEY constraints added to an existing table must be NOT VALID and are validated with ALTER TABLE ASYNC ... VALIDATE CONSTRAINT
The listed actions include DROP NOT NULL but no SET NOT NULL and no change of a column's type

sources.title: Aurora DSQL: CREATE INDEX
supports: Index creation is always asynchronous, so the ASYNC keyword must be specified
CREATE [UNIQUE] INDEX ASYNC supports IF NOT EXISTS, INCLUDE, and a WHERE predicate

sources.title: Asynchronous indexes in Aurora DSQL
supports: CREATE INDEX ASYNC returns a job_id immediately
sys.jobs has job_id, status (submitted, processing, failed, completed), and details
A failed build leaves the index INVALID until it is dropped; completed and failed jobs are removed from sys.jobs after 30 minutes
sources.note: The page names sys.wait_for_job but shows no complete call, so the sample polls sys.jobs instead.

sources.title: Working with foreign key constraints in Aurora DSQL
supports: Foreign keys are checked against the transaction snapshot and again at commit; a violation by a concurrent transaction surfaces as a serialization error
Updating a non-key column of the referenced row does not conflict with an insert that references it
DML on referenced or referencing tables incurs extra reads

sources.title: Aurora DSQL: Working with sequences and identity columns
supports: UUIDs are the recommended default identifier type; sequences and identity columns exist for when integers are needed
CREATE SEQUENCE requires an explicit CACHE of 1 or at least 65536 (stated on the CREATE SEQUENCE page, which was read too)

sources.title: Primary keys in Aurora DSQL
supports: A primary key cannot be changed or added after the table is created
For tables with many writes, AWS advises against monotonically increasing integer keys and for randomly distributed ones

sources.title: Authentication and authorization for Aurora DSQL
supports: dsql:DbConnectAdmin connects as the admin role; dsql:DbConnect connects as a custom database role
AWS IAM GRANT associates a database role with an IAM identity
After revoking the IAM permission, existing connections can stay authorized until they end

sources.title: Generating an authentication token in Amazon Aurora DSQL
supports: The token is the password, used only when a connection is established; an open connection stays valid after the token expires
Tokens expire after 15 minutes by default, one week at most
Generating a token is a local signing operation that does not contact AWS
The cluster endpoint has the form <cluster id>.dsql.<region>.on.aws
The JavaScript signer is DsqlSigner in @aws-sdk/dsql-signer, with getDbConnectAuthToken and getDbConnectAdminAuthToken

sources.title: Aurora DSQL: Using database roles and IAM authentication
supports: CREATE ROLE ... WITH LOGIN, then AWS IAM GRANT <role> TO '<IAM role ARN>', then GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA and GRANT ... ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA
sys.iam_pg_role_mappings lists the mappings, with arn and pg_role_name columns

sources.title: Aurora DSQL Connectors for Node.js
supports: AWS publishes authentication plugins for node-postgres and for Postgres.js

sources.title: Aurora DSQL Connector for node-postgres
supports: The connector wraps node-postgres's Client and Pool and generates a token for each connection
A user named admin gets an admin token, any other user a regular one
sources.note: The sample does not use the connector; it passes the same signer to node-postgres directly, as the AWS Lambda sample does.

sources.title: Amazon Aurora DSQL cluster connectivity tools
supports: AWS lists driver samples for node-postgres, node-postgres on AWS Lambda, and Postgres.js
AWS lists an adapter for Drizzle ORM and samples for Prisma, Sequelize, and TypeORM

sources.title: aws-samples/aurora-dsql-samples: Using AWS Lambda with Amazon Aurora DSQL
supports: A Lambda function defined without a VPC connects with node-postgres, passing a function that calls DsqlSigner as the pool's password
The pool is kept in a module-level variable and shared between invocations
The sample builds the endpoint as <identifier>.dsql.<region>.on.aws and says an admin database role is not good practice for production

sources.title: Aurora DSQL cluster lifecycle
supports: A cluster without connection activity becomes Idle and then Inactive, where running resources are scaled to zero and data is kept
Connecting wakes it; the first connection to an Idle or Inactive cluster is slower
A backup needs an Active cluster

sources.title: Backup and restore for Amazon Aurora DSQL
supports: Backups go through AWS Backup: full cluster backups, on demand or on a schedule with retention
A restore always creates a new cluster
sources.note: The page does not describe point-in-time recovery for Aurora DSQL.

sources.title: How billing works in Aurora DSQL
supports: Activity is metered in DPUs (compute, read, and write components) and storage in GB-month
Worked examples: a point lookup of 0.00675 DPU and a single-row insert of 0.06175 DPU
sources.note: The examples' DPU figures are used as stand-ins in the chapter's cost scenario. Nothing was measured.

sources.title: Amazon Aurora DSQL pricing
supports: Billed for DPUs and for storage in GB-month; an idle cluster incurs no DPU charges
Each month the first 100,000 DPUs and 1 GB of storage are free
Backups are billed through AWS Backup
sources.note: The page shows prices through a script; the numbers in the book come from the Price List. The page does not say whether the free tier ends.

sources.title: Managing and connecting to Amazon Aurora DSQL clusters using AWS PrivateLink
supports: The default cluster host name is a public DNS name; interface VPC endpoints are an option for private connectivity
Connecting through an endpoint's own DNS name or IP address does not support verify-full

sources.title: Troubleshooting issues in Aurora DSQL
supports: After an error during COMMIT the transaction might have committed; AWS says to design transactions to be idempotent
'Wrong user to action mapping' means the token type does not match the database role
A connection is rejected when the assumed role's credentials have expired, even if the token has not

sources.title: Considerations for working with Amazon Aurora DSQL
supports: GRANT and REVOKE changes reach existing connections within the connection lifetime; a new connection sees them at once
A connection should be refreshed to see schemas and tables created in another connection

sources.title: Release notes for Aurora DSQL
supports: Foreign key constraints were added on August 26, 2026
Identity columns and sequences were added on February 13, 2026; partial indexes on September 15, 2026

sources.title: Configuring SSL/TLS certificates for Aurora DSQL connections
supports: The server certificate chains to Amazon Root CA 1; AWS recommends verify-full for production

supports: Properties: DeletionProtectionEnabled, KmsEncryptionKey, MultiRegionProperties, PolicyDocument, Tags; none is required
Ref returns the cluster identifier

supports: aws-cdk-lib/aws-dsql exports the generated CfnCluster (L1) and no higher-level construct
CfnCluster has deletionProtectionEnabled and exposes attrIdentifier, attrEndpoint, and attrResourceArn

sources.title: AWS Price List: Aurora DSQL, ap-northeast-1
supports: USD 0.00001 per DPU and USD 0.40 per GB-month of storage in Tokyo
Global SKUs priced at zero for the first 100,000 DPUs and the first GB-month

Aurora PostgreSQL Serverless v2: USD 0.15 per ACU-hour; Aurora PostgreSQL storage: USD 0.12 per GB-month

sources.title: Scaling to Zero ACUs with automatic pause and resume for Aurora serverless
supports: Auto-pause is a minimum capacity of 0 ACUs; before it existed the lowest minimum was 0.5 ACUs
An instance pauses after 300 to 86,400 seconds without user connections (default 300)
A paused instance has no instance charge; storage is still charged
Resuming takes about 15 seconds, and 30 seconds or longer after more than 24 hours paused
An open user connection, an associated RDS Proxy, logical replication, or a zero-ETL integration keeps instances from pausing
Aurora PostgreSQL needs 16.3, 15.7, 14.12, 13.15 or higher

sources.title: How Aurora serverless works
supports: Capacity ranges from 0 to 256 ACUs; one ACU is about 2 GiB of memory with matching CPU and networking

sources.title: Using the Amazon RDS Data API
supports: Data API is an HTTP endpoint for an Aurora cluster that lets a Lambda function run SQL without being configured for a VPC
It uses database credentials stored in AWS Secrets Manager
sources.note: Region and engine-version availability was not checked.

sources.title: Overview of backing up and restoring an Aurora DB cluster
supports: Aurora automated backups are continuous, with a retention period of 1 to 35 days, and cannot be disabled

sources.title: Working with a DB instance in a VPC
supports: An RDS DB instance is in a VPC and needs a DB subnet group

sources.title: Amazon RDS DB instance storage
supports: General Purpose gp3 storage for PostgreSQL starts at 20 GiB

sources.title: IAM database authentication for MariaDB, MySQL, and PostgreSQL
supports: RDS offers IAM database authentication with 15-minute tokens as an option next to standard passwords

sources.title: Amazon RDS Proxy
supports: RDS Proxy pools and shares database connections for applications that open many of them

sources.title: Restoring a DB instance to a specified time for Amazon RDS
supports: Point-in-time restore creates a new DB instance within the backup retention period

sources.title: PostgreSQL 16: Transaction Isolation
supports: Read Committed is the default isolation level in PostgreSQL
Repeatable Read is implemented as snapshot isolation and raises 'could not serialize access due to concurrent update'; the application should retry the whole transaction

sources.title: Cloudflare D1: Migrations
supports: Migrations are numbered .sql files in a migrations folder, applied in order by Wrangler
Applied migrations are recorded in the d1_migrations table

sources.title: Cloudflare D1: Global read replication
supports: Read replicas are asynchronously replicated and can be arbitrarily out of date; all writes go to the primary
Read replication is used only through the Sessions API, which provides sequential consistency within a session by passing bookmarks
withSession('first-primary') routes the first query to the primary

sources.title: Cloudflare D1: D1 Database (Workers Binding API)
supports: batch() runs its statements as one SQL transaction and rolls the whole sequence back if one fails

sources.title: Cloudflare D1: SQL statements
supports: D1 uses SQLite's query engine and is compatible with most of SQLite's SQL

sources.title: Cloudflare D1: Pricing
supports: D1 bills rows read, rows written, and storage, with no charge for hours or capacity when no queries run

sources.title: Cloudflare Wrangler: d1 commands
supports: `wrangler d1 migrations apply` takes --local or --remote
If applying a migration results in an error, that migration is rolled back

sources.title: Download and upload objects with presigned URLs
supports: A presigned URL uses the credentials of the principal who generated it, and its capabilities are limited by that principal's permissions
Presigned URLs are bearer tokens that grant access to those who possess them, and can be used multiple times until they expire
A presigned URL made with temporary credentials expires when those credentials expire, even if a later expiration was requested
With the AWS CLI or SDKs the expiration can be set as high as 7 days
S3 checks the expiration at the time of the HTTP request
A bucket policy can deny presigned requests by signature age with the s3:signatureAge condition key
sources.note: The page gives typical credential lifetimes for EC2 instance profiles, ECS tasks, and STS AssumeRole. It gives none for a Lambda execution role.

sources.title: Uploading objects with presigned URLs
supports: An upload to a key that already exists replaces the existing object
The content type in the upload request must match the one given when the presigned PUT URL was generated

sources.title: POST Policy
supports: A POST policy holds an expiration and a list of conditions the request must meet
content-length-range sets the minimum and maximum allowable size of the uploaded content
Conditions support exact matching and starts-with matching on fields such as key and Content-Type
Each form field except x-amz-signature, file, policy, and x-ignore- fields must appear in the list of conditions
sources.note: On 2026-10-11 the older path /AmazonS3/latest/API/sigv4-HTTPPOSTConstructPolicy.html redirected to the API reference index; the page was read at the /developerguide/ path. Its conditions table does not list the tagging field by name.

sources.title: POST Object
supports: The file must be the last field in the form
POST Object has a tagging form field that takes an XML tag set
success_action_status defaults to 204
A request without a policy is anonymous and works only on publicly writable buckets
sources.note: Read at the /developerguide/ path, as the /API/ path redirected to the index on 2026-10-11.

sources.title: Authenticating Requests: Using Query Parameters (AWS Signature Version 4)
supports: X-Amz-Expires is between 1 and 604800 seconds
The host header and any x-amz-* headers must be signed, and signing every header you plan to send is recommended
A presigned URL made with STS credentials carries X-Amz-Security-Token
sources.note: The page does not state a rule for content-length specifically. That a signed Content-Length pins the size of a presigned PUT was not confirmed.

sources.title: How to prevent object overwrites with conditional writes
supports: If-None-Match prevents overwriting an existing key
If-None-Match can be used with PutObject, CompleteMultipartUpload, and CopyObject; POST Object is not in the list

sources.title: HeadObject
supports: For a key that does not exist, S3 returns 404 if the caller has s3:ListBucket on the bucket and 403 if it does not

sources.title: Expiring objects
supports: In a nonversioned bucket, S3 queues an expired object for removal and removes it asynchronously
Tag-based filters are evaluated daily, and the object's current tags are re-evaluated when the action executes; if the tag is gone, the expiration does not proceed
There may be a delay between the expiration date and the removal, and expired objects are not charged for storage
A bucket policy cannot prevent deletions by a lifecycle rule

sources.title: Configuring a bucket lifecycle configuration to delete incomplete multipart uploads
supports: AWS recommends a lifecycle rule with AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload to minimize storage costs
The rule aborts multipart uploads not completed within the given number of days and deletes their parts; it deletes no objects

sources.title: Tagging your objects
supports: Tags can be set in a POST Object request
Lifecycle rules can filter on object tags
DELETE Object tagging removes the tag set without a request charge, where PUT Object tagging is billed as a Tier 1 request

sources.title: Using cross-origin resource sharing (CORS)
supports: S3 uses the first CORS rule whose origin, method, and requested headers match the request
ACLs and policies continue to apply when CORS is enabled

sources.title: Elements of a CORS configuration
supports: AllowedMethods accepts GET, PUT, POST, DELETE, and HEAD
AllowedOrigins lists the origins allowed to make cross-origin requests

sources.title: Blocking public access to your Amazon S3 storage
supports: The four settings BlockPublicAcls, IgnorePublicAcls, BlockPublicPolicy, and RestrictPublicBuckets

sources.title: What is Amazon S3? (Strong consistency)
supports: S3 provides strong read-after-write consistency for PUT and DELETE of objects, and reads of object tags and metadata such as HEAD are strongly consistent
sources.note: The sentence names PUT and DELETE. It does not name POST Object.

sources.title: @aws-sdk/s3-presigned-post 3.1149.0 (type definitions and source)
supports: createPresignedPost signs locally and sends no request
Each entry in Fields becomes an exact-match condition, and Conditions accepts content-length-range
The session token of temporary credentials is added as the X-Amz-Security-Token field

sources.title: AWS Price List bulk API: Data Transfer, ap-northeast-1
supports: Unit prices in data/pricing/unit-prices.json with offerCode AWSDataTransfer
Data transfer in from the internet is USD 0.000 per GB in ap-northeast-1
sources.note: The first tier is described as "beyond the global free tier". The size of that free tier was not confirmed.

sources.title: Cloudflare R2: Presigned URLs
supports: R2 presigned URLs support GET, HEAD, PUT, and DELETE; POST form uploads are not currently supported
R2 presigned URLs work on the S3 API domain and cannot be used with custom domains
R2's documentation also calls presigned URLs bearer tokens

sources.title: Working with Lambda environment variables
supports: Lambda sets AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, and AWS_SESSION_TOKEN to the access keys obtained from the function's execution role
sources.note: The page does not say how long these credentials stay valid.

sources.title: nuxt 4.6.1 (npm registry metadata and tarball)
supports: 4.6.1 was the `latest` dist-tag on 2026-10-11
Its server builder @nuxt/nitro-server 4.6.1 depends on nitropack ^2.13.4 (Nitro 2, not the nitro 3 beta)
`nuxt build` with the aws-lambda preset writes .output/server (handler and traced node_modules), .output/public/_nuxt, and .output/nitro.json
sources.note: The last item was observed by building examples/09-ssr. That Nuxt renders a page into one string before the handler writes it is an observation of the built handler (one write per page), not a documented guarantee.

sources.title: nitropack 2.13.4 (npm tarball: dist/presets/aws-lambda)
supports: The preset is named `aws-lambda`; its only option is `awsLambda.streaming` (boolean, default false)
With streaming false the entry exports `handler(event, context)` returning { statusCode, headers, cookies, body, isBase64Encoded }
With streaming true the entry is `awslambda.streamifyResponse(...)`, writes metadata through `awslambda.HttpResponseStream.from`, and adds `Transfer-Encoding: chunked`
Both entries rebuild the Cookie header from the event's `cookies` array and decode a base64 request body as UTF-8 text
.output/nitro.json records the preset and `config.awsLambda.streaming`
sources.note: Read from the installed package, dist/presets/aws-lambda/preset.mjs, types.d.ts, and runtime/aws-lambda{,-streaming}.mjs. The Nitro documentation site was not used as the basis.
