sources.title: aws-cdk-lib 2.273.0: aws-kinesisfirehose, aws-glue and aws-athena type definitions
supports: CfnDeliveryStream.ExtendedS3DestinationConfigurationProperty has prefix, errorOutputPrefix, compressionFormat (default UNCOMPRESSED), bufferingHints, dataFormatConversionConfiguration, dynamicPartitioningConfiguration and customTimeZone
ParquetSerDe compression is UNCOMPRESSED, SNAPPY or GZIP, default SNAPPY; SchemaConfiguration.versionId LATEST picks up table updates
CfnWorkGroup has bytesScannedCutoffPerQuery, enforceWorkGroupConfiguration, publishCloudWatchMetricsEnabled, resultConfiguration and recursiveDeleteOption

sources.title: hyparquet-writer 0.16.11 and hyparquet 1.31.3
supports: parquetWriteBuffer writes a Parquet file with the SNAPPY codec by default; parquetMetadata reads total_compressed_size per column chunk from the footer
sources.note: Used only on the laptop to measure column sizes. It is not what Firehose runs.

sources.title: Cloudflare Workers Analytics Engine (overview, get started, limits, pricing, SQL API, sampling)
supports: Workers Analytics Engine has an API to write data points from Workers and a SQL API to query them; writeDataPoint() need not be awaited
A data point holds up to twenty blobs, twenty doubles and one index; at most 250 data points per Worker invocation; data is stored for three months
Queries operate on a single table; UNION and JOIN are not supported
Data is sampled at write time when points arrive too quickly into one index, and again at query time for complex queries; counts use sum(_sample_interval)
Workers Paid includes 10 million data points and 1 million read queries a month; the pricing page says usage is not currently billed
sources.note: Sub-pages /get-started/, /limits/, /pricing/, /sql-api/, /sql-reference/statements/ and /sampling/ were read through a summarising fetch.

sources.title: Cloudflare Basin SQL (formerly R2 SQL), with pricing and limitations
supports: Basin SQL, formerly known as R2 SQL, is generally available and queries Apache Iceberg tables stored in Basin Catalog (formerly R2 Data Catalog)
It reads Parquet only, is read-only, and supports joins and exact aggregates such as COUNT(DISTINCT)
It is billed by compressed data scanned: 10 GB a month included, then USD 2.50 per TB, with a 10 MB minimum per query
No user-configurable per-query scan cap is documented
sources.note: The overview was re-read on 2026-10-13; /platform/pricing/ and /reference/limitations-best-practices/ on 2026-10-12, through a summarising fetch.

sources.title: Cloudflare Basin Pipelines (formerly Cloudflare Pipelines), with sinks and pricing
supports: Basin Pipelines is generally available on the Workers Paid plan; it receives events over HTTP or a Worker binding and writes Iceberg tables to Basin Catalog or Parquet and JSON files to R2
Ingress is free; sinks include 50 GB a month, then USD 0.03 per GB for JSON and USD 0.06 per GB for Parquet or Iceberg, on uncompressed volume
sources.note: Read through a summarising fetch, with /sinks/ and /platform/pricing/.

sources.title: Cloudflare Logpush (overview, pricing, datasets, destinations)
supports: Logpush delivers logs in batches to destinations such as R2, Basin Pipelines, Amazon S3 and HTTP endpoints; it offers no storage or search of its own
It is available with usage-based pricing on Free, Pro and Business plans; Workers Trace Events Logpush requires the Workers Paid plan
sources.note: Read through a summarising fetch, with /pricing/ and /logpush-job/enable-destinations/.

sources.title: Vercel Web Analytics: pricing, custom events, API
supports: An event is a tracked page view or a custom event; custom events are on Pro and Enterprise
Pro is billed USD 0.03 per 1,000 events with a reporting window of 12 months; Hobby includes 50,000 events a month with a 1-month window
The Web Analytics API returns aggregated data with OData filters; a CSV export holds up to 250 entries of a panel
sources.note: With /docs/analytics, /docs/analytics/custom-events, /docs/analytics/using-web-analytics and /docs/analytics/web-analytics-api.

sources.title: Vercel Observability Plus and Query
supports: Query builds metric aggregations from form fields (event type, metric, filter, group by) and exports results as CSV or JSON; full access requires Observability Plus
Observability Plus is USD 1.20 per million events and keeps data for 30 days
The pages describe no SQL interface
sources.note: With /docs/observability/observability-plus and /docs/query/reference.

sources.title: Vercel Drains
supports: Drains forward logs, traces, Speed Insights and Web Analytics events to a custom HTTP endpoint or a native integration; they are on Pro and Enterprise
S3 bucket destinations are available only for Audit Log Drains
Drains are billed by the uncompressed JSON volume of the drained records (the table shows USD 0.50)
sources.note: With /docs/drains/using-drains. The table does not print the unit; the surrounding text speaks of billed gigabytes.

sources.title: Working with S3 Vectors and vector buckets
supports: S3 Vectors stores vectors in vector indexes inside vector buckets and answers similarity queries, with no infrastructure to provision
Writes to S3 Vectors are strongly consistent
Sub-second latency for infrequent queries and as low as 100 ms for more frequent ones, as described by AWS
Block Public Access is always on for vector buckets
The service namespace is s3vectors

sources.title: S3 Vectors limitations and restrictions
supports: Up to 2 billion vectors per index, dimensions from 1 to 4,096
Up to 2 KB of filterable metadata and 40 KB of total metadata per vector
Up to 500 vectors per PutVectors or DeleteVectors call
Up to 100 results per page of a QueryVectors response
Up to 100 filter constraints per query on an ENHANCED index

sources.title: AWS Regions, endpoints, and quotas for S3 Vectors
supports: S3 Vectors is available in ap-northeast-1 (Tokyo)

sources.title: S3 Vectors metadata filtering
supports: An ENHANCED index applies the metadata filter before the vector search (pre-filtering)
Vector buckets created on or after September 30, 2026 create ENHANCED indexes
On a CLASSIC index a filtered query may return fewer than top K results
The filter operators, including $eq
All metadata is filterable unless declared non-filterable when the index is created

sources.title: S3 Vectors best practices
supports: AWS recommends one vector index per tenant for multi-tenant workloads, with IAM restricting each tenant to its index
Exceeding request rates returns 429 TooManyRequestsException
Hundreds of QueryVectors requests per second per index

sources.title: Creating a vector index in a vector bucket
supports: An index's name, dimension, distance metric and non-filterable metadata keys cannot be changed after creation

sources.title: Identity and Access management in S3 Vectors
supports: The ARN format of a vector index
A QueryVectors call with a metadata filter or returnMetadata also needs s3vectors:GetVectors
The policy actions s3vectors:PutVectors, DeleteVectors, QueryVectors, GetVectors, ListVectors

sources.title: QueryVectors API reference
supports: QueryVectors performs an approximate nearest neighbor search
The request takes indexArn, queryVector, topK, filter, returnMetadata, returnDistance
The response gives key, distance and metadata per vector

sources.title: PutVectors API reference
supports: Vectors are stored as float32
A PutVectors request takes 1 to 500 vectors, each with a key, data and optional metadata

sources.title: DeleteVectors API reference
supports: DeleteVectors takes 1 to 500 keys
sources.note: The page does not say what happens when a key does not exist. The chapter records that as unconfirmed.

sources.title: AWS::S3Vectors::Index
supports: The properties DataType, Dimension, DistanceMetric, IndexName, VectorBucketName
Changing DataType, Dimension or DistanceMetric replaces the index

sources.title: AWS::S3Vectors::VectorBucket
supports: A vector bucket name is unique within an account and Region
Only an empty vector bucket can be deleted

sources.title: Amazon S3 pricing (Vectors)
supports: PUT is billed per logical GB with a minimum of 128 KB per PUT
A query is billed a request fee, data processed based on the size of the whole index, and data returned
Non-filterable metadata is not counted in data processed
Each dimension takes 4 bytes of storage
sources.note: The page's own examples use US East (N. Virginia) prices. The chapter's prices come from the price list for ap-northeast-1.

sources.title: AWS Price List: Amazon S3, ap-northeast-1 (Vectors)
supports: S3 Vectors unit prices in ap-northeast-1: storage, PUT bytes, query requests, data processed, other requests

sources.title: Managing capacity limits for Amazon OpenSearch Serverless
supports: One OCU is 6 GiB of memory with corresponding vCPU
Minimum and maximum OCUs are set per collection group, and a minimum of 0 means no OCUs when idle

sources.title: Collection group capacity limits
supports: A NextGen collection group accepts a minimum of 0 OCUs
A Classic collection group does not support a minimum of 0

sources.title: What is Amazon OpenSearch Serverless?
supports: Collection types: time series, search, vector search
NextGen collections support the search and vector search types only
Search and time series collections cannot use k-NN indexes
The refresh interval of search and time series collections is about 10 seconds

sources.title: Working with vector search collections
supports: NextGen vector search scales indexing and search to zero when idle
NextGen vector collections have a read-after-write latency of 10 seconds

sources.title: Amazon OpenSearch Service endpoints and quotas
supports: OpenSearch Serverless has endpoints in ap-northeast-1
Collection groups have separate quotas for Classic and NextGen

sources.title: Amazon OpenSearch Service pricing (Serverless)
supports: A Classic collection is billed at least 2 OCUs for the first collection in an account, or 1 OCU without standby replicas
NextGen collections have no minimum OCU and scale to zero after 10 minutes of inactivity
Storage is billed separately

sources.title: How DynamoDB global tables work
supports: A global table has two or more replicas in different Regions, one per Region, all with the same table name and key schema
The default consistency mode is multi-Region eventual consistency (MREC), and the mode cannot be changed after creation
In MREC, item changes are replicated asynchronously, typically within a second or less
In MREC, simultaneous changes to one item in several Regions are resolved by the latest internal timestamp per item (last writer wins)
In MREC, a strongly consistent read may return stale data if the item was last updated in another Region, and a conditional write evaluates its condition against the item's version in the Region
In MRSC, a change is replicated synchronously to at least one other Region before the write returns, and conditional writes evaluate against the latest version
An MRSC global table spans exactly three Regions: three replicas, or two replicas and a witness that cannot be read or written
A write to an item being modified in another Region fails with ReplicatedWriteConflictException in MRSC and can be retried
TTL and local secondary indexes are not supported in MRSC; transactions are not supported in MRSC and are atomic only within one Region in MREC
MREC has an RPO equal to the replication delay; MRSC supports an RPO of zero
MREC publishes the ReplicationLatency metric per source and destination Region pair; MRSC does not
Global tables have a 99.999% availability SLA, single-Region tables 99.99%
AWS FIS can pause replication to and from a replica to simulate Region isolation
MRSC is available in Tokyo, Seoul and Osaka among other Regions
sources.note: This page says an MRSC table can combine any three of the listed Regions; the design guide (mr-dynamodb-global-tables-design) lists Region sets that cannot be mixed. Tokyo, Seoul and Osaka are in one set either way.

sources.title: Using DynamoDB global tables
supports: DynamoDB has no global endpoint: every request goes to a Regional endpoint and reaches the replica in that Region
MREC write conflicts are not recorded in CloudWatch or CloudTrail
There is no SLA on ReplicationLatency; a new item usually reaches all replicas within a second
Each item carries a private last-write timestamp, and an incoming replicated item is applied only if its timestamp is greater
Items are replicated individually, and the order of writes in a remote Region may differ from the source Region
The local Region accepts writes while another Region is offline, and pending replication is retried when it returns
With MRSC, a Region accepts reads and writes only while a second Region (replica or witness) is reachable; otherwise it serves eventually consistent reads only
MRSC Region sets: Tokyo, Seoul and Osaka form the AP set, and a table cannot span sets
MRSC was introduced in June 2025

sources.title: Write modes with DynamoDB global tables
supports: Global tables are always active-active at the table level; treating one as active-passive is done by routing writes outside DynamoDB
Writing to one Region avoids conflicts in MREC and is what conditional expressions and transactions need
Writing to any Region suits MRSC tables, and MREC tables whose writes are idempotent assignments

sources.title: Evacuation processes
supports: Moving the write Region of an MREC table means pausing writes, waiting for replication, then resuming in the new Region
No metric says with certainty that replication has completed; waiting ten times the recent maximum ReplicationLatency is given as typically sufficient for a healthy Region
When an MREC Region goes offline, its unreplicated writes are held and propagated after it returns, and a later update in the other Region suppresses them under last writer wins

sources.title: Understanding Amazon DynamoDB billing for global tables
supports: A write to a global table is billed as one replicated write request unit per replica table, in each replica's Region
Replicated write units are priced the same as single-Region write units
DynamoDB does not charge cross-Region data transfer for replication between the Regions of a global table
A witness incurs no replicated write, storage or transfer cost

sources.title: Best practices for global tables
supports: CloudFormation cannot coordinate a global table across stacks: all replicas should be defined in one Region's stack
Changing a resource's type from AWS::DynamoDB::Table to AWS::DynamoDB::GlobalTable may delete the table
Deletion protection is enabled per replica
Point-in-time recovery on one replica may be enough for disaster recovery objectives

Two-way replication keeps buckets in two Regions in sync during a failover

sources.title: What does Amazon S3 replicate?

With the current configuration format, delete markers are not replicated by default
A DELETE that names a version ID is not replicated to the destination
Objects that are themselves replicas created by another rule are not replicated

sources.title: Understanding the Lambda execution environment lifecycle
supports: The Init phase starts all extensions, bootstraps the runtime and runs the function's static code; it is limited to 10 seconds, and if it does not complete Lambda retries it at the first invocation with the configured function timeout
The 10-second limit does not apply to provisioned concurrency, SnapStart or Lambda Managed Instances
The function's timeout limits the entire Invoke phase, extensions included
After a failed invocation Lambda resets the environment and re-initializes it with the next invocation (a suppressed init), without reporting a separate Init phase in CloudWatch Logs
Lambda keeps an environment for some time after an invocation and terminates environments every few hours; objects declared outside the handler remain initialized while it is reused
Cold starts typically occur in under 1% of invocations and take from under 100 ms to over 1 second
The example REPORT and INIT_REPORT lines used as test fixtures, including Init Duration, Status and Error Type
Factors of initialization latency: package size including layers, the amount of initialization code, and the libraries' own setup; objects used only on some paths can be loaded lazily
For on-demand functions Lambda might occasionally initialize environments ahead of requests
sources.note: The page lists three Init tasks. Whether downloading the code and starting the environment are inside the reported Init Duration is not stated there.

sources.title: Understanding Lambda function scaling
supports: Concurrency = (average requests per second) x (average request duration in seconds)
An execution environment is busy for the whole of Init and Invoke and cannot process other requests meanwhile
The default account concurrency limit is 1,000 per Region, shared by all functions
Lambda always keeps 100 units for functions without reserved concurrency
Lambda enforces a requests-per-second limit of 10 times the concurrency, at the account and the function level
Reserved concurrency is both the maximum and the minimum for a function and is free of charge; provisioned concurrency pre-initializes environments and is charged
With provisioned concurrency a cold start can still occur when Lambda has to reset an environment
aws lambda get-account-settings returns ConcurrentExecutions and UnreservedConcurrentExecutions
sources.note: One paragraph of the page says a function can gain 500 concurrency every 10 seconds; the scaling page and the quotas page say 1,000. The chapter quotes the latter two.

sources.title: Lambda scaling behavior
supports: Per function and Region, concurrency scales by at most 1,000 execution environments every 10 seconds (or 10,000 requests per second every 10 seconds)
Requests that arrive faster than the function can scale, or at maximum concurrency, fail with a throttling error (429)

sources.title: Configuring reserved concurrency for a function
supports: You can reserve up to the unreserved account concurrency minus 100
Reserved concurrency 0 stops the function from processing any event
Configuring reserved concurrency incurs no additional charge

sources.title: Configuring provisioned concurrency for a function
supports: Provisioned concurrency cannot be used with $LATEST; it is set on a version or an alias, and the event source must point at that qualifier
Provisioned concurrency cannot exceed the function's reserved concurrency
Initialization code runs at allocation time and again when Lambda recycles environments, and is billed even if the environment never serves a request
With provisioned concurrency Lambda logs a platform.initReport event in the JSON log format each time an environment is initialized
Excess traffic is served by on-demand environments; AWS_LAMBDA_INITIALIZATION_TYPE is provisioned-concurrency or on-demand
Lambda suggests a 10% buffer on top of the usual peak concurrency

sources.title: Configure Lambda function memory
supports: Memory is 128 MB to 10,240 MB in 1-MB increments; CPU is allocated in proportion to memory, and 1,769 MB corresponds to one vCPU
The documentation points to the open source AWS Lambda Power Tuning tool to find the right setting
Compute Optimizer's memory recommendations support only x86_64 functions

sources.title: Configure Lambda function timeout
supports: The default timeout is 3 seconds and the maximum 900 seconds
A timeout close to the average duration risks unexpected timeouts

sources.title: Lambda quotas
supports: New AWS accounts have reduced concurrency and memory quotas, raised automatically based on usage
Concurrent executions: 1,000 by default, adjustable
Function concurrency scaling limit: 1,000 execution environments every 10 seconds per function
Deployment package: 50 MB zipped through the API, 250 MB unzipped including layers
Five layers per function
Lambda's documentation uses MB to mean 1,024 KB

sources.title: Best practices for working with AWS Lambda functions
supports: Initialize SDK clients and database connections outside the handler so that later invocations in the same environment reuse them
Do not keep user data or anything with security implications in the execution environment between invocations
Max Memory Used in the REPORT line shows whether the function is over- or under-provisioned
For an SQS event source the function's invocation time must not exceed the queue's visibility timeout
Reserved concurrency can be used to limit how far a function scales; setting it to 0 stops a runaway function

sources.title: Building Lambda functions with Node.js
supports: Every supported Node.js runtime includes a specific minor version of the AWS SDK for JavaScript v3, which depends on the runtime version and the Region and is not the latest
Keep-alive for TCP connections is on by default in the supported Node.js runtimes
nodejs24.x is a supported runtime on Amazon Linux 2023; nodejs26.x is listed as well

sources.title: Define Lambda function handler in Node.js
supports: Lambda recommends ES modules because they support top-level await, so asynchronous initialization completes in the Init phase
Code outside the handler runs during initialization and what it creates stays in memory between invocations
To control dependencies, package them with the function instead of relying on the libraries in the runtime, which Lambda updates periodically
Minimize the deployment package to its runtime necessities to reduce the time to download and unpack it

sources.title: Deploy Node.js Lambda functions with .zip file archives
supports: Bundling with esbuild, rollup or similar is the recommended way to ship dependencies and improves performance by reducing I/O operations
A different version of a runtime-included library can be bundled with the function

platform.initReport carries initializationType (on-demand or provisioned-concurrency), phase (init, invoke or snap-start), status and metrics.durationMs
For Lambda Managed Instances platform.report contains only durationMs
The two example events used as test fixtures

sources.title: Configuring JSON and plain text log formats

In the JSON format each system log item is an object with time, type and record, shaped like the Telemetry API's events, and often carries more than the text form

Throttles counts refused invocations, which are in neither Invocations nor Errors
ProvisionedConcurrencySpilloverInvocations counts invocations served on standard concurrency when all provisioned concurrency is in use
ConcurrentExecutions is the number of function instances processing events

For Go and Rust the page advises against layers because loading from them can lengthen cold starts

sources.title: Augment Lambda functions using Lambda extensions

You are charged for the time an extension runs, in 1 ms increments
PostRuntimeExtensionsDuration measures the time extensions take after the function code has completed

A single Workers instance may handle multiple requests concurrently in one event loop, and isolates may be evicted

CPU time per HTTP request: 10 ms on Free; on Paid 30 seconds by default, up to 5 minutes
Worker size: 64 MiB uncompressed; larger bundles can affect startup time
Startup time: the global scope must parse and execute within 1 second, checked at deployment

sources.title: Cloudflare Workers: Pricing

sources.title: Vercel: Fluid compute
supports: Fluid compute lets multiple invocations share one function instance (Node.js and Python), and is enabled by default for new projects since April 23, 2025
Vercel reduces cold starts with bytecode caching on Node.js 20+ in production and with pre-warming of functions on production deployments

sources.title: Data modeling foundations in DynamoDB
supports: Single table design stores several entity types in one table; items with the same partition key (an item collection) are stored together, so one query can return several entity types
Listed disadvantages: backups are all or nothing, table encryption is shared, and every change goes to the stream even if only some entities are processed

sources.title: Using Global Secondary Indexes in DynamoDB
supports: A global secondary index is updated asynchronously and eventually consistently; propagation is within a fraction of a second under normal conditions, and longer delays are possible
A global secondary index supports only eventually consistent reads, and GetItem and BatchGetItem cannot be used on it
Only items in which the index key attributes exist appear in the index
Index key attributes must be top-level String, Number, or Binary
Projection is KEYS_ONLY, INCLUDE, or ALL; a query on the index cannot fetch attributes that were not projected
Index write cost: one write to put a new entry, two when an index key attribute changes, one when only a projected attribute changes, none when neither keys nor projected attributes change
If an index has insufficient write capacity, writes to the base table are throttled
Index storage is billed in addition to the table's
Global secondary indexes support multi-attribute keys of up to four attributes each for the partition key and the sort key
sources.note: Multi-attribute keys are mentioned in the chapter but not used; they were not tried with cdkd 0.296.28 or DynamoDB Local 3.3.1.

sources.title: Take advantage of sparse indexes
supports: An index where only a subset of the table's items appear is a sparse index; global secondary indexes are sparse by default

sources.title: Managing Global Secondary Indexes in DynamoDB
supports: The default quota is 20 global secondary indexes per table
Adding an index to an existing table backfills it from the table's items; while it is backfilling, IndexStatus is CREATING and Backfilling is true
A skewed partition key on a new index can cause backfill and writes to throttle writes to the base table; Contributor Insights is suggested for seeing the distribution

sources.title: Local secondary indexes
supports: A local secondary index is specified when the table is created
A local secondary index can be read with strong consistency
A table with a local secondary index is limited to 10 GB per partition key value

sources.title: Amazon DynamoDB Transactions: How it works
supports: TransactWriteItems groups up to 100 actions on up to 100 distinct items, 4 MB in total, in one all-or-nothing operation within one account and Region
One transaction cannot target the same item with more than one action
Actions are Put, Update, Delete, and ConditionCheck
Each item in a transaction costs two underlying reads or writes, and the capacity is consumed even when the transaction is cancelled
A cancelled transaction fails with TransactionCanceledException, which lists CancellationReasons in the order of the request's items; the AWS SDKs do not retry it
A transaction conflicts with another ongoing transaction or write on the same item
A client token makes TransactWriteItems idempotent for 10 minutes
Isolation between a transaction and a Query or Scan is read-committed, not serializable
Changes of one transaction reach indexes and the stream gradually; stream consumers should not assume atomicity or ordering across its records
Transactions are not supported across Regions in global tables

sources.title: Using IAM with DynamoDB transactions
supports: Put, Update, Delete, and Get inside a transaction are governed by the PutItem, UpdateItem, DeleteItem, and GetItem permissions; ConditionCheck needs dynamodb:ConditionCheckItem

sources.title: Constraints in Amazon DynamoDB
supports: A transaction cannot contain more than 100 unique items or more than 4 MB, and no two actions can work against the same item

sources.title: Quotas in Amazon DynamoDB
supports: Up to 5 local secondary indexes per table and a default of 20 global secondary indexes
Up to 100 attributes can be projected across all of a table's secondary indexes
Up to two simultaneous readers per stream shard for a table that is not a global table
DynamoDB counts 1 KB as 1024 bytes

sources.title: Working with items and attributes in DynamoDB
supports: A conditional write whose condition is false still consumes write capacity
Conditional writes check their condition against the most recently updated version of the item

sources.title: Reserved words in DynamoDB
supports: COUNT, SIZE, and NAME are reserved words, so they need expression attribute names

sources.title: Query (DynamoDB API reference)
supports: ExclusiveStartKey is the primary key of the first item the operation evaluates, taken from the previous LastEvaluatedKey
The result of one Query is at most 1 MB
sources.note: What DynamoDB answers to a starting key outside the queried partition is not stated on this page. DynamoDB Local 3.3.1 refused it; AWS was not tried.

sources.title: Change data capture for DynamoDB Streams
supports: A stream keeps item-level changes for up to 24 hours
Each stream record appears exactly once in the stream, and records for one item appear in the order of its modifications
Ordering is guaranteed for an individual item, not for a whole partition or item collection
StreamViewType is KEYS_ONLY, NEW_IMAGE, OLD_IMAGE, or NEW_AND_OLD_IMAGES, and cannot be edited once set
A PutItem or UpdateItem that changes no data writes no stream record

sources.title: Using AWS Lambda with Amazon DynamoDB
supports: Lambda event source mappings process each event at least once, and duplicate processing can occur
Lambda polls each shard at a base rate of four times a second
With LATEST as the starting position the mapping could miss events during creation or updates; TRIM_HORIZON avoids that
Up to two Lambda functions can read one shard of a single-Region table's stream at the same time

sources.title: Lambda parameters for Amazon DynamoDB event source mappings
supports: MaximumRetryAttempts defaults to -1 (retry until the record expires); BatchSize defaults to 100; BisectBatchOnFunctionError defaults to false
The on-failure destination is a standard SQS queue or a standard SNS topic

sources.title: Configuring partial batch response with DynamoDB and Lambda
supports: With ReportBatchItemFailures, the function returns batchItemFailures with the sequence number of a failed record; Lambda checkpoints at the lowest one and retries from there
An empty batchItemFailures list is a complete success
Partial batch responses reduce retries of successful records but do not entirely prevent them

sources.title: Retain discarded records for a DynamoDB event source in Lambda
supports: The message sent to an on-failure destination describes the batch but does not contain the records, which must be read from the stream before they expire
The execution role needs sqs:SendMessage for an SQS on-failure destination

sources.title: Using event filtering with a DynamoDB event source
supports: A DynamoDB event source mapping can filter only on the dynamodb key of the record, for example on dynamodb.Keys

sources.title: Time to Live (TTL): how it works
supports: Expired items are deleted typically within a few days of their expiry time, without consuming write throughput

sources.title: Best practices for designing and using partition keys effectively in DynamoDB
supports: Every partition is designed to deliver at most 3,000 read units and 1,000 write units a second

sources.title: DynamoDB burst and adaptive capacity
supports: Adaptive capacity can isolate a frequently accessed item on its own partition, up to the partition maximum for that single item
Adaptive capacity does not split an item collection across partitions when the table has a local secondary index

sources.title: Key range throughput exceeded (hot partitions)
supports: A partition over its limit is throttled with the reason KeyRangeThroughputExceeded, for a table or an index, whatever the table's total capacity
Short-lived throttling can stop by itself when DynamoDB splits the hot partition

sources.title: Understanding GSI write throttling and back pressure in DynamoDB
supports: When an index cannot keep up, writes to the base table are throttled, and the exception names the index
An index is partitioned by its own partition key, so it can have a hot partition while the table has none

sources.title: CloudWatch contributor insights for DynamoDB: How it works
supports: Two modes: throttled keys, and accessed and throttled keys
In throttled keys mode, a table with a sort key gets two rules (partition key, and partition and sort key), and only throttled requests generate billable events
Billing is a monthly charge per rule plus a charge per event

sources.title: DynamoDB local usage notes
supports: DynamoDB Local does not throw TransactionConflictException for the transactional APIs

sources.title: Amazon DynamoDB pricing for on-demand capacity
supports: A transactional write costs two write request units per 1 KB, and a transactional read two read request units per 4 KB
GetRecords calls made by DynamoDB triggers on AWS Lambda are not charged, except for functions on Lambda Managed Instances

sources.title: Cloudflare D1: Limits
supports: A D1 database is at most 10 GB on the Workers Paid plan, and that limit cannot be raised
Each D1 database is single-threaded and processes queries one at a time
D1 is designed for scaling out across many smaller databases, such as one per user or tenant

sources.title: Cloudflare D1: Use indexes
supports: D1 indexes are created with SQL, and CREATE UNIQUE INDEX enforces uniqueness

sources.title: Cloudflare D1: Pricing
supports: D1 bills rows read and rows written; a write to an indexed column adds at least one more row written

sources.title: Cloudflare D1: D1Database (batch)
supports: Statements sent with batch() run as one SQL transaction: if one fails, the whole sequence is rolled back

sources.title: Cloudflare Durable Objects: SQLite-backed storage API
supports: A SQLite-backed Durable Object has a SQL API, transactionSync(), and point-in-time recovery over the last 30 days

sources.title: Cloudflare Durable Objects: Limits
supports: Storage per SQLite-backed Durable Object is 10 GB

sources.title: Cloudflare: What are Durable Objects?
supports: Each Durable Object is single-threaded and has its own transactional, strongly consistent storage, accessible only within that object

sources.title: Vercel Storage overview
supports: Vercel's own storage products are Blob and Global Config; relational, key-value, NoSQL, and vector databases are provisioned from providers through the Vercel Marketplace

sources.title: Implement Lambda canary deployments using a weighted alias
supports: An alias can point to at most two function versions; both must be published, have the same execution role, and the same dead-letter queue configuration
Lambda uses a simple probabilistic model to distribute traffic, and at low traffic the actual split can differ widely from the configured one
The START log line names the invoked version, and synchronous responses carry x-amz-executed-version
update-alias with an empty AdditionalVersionWeights and a new function-version routes everything to the new version and resets the routing configuration

sources.title: Working with deployment configurations in CodeDeploy
supports: The nine predefined Lambda configurations: four LambdaCanary10Percent{5,10,15,30}Minutes, four LambdaLinear10PercentEvery{1,2,3,10}Minute(s), and LambdaAllAtOnce
A canary configuration shifts 10 percent first and the remaining 90 percent after the wait; a linear one shifts 10 percent at each interval

sources.title: UpdateAlias (Lambda API reference)
supports: UpdateAlias takes FunctionVersion, RoutingConfig.AdditionalVersionWeights, and RevisionId
With RevisionId the alias is only updated if it has not changed since it was read; otherwise PreconditionFailedException (HTTP 412)

sources.title: PublishVersion (Lambda API reference)
supports: PublishVersion creates a version from the current code and configuration of the function
Lambda does not publish a version if the code and configuration have not changed since the last version

sources.title: DeleteFunction (Lambda API reference)
supports: Deleting a function without a qualifier deletes all its versions and aliases
A version that an alias references cannot be deleted on its own

sources.title: @aws-sdk/client-appconfig 3.1149.0 (type definitions)
supports: StopDeployment works only on a deployment in DEPLOYING unless AllowRevert is supplied; with it an in-progress deployment becomes ROLLED_BACK and a completed one REVERTED, within 72 hours of completion
Deployment states are VALIDATING, DEPLOYING, BAKING, COMPLETE, ROLLING_BACK, ROLLED_BACK, REVERTED

sources.title: Types of metrics for Lambda functions
supports: Errors counts invocations that end in a function error (thrown exceptions, timeouts, configuration errors); view it with the Sum statistic
Invocations are not recorded for throttled requests

sources.title: Viewing metrics for Lambda functions
supports: The Resource dimension gives metrics for a version or an alias
The ExecutedVersion dimension gives metrics for a combination of alias and version, to compare the two versions behind a weighted alias

sources.title: Working with Lambda environment variables
supports: AWS_LAMBDA_FUNCTION_VERSION is a reserved runtime variable: the version of the function being executed
Environment variables are locked into a version when it is published

sources.title: Monitor CloudWatch metrics for HTTP APIs in API Gateway
supports: HTTP APIs publish 4xx, 5xx, Count, IntegrationLatency, Latency, and DataProcessed, by ApiId or by ApiId and Stage, in one-minute periods

supports: CodeDeployLambdaAliasUpdate is an UpdatePolicy on AWS::Lambda::Alias: CloudFormation performs a CodeDeploy deployment when the version changes on the alias

sources.title: Using AWS AppConfig Agent with AWS Lambda
supports: AWS recommends adding the AppConfig Agent Lambda extension as a layer to functions that read feature flags
AppConfig pricing is based on the number of times a configuration is called and received, and costs increase with cold starts

sources.title: Understanding how the AWS AppConfig Agent Lambda extension works
supports: The function calls the extension at an HTTP endpoint on localhost:2772; the extension keeps a local cache and calls AppConfig when the data is not cached
On each invocation the extension checks whether the poll interval has elapsed and, if so, checks AppConfig for newly deployed data
Each execution environment has its own cache

sources.title: Configuring the AWS AppConfig Agent Lambda extension
supports: AWS_APPCONFIG_EXTENSION_POLL_INTERVAL_SECONDS defaults to 45, AWS_APPCONFIG_EXTENSION_HTTP_PORT to 2772, AWS_APPCONFIG_EXTENSION_POLL_TIMEOUT_MILLIS to 3000 ms
When AppConfig does not answer within the poll timeout, the extension skips that poll and returns the previously cached data
AWS_APPCONFIG_EXTENSION_PREFETCH_LIST makes the extension retrieve a configuration, named by its /applications/.../environments/.../configurations/... path, before the function is initialized

sources.title: Understanding available versions of the AWS AppConfig Agent Lambda extension
supports: Extension version 2.0.22365 for ARM64 in ap-northeast-1 is arn:aws:lambda:ap-northeast-1:980059726660:layer:AWS-AppConfig-Extension-Arm64:231
The latest layer ARN is also published as the public SSM parameter /aws/service/aws-appconfig/lambda-extension/arm64/latest

sources.title: Understanding the type reference for AWS.AppConfig.FeatureFlags
supports: The stored document has version "1", flags (definitions with attributes and constraints), and values; keys match ^[a-z][a-zA-Z\d_-]{0,63}$
What GetLatestConfiguration returns is a map of flag key to {enabled, ...attributes}, without the definitions, and the attributes are present only if the flag is enabled

sources.title: Working with deployment strategies (AppConfig)
supports: A deployment strategy has a type (linear or exponential), a step percentage (growth factor), a deployment time, and a bake time
If an alarm is triggered during the bake time, AppConfig rolls the deployment back

sources.title: Using predefined deployment strategies (AppConfig)
supports: The predefined strategies are AppConfig.Linear20PercentEvery6Minutes, AppConfig.Canary10Percent20Minutes, AppConfig.AllAtOnce, and AppConfig.Linear50PercentEvery30Seconds

sources.title: How to use AWS AppConfig Agent to retrieve configuration data
supports: The agent serves GET /applications/{Application}/environments/{Environment}/configurations/{Configuration} on localhost:2772
With an Entity-Id header the agent keeps one entity on one configuration version throughout a gradual deployment; this needs agent version 2.0.136060 or later

sources.title: Setting up AWS AppConfig: configure permissions for automatic rollback
supports: AppConfig rolls back on CloudWatch alarms through an IAM role that trusts appconfig.amazonaws.com and allows cloudwatch:DescribeAlarms
The documented policy uses Resource "*", which is required to read composite alarms

sources.title: Understanding validators (AppConfig)
supports: AppConfig validates feature flag documents against a JSON Schema automatically; Lambda validators are also supported for feature flags

sources.title: DeleteConfigurationProfile (AppConfig API reference)
supports: DeleteConfigurationProfile can answer ConflictException; the page does not say whether stored versions must be deleted first

sources.title: Amazon ECS blue/green deployments
supports: ECS runs the blue and the green service revision side by side and shifts traffic itself for services behind a load balancer, Service Connect, or VPC Lattice
Bake time is how long both revisions keep running after production traffic has shifted
Both revisions run at once, which may double resource usage during a deployment

sources.title: Amazon ECS canary deployments
supports: An ECS canary deployment shifts the canary percentage first and the rest after the canary bake time, using two target groups and weighted routing on the load balancer
Lifecycle stages run from RECONCILE_SERVICE to CLEAN_UP, and hooks can run at most of them
CloudWatch alarms can trigger an automatic rollback

sources.title: DeploymentConfiguration (ECS API reference)
supports: strategy is one of ROLLING, BLUE_GREEN, LINEAR, CANARY
The API reference says the deployment circuit breaker can only be used for services using the rolling update (ECS) deployment type

sources.title: CanaryConfiguration (ECS API reference)
supports: canaryPercent takes multiples of 0.1 from 0.1 to 100.0 and defaults to 5.0; canaryBakeTimeInMinutes takes 0 to 1440 and defaults to 10

sources.title: How the Amazon ECS deployment circuit breaker detects failures
supports: The circuit breaker counts tasks that fail to reach RUNNING and tasks replaced for failing health checks
The default threshold is 50 percent of the desired count, bounded to at least 3 and at most 200

sources.title: How CloudWatch alarms detect Amazon ECS deployment failures
supports: ECS fails a deployment when a named alarm goes into ALARM, and can roll back
If an alarm is already in ALARM when a deployment starts, ECS does not monitor alarms for that deployment

sources.title: Cloudflare Workers: Gradual deployments
supports: A gradual deployment splits traffic between two versions of a Worker by percentage, and each request is routed independently by default
Version affinity can keep a user on one version; only one version of a Durable Object runs at a time
The page describes rolling back by hand and no automatic rollback on an error rate

sources.title: Cloudflare Flagship
supports: Flagship is Cloudflare's feature flag service, evaluated through a Worker binding or OpenFeature SDKs, with targeting rules and percentage rollouts by consistent hashing
sources.note: The page states neither a beta or GA status nor a price.

sources.title: Cloudflare Flagship: Concepts
supports: Flag configuration is distributed across Cloudflare's network within seconds, and can take up to 30 seconds
If the dashboard is unavailable, evaluation continues with the last propagated configuration

sources.title: Vercel: Rolling Releases
supports: Rolling Releases are available on Pro (one project) and Enterprise plans
Stages are traffic fractions ending at 100%; advancing is by hand or after a configured time, and aborting is by hand or Instant Rollback
A visitor is assigned to a bucket stored in a cookie, so the same device keeps seeing the same deployment

sources.title: Vercel: Skew Protection
supports: Skew Protection pins framework-managed requests to the deployment that served the page, by a dpl query parameter or x-deployment-id header
It is available on Pro and Enterprise plans, with a default maximum age of one day

sources.title: Vercel: Flags
supports: Vercel can be the feature flag provider itself (Vercel Flags) or connect providers from its Marketplace

sources.title: What is Service Quotas?
supports: Quotas, also referred to as limits, are the maximum values for the resources, actions, and items in an AWS account; each service defines its quotas and their default values
The console shows whether a quota is adjustable; an applied quota is the value after an increase, the default value is the initial value AWS set
A quota applies to an account or to a Region; a global quota can be raised only from US East (N. Virginia)
Utilization is the percentage of a quota in use; the console graphs it after the account has been active for a period of time
Support might approve, deny, or partially approve an increase request

sources.title: Requesting a quota increase
supports: Smaller increases are usually approved automatically; larger requests go to Support and take time to review, process, approve and deploy
Quota increase requests do not receive priority support
aws service-quotas list-service-quotas --service-code <code> prints QuotaName, QuotaCode, Value and Adjustable for each quota
aws service-quotas request-service-quota-increase takes --service-code, --quota-code and --desired-value, and answers with a Status of PENDING
Requesting through the CLI needs permission to create a service-linked role (ServiceQuotasFullAccess or iam:CreateServiceLinkedRole)

sources.title: Lambda quotas
supports: Concurrent executions: default 1,000 per Region, can be increased up to tens of thousands
New AWS accounts have reduced concurrency and memory quotas; AWS raises them automatically based on usage
Function timeout is 900 seconds; the synchronous invocation payload is 6 MB each for request and response; these cannot be changed
Each instance of an execution environment can serve up to 10 requests per second, so the invocation limit is 10 times the concurrency
API Gateway's default throttle of 10,000 requests per second and Lambda's default concurrency of 1,000 do not match; the page recommends load testing to find the quota that limits first
Service quotas consist of hard limits, which cannot be changed, and soft limits, for which an increase can be requested

sources.title: Configuring reserved concurrency for a function
supports: Reserved concurrency is both the maximum and the minimum for a function: no other function can use it, and the function cannot scale past it
Configuring reserved concurrency incurs no additional charge
You can reserve up to the unreserved account concurrency minus 100; the remaining 100 are for functions without reserved concurrency
Setting reserved concurrency to 0 stops the function from processing any events
Concurrency = average requests per second x average request duration in seconds

sources.title: Lambda scaling behavior
supports: For each function in each Region, concurrency can grow by 1,000 execution environments every 10 seconds
Requests that arrive faster than the function can scale, or while it is at maximum concurrency, fail with a throttling error (429 status code)

sources.title: Throttle requests to your HTTP APIs for better throughput in API Gateway
supports: API Gateway throttles with the token bucket algorithm, where a token counts for a request
Throttles are applied on a best-effort basis and should be thought of as targets rather than guaranteed request ceilings
Past the rate and burst limits, clients may receive 429 Too Many Requests
Account-level limits apply to all APIs of the account in a Region; stage and route limits cannot exceed them
Route-level throttling is set with RouteSettings keyed by the route key, with ThrottlingBurstLimit and ThrottlingRateLimit
sources.note: The page does not show the body of a 429 or say whether it carries a Retry-After header.

sources.title: Quotas for configuring and running an HTTP API in API Gateway
supports: Maximum integration timeout: 30 seconds, cannot be increased
Payload size: 10 MB, cannot be increased
Routes per API: 300, can be increased (quota code L-65B5C802)

sources.title: Amazon API Gateway quotas
supports: Throttle quota per account, per Region, across HTTP, REST and WebSocket APIs: 10,000 requests per second with a bucket of 5,000; can be increased (quota code L-8A5B8E43)
The burst quota is set by the API Gateway team from the account's rate quota and cannot be requested separately
Thirteen named Regions default to 2,500 requests per second; Asia Pacific (Tokyo) is not among them

sources.title: Usage plans and API keys for REST APIs in API Gateway
supports: Usage plans and API keys are a REST API feature: they throttle and set a quota per API key
Usage plan throttling and quotas are not hard limits and are applied on a best-effort basis; AWS says not to rely on them to control costs or block access
API keys are not to be used for authentication or authorization

sources.title: Quotas in Amazon DynamoDB
supports: On-demand tables: 40,000 read request units and 40,000 write request units per second per table by default, adjustable; no account-level throughput quota applies to on-demand tables
The listed values are initial defaults, not maximums

sources.title: Error handling with DynamoDB
supports: ProvisionedThroughputExceededException, RequestLimitExceeded and ThrottlingException are HTTP 400 errors that are OK to retry
For on-demand tables ThrottlingException can be returned for any data plane operation; the error carries ThrottlingReason fields such as IndexWriteMaxOnDemandThroughputExceeded
After a 500 on a single-item write the write may or may not have happened; the application should read the item or use a condition before retrying
The page recommends stopping retries after about a minute

sources.title: Retry behavior (AWS SDKs and Tools Reference Guide)
supports: The page describes a retry behaviour that needs AWS_NEW_RETRIES_2026=true until it becomes the default
Retry modes: standard (default), adaptive (adds a client-side rate limiter that can delay first attempts; not recommended as a general default), legacy (not available in JavaScript)
Max attempts defaults to 3 including the first; DynamoDB clients default to 4 under the described behaviour
delay = random(0, 1) x min(20,000 ms, base x 2^retry); base is 50 ms for transient errors and 1,000 ms for throttling errors
Retry quota: 500 tokens, 14 per transient retry, 5 per throttling retry, 1 restored by a first-try success; typically scoped to one client instance
With 3 attempts the quota starts to drain above roughly 22% sustained transient failures or 32% throttling
Full jitter spreads retries so that clients that failed together do not retry together
sources.note: Read again for chapter 32. The installed @smithy/util-retry 4.6.2 uses the older numbers (100 ms / 500 ms bases, costs 5 and 10) unless the variable is set; see limits-smithy-util-retry.

sources.title: @smithy/util-retry 4.6.2 (installed package, with @smithy/core 3.35.2)
supports: DEFAULT_MAX_ATTEMPTS is 3 and DEFAULT_RETRY_MODE is standard
Without the opt-in: base delay 100 ms, throttling base delay 500 ms, maximum delay 20 s, 500 retry tokens, 5 per throttling retry, 10 per transient retry, 1 restored by a success without retry
The backoff is Math.floor(Math.random() x min(base x 2^i, 20,000))
ProvisionedThroughputExceededException, ThrottlingException, RequestLimitExceeded and TooManyRequestsException are classified as throttling errors
@aws-sdk/core 3.978.2 turns the 2026 behaviour on when AWS_NEW_RETRIES_2026 is "true"; the DynamoDB client then defaults to 4 attempts
sources.note: Read in node_modules, not on the web page: @smithy/core/dist-es/submodules/retry and @aws-sdk/client-dynamodb/dist-es/runtimeConfig.js. A test compares the constants.

sources.title: Timeouts, retries, and backoff with jitter (Amazon Builders' Library)
supports: Retries are selfish: they spend more of the server's capacity to improve one client's odds, and make an overload worse
Retries at every layer multiply: five layers with three retries each can raise load on the bottom layer 243 times
Retries can be limited locally with a token bucket; the AWS SDK adopted this in 2016
A call with side effects is safe to retry only if the API is idempotent
sources.note: aws.amazon.com/builders-library/timeouts-retries-and-backoff-with-jitter/ redirects here. Read through a summary of the page, not word for word.

sources.title: Exponential Backoff And Jitter (AWS Architecture Blog)
supports: Backoff without jitter takes more work and more time than any jittered variant
Full jitter needs the least work among the variants compared
sources.note: The formulas are in images on the page and were not read. The full-jitter formula in this chapter is the one in the SDK reference and the installed package.

sources.title: Amazon EC2 Testing Policy
supports: The guidelines concern high volume network tests run from EC2 instances; a network stress test sends a large volume of legitimate or test traffic to a specific intended target application that is expected to handle it
Tests that purposefully attempt to overwhelm the target with floods are DDoS tests, and volumetric network-based DDoS simulations are prohibited from EC2
Endpoints hosted in AWS should be in the same Region as the test
AWS may shape traffic where surges exceed 25 Gbps or 100 Gbps, depending on the paths and Regions
sources.note: The page states no request-rate threshold and no approval step for a stress test. It says nothing about tests sent from outside AWS.

sources.title: AWS Customer Support Policy for Penetration Testing
supports: Security assessments of the listed services need no prior approval; API Gateway, Lambda and CloudFront are on the list
Prohibited: DoS and DDoS, simulated or not, port flooding, protocol flooding, and request flooding (login request flooding, API request flooding)

Network stress testing or load testing is a performance test that sends a large volume of legitimate or test traffic to a specific intended target application; the page sends readers to the stress test policy

sources.title: Organizing and tracking costs using AWS cost allocation tags
supports: User-defined and AWS-generated tags must each be activated before they appear in Cost Explorer or a cost allocation report
Only the management account of an organization, or a single account that is not a member, can manage cost allocation tags
The report includes both tagged and untagged resources

sources.title: Activating user-defined cost allocation tags
supports: Activation is done per tag key in the Billing and Cost Management console under Cost allocation tags, or with the UpdateCostAllocationTagsStatus API
It can take up to 24 hours for a new tag key to appear for activation, and up to 24 hours more for it to activate

sources.title: Using user-defined cost allocation tags
supports: Tags are not applied to resources that were created before the tags were created
User-defined tag names carry the prefix user: in the cost allocation report
How cost allocation tags behave varies across services

sources.title: GetCostAndUsage (AWS Billing and Cost Management API Reference)
supports: GroupBy takes up to two groups, of type DIMENSION, TAG, COST_CATEGORY or PRODUCT_ATTRIBUTE; grouping by TAG returns all tag values, including empty strings
The sample response shows a tag group key in the form key$value (Environment$Prod)
TimePeriod's start is inclusive and its end exclusive; Granularity is DAILY, MONTHLY or HOURLY
Amounts are returned as strings; the sample request is sent to ce.us-east-1.amazonaws.com
LimitExceededException: too many calls in a short period of time

sources.title: AWS Cost Explorer pricing
supports: Each API request using the primary billing view costs USD 0.01
Hourly granularity is charged per usage record

sources.title: AWS Budgets pricing
supports: Monitoring budgets and receiving notifications is free of charge
The first two action-enabled budgets a month are free; each further one costs USD 0.10 a day

sources.title: AWS::Budgets::Budget BudgetData
supports: BudgetType COST and TimeUnit MONTHLY are allowed values; BudgetLimit is required for a cost budget
FilterExpression is a property of type Expression, with no description on the page; CostFilters is JSON and lists Tag among its filters
sources.note: The page does not say how a tag key is written in FilterExpression. aws-cdk-lib 2.273.0 types it as tags: { key, values, matchOptions }.

The Budgets provider's comment says the API is global and served from us-east-1

Usage type ActionEnabledBudgetsUsage: USD 0.00 up to 62 budget-days, then USD 0.10 per budget-day

sources.title: Cloudflare Workers: Limits
supports: As of 2026-10-12: the Free plan allows 100,000 requests a day and answers with error 1027 past that; the Paid plan has no daily limit
The page states no general limit on requests per second for Workers
Limits such as the number of Workers per account can be raised through a limit increase request form

sources.title: Cloudflare Workers: Rate Limiting binding
supports: As of 2026-10-12: a binding with a limit and a period of 10 or 60 seconds, enforced from Worker code with limit()
Limits are local to the Cloudflare location the Worker runs in
The API is described as permissive, eventually consistent, and not an accurate accounting system

sources.title: Vercel: Limits
supports: As of 2026-10-12 (page last updated 2026-09-16): limits depend on the plan (Hobby, Pro, Enterprise); Enterprise raises them through the account team, Pro by talking to sales, Hobby by upgrading
REST API rate limits are hard limits with a scope of user, team or project; a request over a limit gets a 429 with rate_limit_exceeded

sources.title: Vercel: Spend Management
supports: As of 2026-10-12 (page last updated 2026-09-18): on Pro and Enterprise Flexible Commitment plans, a spend amount can notify at 50%, 75% and 100%, call a webhook, and pause the production deployments of all projects
Setting an amount does not stop usage by itself; pausing must be turned on
Usage is checked every few minutes, so pausing can come several minutes after the amount is crossed; paused deployments answer 503 DEPLOYMENT_PAUSED and must be resumed by hand

sources.title: AWS Well-Architected Framework: The pillars of the framework
supports: The framework has six pillars: operational excellence, security, reliability, performance efficiency, cost optimization, and sustainability

sources.title: Operational Readiness Reviews (ORR)
supports: AWS created the Operational Readiness Review to distill the learnings from its operational incidents into curated questions with best practice guidance
An ORR program can supplement Well-Architected reviews with lessons specific to your business, culture, tools, and governance rules
sources.note: Publication date on the page: June 30, 2022. Only the abstract and introduction were read.

sources.title: OPS07-BP02 Ensure a consistent review of operational readiness
supports: An ORR is a review and inspection process using a checklist of requirements, run before a workload launches and then throughout its lifecycle
Your own post-incident analysis should drive the evolution of your own ORR

sources.title: OPS07-BP03 Use runbooks to perform procedures
supports: A runbook is a documented process to achieve a specific outcome; at its simplest, a checklist to complete a task

sources.title: OPS06-BP01 Plan for unsuccessful changes
supports: Plan to revert to a known good state, or remediate in production, if a deployment causes an undesired outcome

sources.title: OPS06-BP03 Employ safe deployment strategies
supports: Safe roll-outs may include feature flags, one-box, rolling (canary releases), immutable, traffic splitting, and blue/green deployments

sources.title: OPS10-BP02 Have a process per alert
supports: Every alert initiates a specific, well-defined response plan, with clear ownership and a defined escalation path

sources.title: OPS11-BP02 Perform post-incident analysis
supports: Review customer-impacting events, identify the contributing factors and preventative actions, and use them to limit or prevent recurrence

sources.title: SEC01-BP01 Separate workloads using accounts
supports: Account-level separation is strongly recommended, as it provides a strong isolation boundary for security, billing, and access

sources.title: SEC03-BP02 Grant least privilege access
supports: Grant only the access that users require to perform specific actions on specific resources under specific conditions
Developers are given limited and controlled access to production only for the duration of a task

sources.title: REL01-BP01 Aware of service quotas and constraints
supports: Anti-patterns include deploying a workload without understanding its quotas, and assuming that quotas will be increased automatically

sources.title: REL09-BP04 Perform periodic recovery of the data to verify backup integrity and processes
supports: Validate that the backup process meets the RTO and RPO by performing a recovery test
Anti-patterns include assuming that a backup exists, and restoring a backup without querying any data to check that it is usable

sources.title: REL12-BP05 Conduct game days regularly
supports: Game days exercise the procedures for responding to workload-impacting events, with the same teams who would handle production scenarios

sources.title: REL13-BP01 Define recovery objectives for downtime and data loss
supports: RTO is the maximum acceptable delay between the interruption of service and its restoration; RPO is the maximum acceptable time after the last data recovery point
Anti-patterns include arbitrary objectives and unrealistic ones such as zero time to recover

sources.title: COST01-BP03 Establish cloud budgets and forecasts
supports: Budgeting and forecasting have to follow cloud costs that vary monthly, daily, or hourly

sources.title: Organizing Your AWS Environment Using Multiple Accounts
supports: AWS describes a multi-account strategy as part of the foundation of an AWS environment
sources.note: Publication date on the page: April 30, 2025. Only the abstract was read; the recommended OU structure is not quoted in the chapter.

sources.title: DeletionPolicy attribute
supports: If a resource has no DeletionPolicy attribute, CloudFormation deletes the resource by default
The default is Snapshot for AWS::RDS::DBCluster, and for AWS::RDS::DBInstance resources that don't specify DBClusterIdentifier
The options are Delete, Retain, RetainExceptOnCreate, and Snapshot
A retained resource continues to exist and to incur charges after the stack is deleted

sources.title: UpdateReplacePolicy attribute
supports: When an update replaces a resource, CloudFormation creates the replacement first and by default then deletes the old resource
UpdateReplacePolicy can retain, or for some types snapshot, the old resource

sources.title: AWS::Logs::LogGroup
supports: To set a log group so that its log events do not expire, do not specify RetentionInDays
The allowed values of RetentionInDays, 90 among them

sources.title: AWS::S3::Bucket PublicAccessBlockConfiguration
supports: The four Boolean properties BlockPublicAcls, BlockPublicPolicy, IgnorePublicAcls, and RestrictPublicBuckets, none of them required
Bucket-level settings work alongside account-level settings

sources.title: AWS::DynamoDB::Table
supports: DeletionProtectionEnabled is disabled by default; when enabled, the table cannot be deleted by any user or process
PointInTimeRecoverySpecification is not required

sources.title: AWS::DynamoDB::Table PointInTimeRecoverySpecification
supports: PointInTimeRecoveryEnabled is a Boolean; RecoveryPeriodInDays is 1 to 35 and defaults to 35

sources.title: AWS::CloudWatch::Alarm
supports: AlarmActions is the list of actions to execute when the alarm transitions into ALARM; it is not required
ActionsEnabled defaults to TRUE
An alarm on a math expression uses Metrics and cannot specify Dimensions

sources.title: Configuring CloudWatch log groups (Lambda)
supports: By default a log group named /aws/lambda/<function name> is created automatically when the function is first invoked
A function can be configured to send its logs to an existing log group

supports: The list includes dynamodb-pitr-enabled, cw-loggroup-retention-period-check, s3-bucket-level-public-access-prohibited, lambda-dlq-check, and iam-policy-no-statements-with-admin-access

None of the 27 products in the offer file mentions deletion protection

sources.title: Vercel: Production checklist for launch
supports: Vercel publishes a production checklist grouped as operational excellence, security, reliability, performance efficiency, and cost optimization
Its items include an incident response plan with rollback strategies, the Vercel WAF, rate limiting, access roles, Log Drains to persist logs, and Spend Management
Several items are marked Enterprise only, among them audit logs, automatic function failover, and running a load test

sources.title: Amazon EKS architecture
supports: Every cluster has its own Kubernetes control plane, not shared with other clusters or accounts
The control plane has at least two API server instances and three etcd instances across three Availability Zones
EKS replaces a control plane instance that fails

sources.title: Automate cluster infrastructure with EKS Auto Mode
supports: Auto Mode manages compute autoscaling, pod and service networking, application load balancing, cluster DNS, and block storage as core components instead of add-ons
Nodes are EC2 managed instances running Bottlerocket variants; SSH and SSM access to them is not allowed
Nodes have a maximum lifetime of 21 days, which can be reduced
Upgrades respect Pod Disruption Budgets; intervention might be required if a blocking budget prevents an update
The EKS Pod Identity Agent does not have to be installed on Auto Mode clusters
Auto scaling relies on Karpenter
Since April 22, 2026 new managed instances are hidden by default from EC2 console views and list APIs

sources.title: Create a Node Pool for EKS Auto Mode
supports: The built-in system and general-purpose node pools cannot be modified, only enabled or disabled
A cluster can be created with nodePools and nodeRoleArn both empty; then no default NodeClass exists, and a custom NodeClass, an access entry for its role, and a custom NodePool are needed
A NodePool is a karpenter.sh/v1 object whose nodeClassRef names group eks.amazonaws.com, kind NodeClass
Supported requirement labels include kubernetes.io/arch, karpenter.sh/capacity-type, and node.kubernetes.io/instance-type
By default Auto Mode consolidates underutilized instances, terminates instances after 336 hours, and sets one disruption budget of 10% of nodes
limits.cpu and limits.memory bound what a node pool may provision

sources.title: Enable or Disable Built-in NodePools
supports: general-purpose uses only the amd64 architecture; system supports amd64 and arm64 and carries a CriticalAddonsOnly taint
Both built-in pools use on-demand capacity, the C, M, and R families, and generation 5 or newer
At least one built-in pool must be enabled for EKS to provision the default NodeClass

sources.title: Create a Node Class for Amazon EKS
supports: A NodeClass is an eks.amazonaws.com/v1 object with role, subnetSelectorTerms, securityGroupSelectorTerms, ephemeralStorage, and advancedNetworking
advancedNetworking.associatePublicIPAddress controls whether instances get a public IP address; unset, it follows the subnet's MapPublicIpOnLaunch
A custom node class needs an access entry of type EC2 with the AmazonEKSAutoNodePolicy access policy, or its nodes cannot join; the page gives the CloudFormation for it
subnetSelectorTerms and securityGroupSelectorTerms select by tags or by id; nodes are distributed across the matching subnets
ephemeralStorage.size accepts 1 to 59000Gi; the specification example shows 80Gi, iops 3000 and throughput 125

sources.title: Create an IngressClass to configure an Application Load Balancer
supports: An IngressClass with controller eks.amazonaws.com/alb and an IngressClassParams (eks.amazonaws.com/v1) make Auto Mode create an ALB for an Ingress
IngressClassParams fields include scheme, subnets.ids, and subnets.matchTags (filters with a key and a list of values); targetType defaults to ip
IngressClass annotations cannot configure the load balancer; annotations on individual Ingress resources can
The page lists the Ingress annotations that are not supported; the health check and target group attribute annotations are not on that list
Deleting the Ingress makes Auto Mode delete the load balancer
The page does not mention the Gateway API
sources.note: Whether each health check annotation of the open source controller takes effect under Auto Mode was not confirmed beyond its absence from the unsupported list.

sources.title: Learn about VPC Networking and Load Balancing in EKS Auto Mode
supports: Auto Mode supports nodes and pods in public or private subnets
Security groups per pod and alternate CNI plugins are not supported
CoreDNS runs as a system service on each node, not as a Deployment
The default target mode of load balancers is IP
The EKS managed policy only lets EKS modify security groups named eks-cluster-sg-*; nodes with other security groups need extra permissions on the cluster role

sources.title: Tag subnets for EKS Auto Mode
supports: Subnets used for load balancing by Auto Mode need the tag kubernetes.io/role/elb (public) or kubernetes.io/role/internal-elb (private)

sources.title: Learn about Amazon EKS Auto Mode Managed instances
supports: Auto Mode supports the t4g family among others
Auto Mode only creates instances with more than 1 CPU whose size is not nano, micro, or small
EKS generally releases a new AMI each week
IMDSv2 with a hop limit of 1 is enforced and cannot be changed

sources.title: Amazon EKS Auto Mode cluster IAM role
supports: The suggested managed policies are AmazonEKSClusterPolicy, AmazonEKSComputePolicy, AmazonEKSBlockStoragePolicyV2, AmazonEKSLoadBalancingPolicy, and AmazonEKSNetworkingPolicy
The trust policy allows sts:AssumeRole and sts:TagSession for eks.amazonaws.com

sources.title: Amazon EKS Auto Mode node IAM role
supports: The node role trusts ec2.amazonaws.com and carries AmazonEKSWorkerNodeMinimalPolicy and AmazonEC2ContainerRegistryPullOnly

sources.title: Create an EKS Auto Mode Cluster with the AWS CLI
supports: The create-cluster request enables computeConfig, kubernetesNetworkConfig.elasticLoadBalancing, and storageConfig.blockStorage, and sets accessConfig.authenticationMode to API
The example enables both the public and the private endpoint
sources.note: The page's request does not set bootstrapSelfManagedAddons. aws-cdk-lib 2.273.0 refuses true with Auto Mode (see aws-cdk-lib-eks); what happens when it is omitted was not confirmed.

sources.title: Enable EKS Auto Mode on an existing cluster
supports: The compute, block storage, and load balancing capabilities must all be enabled or disabled in the same request

sources.title: Update the Kubernetes Version of an EKS Auto Mode cluster
supports: After a control plane upgrade Auto Mode replaces nodes as they expire, with nodes of the new version, observing pod disruption budgets
The VPC CNI, the load balancer controller, CoreDNS, kube-proxy, Karpenter, and the EBS CSI driver no longer need updating by the user

sources.title: Manage compute resources by using nodes
supports: With managed node groups you must deploy and manage EC2 instances, patch the operating system, and update the node AMI and Kubernetes version yourself; with Auto Mode you do not
Auto Mode nodes cannot be reached by SSH, cannot run a custom AMI or CNI, and cannot run Windows containers
Auto Mode charges a separate fee on top of the EC2 instance price

sources.title: Simplify compute management with AWS Fargate
supports: Pods on Fargate run only in private subnets with NAT gateway access
DaemonSets, privileged containers, and GPUs are not supported on Fargate
The comparison table says Fargate cannot run workloads that require Arm processors

sources.title: Learn how EKS Pod Identity grants pods access to AWS services
supports: An association maps an IAM role to a service account in a namespace of a cluster
The role's trust policy names the service principal pods.eks.amazonaws.com; no OIDC provider is involved
EKS sets environment variables in the pod's containers so that the AWS SDKs use the Pod Identity credentials
Up to 5,000 associations per cluster
Associations are eventually consistent, with delays of several seconds
Pod Identity is not available for pods on Fargate or on Windows instances
Containers are not a security boundary; pods on the same node share a kernel

sources.title: Assign an IAM role to a Kubernetes service account
supports: The trust policy allows sts:AssumeRole and sts:TagSession
The namespace and the service account of an association may be named before they exist in the cluster

sources.title: Understand how EKS Pod Identity works
supports: The pod gets AWS_CONTAINER_CREDENTIALS_FULL_URI pointing at http://169.254.170.23/v1/credentials and AWS_CONTAINER_AUTHORIZATION_TOKEN_FILE

sources.title: Grant Kubernetes workloads access to AWS using Kubernetes Service Accounts
supports: AWS recommends EKS Pod Identity over IRSA whenever possible
IRSA needs an IAM OIDC provider per cluster (default limit of 100 per account) and the cluster's provider in each role's trust policy
With IRSA the SDK in the pod calls sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity itself
IRSA also works outside EKS (EKS Anywhere, OpenShift on AWS, self-managed clusters); Pod Identity is EKS only

sources.title: Grant IAM users access to Kubernetes with EKS access entries
supports: An access entry associates Kubernetes permissions with an IAM identity, through an access policy or a Kubernetes group
Access is managed through the EKS API, and can be restored there without access to the Kubernetes API

sources.title: Review access policy permissions
supports: AmazonEKSClusterAdminPolicy allows every verb on every resource
AmazonEKSEditPolicy allows create, delete, patch, and update on deployments, services, service accounts, ingresses, and pod disruption budgets, and only read access to namespaces
AmazonEKSAutoNodePolicy exists for Auto Mode nodes

sources.title: Understand the Kubernetes version lifecycle on EKS
supports: A minor version is in standard support for 14 months after its release on EKS, then in extended support for 12 months
Extended support is enabled by default; at its end the cluster is auto-upgraded to the oldest version still in extended support
On 2026-10-13 standard support covered 1.37, 1.36, 1.35, and 1.34; extended support covered 1.33, 1.32, and 1.31
The release calendar: 1.37 leaves standard support on December 1, 2027; 1.34 on December 2, 2026
A cluster upgraded in place can be rolled back to the previous minor version within 7 days
Billing for extended support starts at the beginning of the day (UTC) that standard support ends

sources.title: Prevent increased cluster costs by disabling EKS extended support
supports: With the upgrade policy STANDARD the cluster is automatically upgraded to the next version at the end of standard support
Extended support cannot be disabled once the cluster has entered it

sources.title: Update existing cluster to new Kubernetes version
supports: A cluster is updated one minor version at a time
An update needs up to five available IP addresses in the cluster's subnets
kubectl must be within one minor version of the control plane
After the 7-day window a cluster cannot be downgraded

sources.title: Delete a cluster
supports: Ingress resources should be deleted before the cluster; otherwise the Application Load Balancer remains after the cluster is deleted
For Auto Mode the page says that all nodes and all load balancers will be deleted with the cluster
Deletion protection must be disabled before a cluster can be deleted
sources.note: The two statements about load balancers stand side by side on the page. This chapter deletes the Ingress first.

sources.title: Route internet traffic with AWS Load Balancer Controller
supports: Outside Auto Mode the controller is installed into the cluster, with Helm for example
From version 2.14.0 the controller creates an ALB for a Kubernetes Gateway

sources.title: Simplify node lifecycle with managed node groups
supports: Every managed node is part of an EC2 Auto Scaling group that EKS manages, in your account
Managed node groups are tagged for discovery by the Kubernetes Cluster Autoscaler

sources.title: Set up the Amazon EKS Pod Identity Agent
supports: Outside Auto Mode the Pod Identity Agent is installed as an EKS add-on

sources.title: Assign IAM roles to Kubernetes service accounts
supports: With IRSA the service account is annotated with eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn

sources.title: Roll back a cluster to a previous Kubernetes version
supports: A rollback must be started within 7 days of the upgrade completing

sources.title: Connect kubectl to an EKS cluster by creating a kubeconfig file
supports: aws eks update-kubeconfig --region ... --name ... writes the kubeconfig entry; authentication uses aws eks get-token

sources.title: Set up kubectl and eksctl
supports: kubectl must be within one minor version of the cluster's control plane

sources.title: Troubleshoot EKS Auto Mode
supports: kubectl get nodeclaim and kubectl describe nodeclaim show why a node has not joined the cluster

sources.title: kubectl apply
supports: kubectl apply takes a configuration by file name or stdin; the examples include applying JSON passed into stdin

sources.title: kubectl diff
supports: kubectl diff shows the difference between the live configuration and the one that would be applied

sources.title: Amazon EKS pricing
supports: USD 0.10 per cluster per hour in standard support; USD 0.60 per cluster per hour in extended support, which includes the 0.10
Auto Mode charges are in addition to the EC2 instance price, per second with a one-minute minimum, and independent of the EC2 purchase option
Worker nodes' EC2 instances, EBS volumes, and public IPv4 addresses are billed on top

sources.title: Amazon ECS pricing
supports: There is no additional charge for Amazon ECS orchestration
