sources.title: Kubernetes: Deployments
supports: maxUnavailable is calculated from a percentage by rounding down, maxSurge by rounding up; both default to 25%
maxUnavailable cannot be 0 if maxSurge is 0, and the reverse
progressDeadlineSeconds defaults to 600; Kubernetes takes no action on a stalled Deployment other than to report a status condition
minReadySeconds is how long a new pod must be ready before it counts as available

sources.title: Kubernetes: Specifying a Disruption Budget for your Application
supports: A budget has a selector and exactly one of minAvailable and maxUnavailable, each a number or a percentage
A minAvailable percentage rounds up; a maxUnavailable percentage rounds up the number of pods that may be disrupted
A budget does not guarantee the number of pods: a node may still fail

sources.title: Kubernetes: Disruptions
supports: Draining a node is a voluntary disruption and goes through the eviction API, which respects budgets; deleting pods or deployments directly bypasses them
Pods unavailable because of a rolling upgrade count against the budget, but a Deployment is not limited by budgets when it rolls
Involuntary disruptions cannot be prevented by a budget, but count against it
The AlwaysAllow unhealthy pod eviction policy is recommended so that a misbehaving application cannot block a drain

sources.title: Kubernetes: API-initiated Eviction
supports: An eviction the budget does not allow is answered with 429 Too Many Requests

sources.title: Kubernetes: Pod Lifecycle
supports: The grace period defaults to 30 seconds; a preStop hook runs first and its time counts against the grace period
The kubelet sends TERM to process 1 of each container, and KILL when the grace period has expired
At the same time as the kubelet starts the graceful shutdown, the control plane removes the pod from EndpointSlices

sources.title: Kubernetes: Container Lifecycle Hooks
supports: Hook handlers are Exec, HTTP, and Sleep; Sleep pauses the container for a given duration and is run by the kubelet

sources.title: Kubernetes: Pod Topology Spread Constraints

sources.title: Lambda Managed Instances
supports: Lambda Managed Instances runs Lambda functions on current-generation EC2 instances in your account without you managing instance lifecycles, OS and runtime patching, routing, load balancing, or scaling policies
Capacity providers are the foundation: create a capacity provider, create a function attached to it, publish a function version
When a function version is published with a capacity provider, Lambda launches three instances by default for AZ resiliency and starts three execution environments before marking the version ACTIVE
One execution environment handles multiple invocations at the same time; Lambda (default) runs at most one invocation per execution environment
Managed Instances use containers on EC2 Nitro instances for isolation rather than Firecracker; the capacity provider is the security boundary

The instances are EC2 managed instances: the Operator field appears in DescribeInstances, they carry the aws:lambda:capacity-provider tag, they cannot be terminated directly, and they are hidden from the EC2 console and list operations by default while remaining billable
Pricing is EC2-based with a 15% management fee on top of the EC2 instance cost; EC2 Savings Plans, Reserved Instances and other EC2 discounts apply to the EC2 compute only, not to the management fee

Lambda Managed Instances scales asynchronously on CPU resource utilization, without cold starts, and scales to the configured minimum of execution environments without traffic; Lambda (default) scales to zero
By default Managed Instances scale to handle traffic doubling within five minutes

sources.title: Core concepts
supports: All functions assigned to the same capacity provider must be mutually trusted
If traffic more than doubles within 5 minutes, throttles may occur while Lambda scales up
Users need lambda:PassCapacityProvider to assign functions to a capacity provider

sources.title: Capacity providers
supports: A capacity provider takes a VPC configuration (1 to 16 subnets, security groups), an operator role, and optionally instance requirements and a scaling configuration
Architectures is x86_64 or arm64, default x86_64; AllowedInstanceTypes and ExcludedInstanceTypes are mutually exclusive
Lambda chooses instance types by default, and restricting them might result in lower availability
MaxVCpuCount defaults to 400; ScalingMode is Auto or Manual
KmsKeyArn is a KMS key for EBS encryption, defaulting to an AWS managed key
A capacity provider that has function versions attached cannot be deleted
States: Pending, Active, Failed, Deleting

sources.title: Scaling Lambda Managed Instances
supports: Managed Instances does not scale when invocations arrive and does not support cold starts; it scales asynchronously on CPU utilization and multi-concurrency saturation
The smallest supported function size is 2 GB and 1 vCPU
Maximum concurrency per execution environment can be raised to 64 per vCPU
The default minimum is 3 execution environments across Availability Zones with no default maximum; values below 3 reduce Availability Zone redundancy
MinExecutionEnvironments and MaxExecutionEnvironments range from 0 to 15000 and are set together; a minimum of 0 is valid only when the maximum is also 0, which deactivates the function version
A deactivated function does not scale back up with traffic; Lambda terminates an instance once it has no active execution environments, and instance charges continue until termination completes
The Router and Scaler are shared Lambda components; a Lambda Agent runs on each instance
The default target keeps enough headroom for traffic to double within 5 minutes without throttles
For testing or development you might choose smaller instance types

sources.title: Lambda Managed Instances runtimes
supports: Supported: Java 21 and later, Python 3.13 and later, Node.js 22 and later, .NET 8 and later, and Rust on the OS-only runtime provided.al2023 and later
Node.js uses worker threads with asynchronous execution; Python uses one process per concurrent request; Java uses OS threads

sources.title: Node.js runtime for Lambda Managed Instances
supports: Function initialization occurs once per worker thread; concurrent requests on the same worker thread share the handler object and global state
For Node.js the default maximum is 64 concurrent requests per vCPU; the number of worker threads follows the vCPU count or AWS_LAMBDA_NODEJS_WORKER_COUNT
For mutable objects, avoid global state or use AsyncLocalStorage; AWS SDK clients are async safe
On Node.js 22, callback-based handlers cannot be used with Managed Instances
/tmp is shared across all concurrent requests in the execution environment
Functions on Managed Instances always use the structured JSON log format, which carries the requestId
context.awsRequestId and context.xRayTraceId are async-safe; the _X_AMZN_TRACE_ID environment variable is not supported
process.on() cannot be used with worker threads, so a function cannot subscribe to SIGTERM
Minimum versions: AWS SDK for JavaScript v3 3.933.0, Powertools for AWS Lambda (TypeScript) 2.29.0

sources.title: Networking for Lambda Managed Instances
supports: Connectivity is needed for functions to reach resources outside the VPC and for transmitting telemetry to CloudWatch Logs and X-Ray
Three options: public subnet with an internet gateway, VPC endpoints, private subnet with a NAT gateway
VPC endpoints are recommended for production with strict security requirements and are billed per endpoint, per Availability Zone, and per GB

sources.title: Security and permissions
supports: Containers are not a security boundary between functions on a capacity provider
lambda:PassCapacityProvider is required when creating or updating functions that use a capacity provider, including through infrastructure as code
Lambda uses the AWSServiceRoleForLambda service-linked role to manage the EC2 resources of capacity providers

sources.title: Lambda operator role for Lambda Managed Instances
supports: Lambda assumes the operator role to manage EC2 instances in the capacity provider; its trust policy names lambda.amazonaws.com

The role needs at least the AWSLambdaManagedEC2ResourceOperator managed policy; the page prints its statements (ec2:RunInstances, ec2:CreateTags, ec2:AttachNetworkInterface, ec2:CreateNetworkInterface, several ec2:Describe*, logs:CreateLogGroup, logs:CreateLogStream, logs:PutLogEvents)
The service-linked role is created with the first capacity provider, needs iam:CreateServiceLinkedRole for lambda.amazonaws.com, and holds ec2:TerminateInstances and ec2:DescribeInstances

sources.title: Lambda Managed Instances quotas
supports: 1,000 capacity providers per account; 100 function versions per capacity provider (cannot be increased); 15,000 vCPUs per capacity provider
Capacity provider APIs: 15 read requests and 1 write request per second, not adjustable
EC2 quotas apply as well: vCPU limits, EBS volume limits, and free IP addresses in the subnets
Event source mappings on Managed Instances support SQS, DynamoDB Streams, Kinesis Data Streams, Amazon MSK, and self-managed Apache Kafka

sources.title: Understanding the Lambda Managed Instances execution environment
supports: The execution environment stays active between invocations instead of being frozen
The configured timeout applies to each invocation; when one times out Lambda reports it failed but does not stop the code, which keeps running and keeps a runtime worker busy
If all runtime workers are busy, new invocations are rejected until one is free
Initialization may take up to the larger of 130 seconds and the function timeout
Unhealthy containers are terminated and replaced rather than reset

sources.title: $LATEST.PUBLISHED version in Lambda Managed Instances
supports: An unqualified ARN of a Managed Instances function invokes $LATEST.PUBLISHED, not $LATEST
CloudFormation and the console create the $LATEST.PUBLISHED version automatically

sources.title: Getting started with Lambda Managed Instances
supports: A function is attached with --capacity-provider-config LambdaManagedInstancesCapacityProviderConfig={CapacityProviderArn=...}, and a version must be published before it runs
Cleanup deletes the function first, then the capacity provider
Function creation typically takes several minutes

sources.title: Troubleshooting Lambda Managed Instances
supports: Throttles are HTTP 429; the throttle reason metrics tell CPU, memory, disk and concurrency apart
Node.js state isolation issues: global variables are shared across concurrent invocations on the same worker thread
Missing logs are a VPC connectivity problem: the instances need a path to CloudWatch Logs, for example the com.amazonaws.<region>.logs interface endpoint with private DNS
A function version stays pending while Lambda launches three instances and starts three execution environments; this typically takes several minutes
Metrics are in the AWS/Lambda namespace with the dimensions CapacityProviderName, FunctionName, or InstanceType

sources.title: Lambda quotas
supports: On Managed Instances, asynchronous and event source mapping invocations may run up to 5,400 seconds (90 minutes); the general function timeout is 900 seconds
Managed Instances use a file descriptor limit of 4,096 and the process and thread limits of Bottlerocket

sources.title: Introducing AWS Lambda Managed Instances: Serverless simplicity with EC2 flexibility (AWS News Blog, 2025-11-30)
supports: At launch the feature was available in US East (N. Virginia), US East (Ohio), US West (Oregon), Asia Pacific (Tokyo), and Europe (Ireland)
New instances are launched within tens of seconds; by default a capacity provider absorbs spikes of up to 50% without scaling, and throttles with 429 beyond what is provisioned
Instances have a maximum lifetime of 14 days
sources.note: The blog says a 50% spike is absorbed without scaling; the developer guide says capacity is kept for traffic doubling within five minutes. The chapter quotes both and treats neither as measured.

sources.title: AWS Lambda pricing: Lambda Managed Instances

Compute Savings Plans, EC2 Instance Savings Plans and Reserved Instances reduce the EC2 instance charges
Functions on Managed Instances do not pay for the execution duration of each request
Worked example: 100 million requests, m7g.xlarge at USD 0.1632 per hour in us-east-1, a 3-year Compute Savings Plan at 72% off, about 2,000 instance-hours: 20 + 91.40 + 48.96 = USD 160.36

sources.title: Node.js v24: Asynchronous context tracking
supports: AsyncLocalStorage is stable; run(store, callback) makes the store available to everything called inside the callback, across asynchronous operations, and getStore() returns undefined outside of it

sources.title: Cloudflare Workers: How Workers works (last updated 2026-09-18)
supports: A single Workers instance may handle multiple requests, including concurrent requests, in a single-threaded event loop
Cloudflare recommends not using or mutating global state, because requests may or may not share an instance and an isolate may be evicted

sources.title: Vercel: Fluid compute (last updated 2026-08-24)

Fluid compute has been enabled by default for new projects since April 23, 2025
Multiple invocations can share the same physical instance (a global state/process) concurrently

sources.title: Use a tool to complete an Amazon Bedrock model response
supports: The model does not call a tool itself: the application (client-side) or Bedrock (server-side) runs it and returns the result
Three modes: client-side tool use (Responses, Chat Completions, Converse, InvokeModel), server-side tool use (currently the Responses API), Anthropic-defined tool types

sources.title: Client-side tool use
supports: With Converse the response has stopReason tool_use and toolUse blocks; the application appends the assistant message and a user message with toolResult blocks, with status error for a failed tool
toolUseId is generated by Bedrock for tools defined in toolConfig (prefix tooluse_), but for some models the provider's identifier is passed through

sources.title: Server-side tool use
supports: Server-side tool calling is available with the Responses API: Bedrock invokes a Lambda function that implements MCP

sources.title: Inference using Converse API
supports: ConverseStream event order: messageStart, per content block contentBlockStart (tool use only), contentBlockDelta (text, reasoning, or tool use partial JSON), contentBlockStop, then messageStop with stopReason, then metadata with usage and metrics
contentBlockIndex correlates the events of one content block
Request fields guardrailConfig, toolConfig, serviceTier, requestMetadata (key-value tags recorded in model invocation logs)
Converse needs bedrock:InvokeModel; ConverseStream needs bedrock:InvokeModelWithResponseStream

sources.title: ConverseStream (API reference)
supports: Request members toolConfig, guardrailConfig (GuardrailStreamConfiguration), outputConfig, requestMetadata, serviceTier

sources.title: MessageStopEvent
supports: stopReason values: end_turn, tool_use, max_tokens, stop_sequence, guardrail_intervened, content_filtered, malformed_model_output, malformed_tool_use, model_context_window_exceeded

sources.title: ToolSpecification, ToolUseBlock, ToolResultBlock, ToolChoice, ContentBlockStart/Delta (API reference)
supports: ToolSpecification: name ([a-zA-Z0-9_-]+, 1-64), description, inputSchema, strict
ToolUseBlockStart carries name and toolUseId; ToolUseBlockDelta carries input as a string
ToolResultBlock.status (success | error) is supported only by Amazon Nova and Anthropic Claude 3 and 4 models
ToolChoice: auto (default), any, tool (a named tool; only Anthropic Claude 3 and Amazon Nova models)
sources.note: Read together with API_runtime_ToolUseBlock, API_runtime_ToolUseBlockStart, API_runtime_ToolUseBlockDelta, API_runtime_ToolResultBlock, API_runtime_ToolChoice, API_runtime_ContentBlockDelta and API_runtime_ContentBlockStart on the same day.

sources.title: Get validated JSON results from models
supports: Two mechanisms: a JSON Schema output format (outputConfig.textFormat for Converse) and strict tool use (strict: true on a tool definition)

Supported subset of JSON Schema Draft 2020-12; not supported: recursive schemas, external $ref, minimum/maximum/multipleOf, minLength/maxLength, additionalProperties other than false; array minItems only 0 and 1
A new schema is compiled on first use, which may take up to a few minutes; compiled grammars are cached for 24 hours
Supported with Converse/ConverseStream, InvokeModel, cross-Region inference, and (according to this page) batch inference; model support is on each model card
Structured outputs are incompatible with citations for Anthropic models
sources.note: This page lists batch inference as supported. The batch inference overview page says batch does not support tool calling or structured output. The two pages disagree; the chapter says so.

sources.title: OutputConfig, OutputFormat, JsonSchemaDefinition (API reference)
supports: outputConfig.textFormat has type json_schema and structure.jsonSchema with schema (a string), name and description
sources.note: Read together with API_runtime_OutputFormat, API_runtime_OutputFormatStructure and API_runtime_JsonSchemaDefinition.

sources.title: Detect and filter harmful content by using Amazon Bedrock Guardrails
supports: Filters: content filters (Hate, Insults, Sexual, Violence, Misconduct, Prompt Attack), denied topics, word filters, sensitive information filters, contextual grounding checks, Automated Reasoning checks
A guardrail has a working draft and numbered versions; it is used by passing its ID and version on an inference call, or alone through ApplyGuardrail
Reasoning content blocks are not evaluated

sources.title: Include a guardrail with the Converse API
supports: guardrailConfig carries guardrailIdentifier, guardrailVersion, trace; ConverseStream adds streamProcessingMode
With tools, a guardrail does not evaluate toolResult content, tool definitions, or the toolUse input the model generates; it evaluates text and guardContent

When blocked: stopReason guardrail_intervened, the configured blocked message is returned as the output (in the streamed message for ConverseStream), the trace is in metadata, and the documented example shows zero tokens
Once any guardContent block is present, only guardContent blocks are evaluated; a system prompt is evaluated only inside guardContent

sources.title: Configure streaming response behavior to filter content
supports: Synchronous mode (default) buffers and scans chunks before they are sent, adding latency; asynchronous mode sends chunks immediately and blocks later chunks once a violation is found
Masking of sensitive information is not supported in asynchronous mode

sources.title: GuardrailStreamConfiguration (API reference)
supports: Members guardrailIdentifier, guardrailVersion (a number or DRAFT), streamProcessingMode (sync | async), trace (enabled | disabled | enabled_full)

sources.title: Set up permissions to use Amazon Bedrock Guardrails
supports: A role that invokes a model with a guardrail needs bedrock:ApplyGuardrail on arn:aws:bedrock:<region>:<account>:guardrail/<id> in addition to the InvokeModel permissions

sources.title: Supported Regions and models for Amazon Bedrock Guardrails
supports: Guardrails apply to InvokeModel, InvokeModelWithResponseStream, Converse and ConverseStream on bedrock-runtime; the bedrock-mantle endpoint does not support them
The page lists the models that do not support guardrails (embedding, rerank, speech and some others); Nova 2 Lite and Claude Haiku 4.5 are not on that list

sources.title: Safeguard tiers for guardrails policies
supports: Tiers apply to content filters (including prompt attacks) and denied topics
Classic tier supports English, French and Spanish; Standard tier has broader language support, prompt leakage detection, and uses cross-Region inference
Safeguard tiers are available in Asia Pacific (Tokyo) among other Regions

sources.title: Languages supported by Amazon Bedrock Guardrails
supports: Japanese is 'Optimized and supported' for content filters and prompt attacks and for denied topics in the Standard tier, and for sensitive information filters
Classic tier content filters and denied topics, word filters, and contextual grounding checks list English, French and Spanish only
Guardrails are ineffective with languages that are not supported

sources.title: Supported Regions for cross-Region guardrail inference
supports: Guardrail profile apac.guardrail.v1:0: from source ap-northeast-1 the destinations are ap-south-1, ap-northeast-3, ap-northeast-2, ap-southeast-1, ap-southeast-2 and ap-northeast-1
sources.note: Read with guardrails-cross-region.html (prompts and results may move outside the primary Region; the configuration stays in the primary Region) and guardrail-profiles-permissions.html (bedrock:ApplyGuardrail on the guardrail and on the guardrail profile in each destination Region).

sources.title: Remove PII from conversations by using sensitive information filters
supports: Block or mask (anonymize) modes; built-in entity types include EMAIL, PHONE, AWS_ACCESS_KEY and AWS_SECRET_KEY; custom regex patterns
The filter does not evaluate toolUse input, toolResult content, or tool definitions

sources.title: Detect prompt attacks with Amazon Bedrock Guardrails
supports: Prompt attack types: jailbreaks, prompt injection, and prompt leakage (Standard tier only); the filter is a content filter of type PROMPT_ATTACK configured with inputStrength

sources.title: Prompt injection security
supports: Preventing prompt injection is the customer's responsibility under the shared responsibility model, compared to SQL injection; guardrails are offered as a help, not a guarantee

sources.title: Prompt caching for faster model inference
supports: Implicit caching is best effort; explicit caching uses cache checkpoints, with a per-model minimum prefix (512 to 4,096 tokens) counted cumulatively across tools, system and messages

Nova 2 Lite: minimum 1K tokens, 4 checkpoints, 5-minute TTL, checkpoints in system and messages, at most 20K cached tokens. Claude Haiku 4.5: 4,096 tokens, 4 checkpoints, 5 minutes or 1 hour, system, messages and tools
The TTL resets on each cache hit; a checkpoint in front of too few tokens still succeeds but is not cached; a ttl field on a model that supports only 5 minutes can cause a ValidationException
Usage reports cacheReadInputTokens and cacheWriteInputTokens; inputTokens then counts only non-cached input; total input = inputTokens + cacheReadInputTokens + cacheWriteInputTokens
Checkpoints are processed in the order tools, system, messages; prompt caching is not supported with batch inference

sources.title: TokenUsage and CachePointBlock (API reference)
supports: TokenUsage: inputTokens, outputTokens, totalTokens, cacheReadInputTokens, cacheWriteInputTokens, cacheDetails
CachePointBlock: type default, optional ttl 5m | 1h

sources.title: Set up a model invocation resource using inference profiles
supports: System-defined cross-Region profiles and application inference profiles (user-created, taggable for cost tracking, over one model or one cross-Region profile)
The price of an inference profile is that of the model in the Region the profile is called from

sources.title: Prerequisites for inference profiles
supports: A policy that names an inference profile must also name the foundation model in each Region of the profile; bedrock:InferenceProfileArn restricts model access to calls through one profile
A global profile needs the Region-less model ARN; aws:RequestedRegion equal to 'unspecified' can be denied to block global routing

sources.title: Route model inference requests across AWS Regions with cross-Region inference
supports: Geographic profiles keep processing within a geography; global profiles may use any supported commercial Region and cost about 10% less
Data in transit stays on the AWS network and is encrypted; CloudTrail logs the request in the source Region with additionalEventData.inferenceRegion
Inference profiles do not support Provisioned Throughput
sources.note: Read with geographic-cross-region-inference.html and global-cross-region-inference.html.

sources.title: Model card: Nova 2 Lite
supports: bedrock-runtime features supported: response streaming, guardrails, client-side tool calling; not supported: structured outputs, count tokens, knowledge base, agents, prompt management, intelligent prompt routing
Tokyo: no In-Region access, Geo (jp. profile to ap-northeast-1 and ap-northeast-3) and Global
Lifecycle Active; EOL no sooner than Dec 02, 2026; legacy period at least 6 months
Service tiers: Standard, Priority and Flex yes; Reserved no

sources.title: What is AWS DataSync?
supports: DataSync is a file transfer service for file or object data to, from, and between AWS storage services
The other clouds it lists include Google Cloud Storage, Azure Blob Storage, and Cloudflare R2 Storage
DataSync includes encryption in transit and data integrity validation

sources.title: How AWS DataSync transfers work
supports: An agent is a VM appliance; a location is where data is copied from or to; a task describes a transfer; a task execution is one run of it
By default DataSync prepares a transfer by scanning both locations to find differences; with transfer-all it does not compare
DataSync always performs integrity checks during a transfer and can verify again at the end
A file written to during a transfer can be detected at verification, and getting its latest version needs another run
Transfers between AWS storage services in one account need no agent and stay on the AWS network

sources.title: Choosing a task mode for your data transfer
supports: Enhanced mode lists, prepares, transfers, and verifies in parallel and works with virtually unlimited numbers of objects; Basic mode does these sequentially and is subject to quotas
Enhanced mode verifies only transferred data; Basic mode verifies all data by default
Enhanced mode logs are structured JSON; Basic mode logs are unstructured
The task mode cannot be changed after the task is created
Creating an Enhanced mode task needs iam:CreateServiceLinkedRole

sources.title: Where can I transfer my data with AWS DataSync?
supports: S3 to S3 needs no agent in Basic and Enhanced mode, within one account and across accounts
Other cloud storage to S3 needs an agent only in Basic mode; NFS and SMB always need an agent
Between AWS storage services in different Regions, one of the two locations must be in the Region where DataSync is used
Data transferred between Regions is billed as data transfer out from the source Region to the destination Region

sources.title: Do I need an AWS DataSync agent?
supports: An agent is needed between AWS storage and on-premises storage, and between EFS or FSx and other clouds
No agent is needed between AWS storage services in the same account, or between S3 and object storage in other clouds

sources.title: Configuring AWS DataSync transfers with Amazon S3
supports: The IAM permissions a source location role and a destination location role need, action by action
New objects get the storage class of the destination location; existing objects keep theirs unless the task transfers all data
In a versioned bucket DataSync creates a new version when the source object is modified, and only the latest version of a source object is transferred
DataSync makes LIST, HEAD, GET, PUT, and COPY requests on every run, HEAD requests even when nothing moves

Standard-IA, One Zone-IA, and Glacier Instant Retrieval can charge for overwriting, deleting, or retrieving, and objects under 128 KB are stored in S3 Standard instead; archived objects must be restored before DataSync can read them
A bucket encrypted with SSE-C cannot be accessed; SSE-KMS needs the role in the key policy

sources.title: Tutorial: Transferring data between Amazon S3 buckets across AWS accounts
supports: The DataSync role, both locations, and the task are created in the source account
The destination bucket's policy names that role and allows ten S3 actions on the bucket and its objects
ACLs are disabled on the destination bucket so that its account owns the objects
A cross-account location cannot be created in the console; create-location-s3 is run with the destination bucket's Region
To avoid a network connection error the task is created in the same Region as the destination location; with Basic mode across accounts and Regions the alternative is an Enhanced mode task

sources.title: DataSync API: Options
supports: TransferMode CHANGED (default) or ALL; OverwriteMode ALWAYS (default) or NEVER; PreserveDeletedFiles PRESERVE (default) or REMOVE
VerifyMode ONLY_FILES_TRANSFERRED, POINT_IN_TIME_CONSISTENT (default for Basic mode, not supported in Enhanced mode), or NONE
ObjectTags PRESERVE (default) or NONE; LogLevel OFF, BASIC, or TRANSFER
OverwriteMode NEVER protects against overwriting changes made in the destination

sources.title: Configuring how to handle files, objects, and metadata
supports: A task cannot both delete data in the destination and transfer all data, because transfer-all does not scan the destination
Deleting or overwriting objects can incur minimum storage duration, retrieval, or early deletion charges in some storage classes

sources.title: Understanding how DataSync handles file and object metadata
supports: Between object storage and Amazon S3, DataSync copies user-defined metadata, object tags, and Content-Disposition, Content-Encoding, Content-Language, and Content-Type
DataSync does not copy object ACLs, prior object versions, or the Last-Modified key
sources.note: The table row is headed 'Object storage, Amazon S3'. The page has no row that names S3 to S3 separately.

sources.title: Configuring how AWS DataSync verifies data integrity
supports: During a transfer DataSync uses checksum verification; verification at the end is an additional, configurable step
Verify-all checks the entire source and destination at the end and cannot be used with Enhanced mode or with Glacier Flexible Retrieval and Deep Archive destinations

sources.title: Transferring specific files, objects, and folders by using filters
supports: A filter is patterns joined by a pipe; filters are case sensitive and relative to the source location path
/dir and /dir/ both match the folder and its content, and a slash in an S3 key is treated as a folder
Include filters support the wildcard only as the rightmost character of a pattern
A backslash escapes *, | and \
sources.note: The page does not say whether a destination object that a filter excludes is deleted when deleted files are removed.

sources.title: Transferring specific files or objects by using a manifest
supports: A manifest is a CSV file listing the exact files or objects to transfer, optionally with an S3 version ID
A manifest cannot be combined with filters, and DataSync deletes nothing in the destination when one is used
The maximum manifest size with Enhanced mode is 20 GB

sources.title: Scheduling when your AWS DataSync task runs
supports: A task schedule is a cron or rate expression with a minimum interval of one hour
DataSync may disable a schedule when the task fails repeatedly with the same error; the schedule's Status, DisabledBy, and DisabledReason show it

sources.title: Starting a task to transfer your data
supports: Task execution statuses are QUEUED, LAUNCHING, LAUNCHED, PREPARING, TRANSFERRING, VERIFYING, SUCCESS, CANCELLING, and ERROR
start-task-execution starts a run and can override options for that run

sources.title: Monitoring your data transfers with task reports

sources.title: What is Amazon S3? (data consistency model)
supports: Updates to a single key are atomic: a concurrent GET returns the old data or the new data, never partial or corrupt data
There is no way to make atomic updates across keys

sources.title: Performing object operations in bulk with Batch Operations

sources.title: What is AWS Database Migration Service?
supports: AWS DMS creates the tables and associated primary keys if they don't exist on the target; you can create the target tables yourself
DMS Schema Conversion is for migrating to a different database engine: it assesses and converts source schemas to a new target engine

sources.title: High-level view of AWS DMS
supports: A task can consist of three phases: full load, application of cached changes, and ongoing replication (CDC)
AWS DMS doesn't capture changes for a given table until the full load for that table is started, so the point when change capture starts differs per table
After all cached changes are applied the tables are transactionally consistent and DMS moves to ongoing replication, applying changes as transactions
At steady state you can shut down your applications, allow any remaining transactions to be applied to the target, and bring your applications up pointing at the target
With the minimalist approach AWS DMS creates tables, primary keys, and in some cases unique indexes, and no other objects

sources.title: Components of AWS DMS
supports: A replication instance is a managed Amazon EC2 instance that hosts one or more replication tasks, and comes with 50 GB or 100 GB of storage depending on its class
The three migration types are full load, full load + CDC, and CDC only
Target table preparation modes are do nothing, drop tables on target, and truncate
If changes are captured faster than they can be applied, pending changes spill to disk on the replication instance and target latency exceeds source latency

sources.title: Sources for AWS DMS
supports: Source endpoints for data migration include PostgreSQL 9.4 and higher on premises and on EC2, RDS for PostgreSQL 10.x to 18.x, and Aurora PostgreSQL
The third-party managed PostgreSQL services listed are Microsoft Azure PostgreSQL Flexible Server and Google Cloud for PostgreSQL
The page lists neither Aurora DSQL, nor SQLite, nor Neon

sources.title: Targets for AWS DMS
supports: Target endpoints for data migration include RDS for PostgreSQL, Aurora PostgreSQL-Compatible Edition, Aurora PostgreSQL Limitless, and Aurora Serverless v2
The page does not list Aurora DSQL

sources.title: Using a PostgreSQL database as an AWS DMS source
supports: For an RDS for PostgreSQL source, CDC needs rds.logical_replication set to 1 in the parameter group, a static parameter that requires a reboot
The user on an AWS-managed source must have the rds_superuser role and the rds_replication role; using the master account is not recommended
A captured table must have a primary key; without one AWS DMS ignores DELETE and UPDATE operations for that table
For full load and CDC tasks AWS DMS uses logical replication slots to retain WAL until the logs are decoded; on restart (not resume) the slot is recreated
Slots remain open even when the task is no longer running; DMS drops a slot it created when the task is deleted
DMS uses the pglogical plugin if it is available on the source and test_decoding otherwise
If max_slot_wal_keep_size is set and a slot's restart_lsn falls behind by more than that size, the DMS task fails
Changes held in a slot can cause elevated disk usage; AWS recommends space usage alarms on the source
HeartbeatEnable mimics a dummy transaction so that idle slots do not hold on to old WAL; HeartbeatSchema defaults to public
With CaptureDdls false, DMS does not need its DDL audit table and event trigger on the source
FailTasksOnLobTruncation makes a task fail instead of truncating a LOB larger than LobMaxSize
The source data type table maps TEXT, JSON and JSONB to NCLOB, XML to CLOB, BYTEA to BLOB, and UUID to STRING
For PostgreSQL to PostgreSQL migrations of an entire database, AWS recommends native tools such as pg_dump
AWS DMS does not support CDC for Amazon RDS Proxy for PostgreSQL as a source, and does not support materialized views
AWS DMS does not support change processing of ALTER COLUMN SET DEFAULT or SET/DROP NOT NULL

sources.title: Using a PostgreSQL database as a target for AWS Database Migration Service
supports: Table order during full load cannot be guaranteed, so active foreign keys can make the task fail; AWS recommends disabling them during the full load
AfterConnectScript=SET session_replication_role = replica makes AWS DMS bypass foreign keys and user triggers
AWS DMS doesn't migrate sequences during ongoing replication: update NEXTVAL for each sequence on the target after stopping replication from the source
The minimum grants for the target user: CONNECT and CREATE on the database, USAGE and CREATE on the schema, and UPDATE, INSERT, SELECT, DELETE, TRUNCATE on its tables

sources.title: Working with AWS DMS Serverless
supports: With AWS DMS Serverless you create endpoints and a replication configuration, and start, stop, modify, or delete replications
The current engine version for AWS DMS Serverless is 3.5.4

sources.title: AWS DMS Serverless components
supports: A DCU is 2 GB of RAM, and AWS DMS bills for each DCU the replication is currently using
AWS DMS Serverless supports PostgreSQL-compatible databases as sources and PostgreSQL as a target
After a serverless replication has been started it is resumed with the start type resume-processing; a replication that has not started in 48 hours is deprovisioned and cannot be resumed
MinCapacityUnits defaults to 1 DCU; MultiAZ is recommended for CDC
CDCLatencySource is the gap between the last event captured from the source and the current time, and can be 0 when there are no new events
CDCLatencyTarget is the gap between the first event waiting to commit on the target and the current time
Logs go to a log group named dms-serverless-replication-<replication config resource ID>, which DMS creates only when the replication runs
A configuration can be modified only in the CREATED, STOPPED, FAILED, or FAILED_PROVISION states

sources.title: AWS DMS Serverless limitations
supports: Serverless replications must reach AWS Secrets Manager, Amazon S3 and other dependencies through VPC endpoints
AWS DMS Serverless does not support views and does not support custom CDC start points
A replication configuration can be deleted only in the STOPPED or FAILED states

sources.title: Selection rules and actions
supports: A selection rule has rule-type, rule-id (numeric, unique), rule-name (unique), rule-action (include, exclude, explicit) and an object-locator with schema-name and table-name
At least one selection rule is required
The documented example includes every table of a schema and then excludes those matching a pattern

sources.title: Transformation rules and actions
supports: A transformation rule with rule-action rename and rule-target schema renames a schema on the target, with the new name in value
Transformation rules that alter the target schema take effect only after the task is restarted, not resumed

sources.title: Wildcards in table mapping
supports: % matches zero or more characters and _ matches a single character
Bracket patterns may not work with all endpoint types

sources.title: Specifying task settings for AWS Database Migration Service tasks
supports: The example settings show the sections TargetMetadata, FullLoadSettings, Logging, ErrorBehavior and ValidationSettings, with LobMaxSize 32 in limited LOB mode

sources.title: Full-load task settings
supports: TargetTablePrepMode is DO_NOTHING, DROP_AND_CREATE, or TRUNCATE_BEFORE_LOAD
MaxFullLoadSubTasks, the number of tables loaded in parallel, defaults to 8

sources.title: Error handling task settings
supports: ApplyErrorInsertPolicy and ApplyErrorUpdatePolicy default to LOG_ERROR, ApplyErrorDeletePolicy to IGNORE_RECORD
TableErrorPolicy defaults to SUSPEND_TABLE: the task continues without that table
FailOnNoTablesCaptured defaults to true

sources.title: Data validation task settings
supports: EnableValidation defaults to false; FailureMaxCount defaults to 10,000
ValidationPartialLobSize limits how much of a LOB column is validated

sources.title: Setting LOB support for source databases in an AWS DMS task
supports: In limited LOB mode, LOBs larger than the maximum LOB size are truncated and a warning is logged
A primary key or unique index is required for tables containing LOB columns during CDC

sources.title: AWS DMS data validation
supports: Validation begins after a table's full load and compares incremental changes as they occur; DMS compares each source row with its target row
Data validation requires a primary key or unique index; a VARCHAR or CHAR key must declare a length under 1024
The per-table ValidationState values, including Validated, Mismatched records, Pending records, and No primary key
If the target is modified outside DMS during validation, discrepancies might not be reported accurately; continuously modified rows can't be validated
Validation stops after more than 10,000 failed or suspended records

sources.title: Enabling and working with premigration assessments for a task
supports: A premigration assessment run evaluates a task configuration for problems such as unsupported data types and primary key formats before the task runs

sources.title: Troubleshooting migration tasks in AWS Database Migration Service
supports: In full or limited LOB mode AWS DMS doesn't support replication of primary keys that are LOB data types
A full load and CDC task can create duplicate records on target tables without a primary key or unique index
With target table preparation mode Do nothing, a restarted task can hit primary key violations from rows of a previous run

sources.title: Using secrets to access AWS Database Migration Service endpoints
supports: An endpoint takes either clear-text credentials or SecretsManagerSecretId with SecretsManagerAccessRoleArn, not both
The secret is JSON with username, password, port and host
Master credentials managed by Amazon RDS cannot be used because they lack host and port
The secret access role trusts the Regional principal dms.<region>.amazonaws.com and needs secretsmanager:GetSecretValue on the secret
AWS DMS does not allow the characters ; . : + { } * & , % \ in endpoint passwords

sources.title: Configuring AWS DMS secrets manager VPC Endpoint

sources.title: Identity and access management for AWS Database Migration Service

dms-vpc-role trusts dms.amazonaws.com and carries the managed policy AmazonDMSVPCManagementRole; dms-cloudwatch-logs-role carries AmazonDMSCloudWatchLogsRole

sources.title: PostgreSQL 18: 29.8. Restrictions (logical replication)
supports: The database schema and DDL commands are not replicated
Sequence data is not replicated; for a switchover the sequences must be updated to the latest values
Large objects are not replicated, and only tables can be replicated, not views or materialized views

sources.title: PostgreSQL 18: 29.1. Publication
supports: A published table needs a replica identity to replicate UPDATE and DELETE; by default this is the primary key

sources.title: PostgreSQL 18: 26.2. Log-Shipping Standby Servers (replication slots)
supports: Replication slots can cause the server to retain so many WAL segments that they fill up the space allocated for pg_wal

sources.title: PostgreSQL 18: 19.6. Replication
supports: max_slot_wal_keep_size defaults to -1, meaning slots may retain an unlimited amount of WAL
max_replication_slots and max_wal_senders default to 10

sources.title: PostgreSQL 18: pg_replication_slots
supports: active is true while a slot is being streamed; restart_lsn is the oldest WAL the slot's consumer might still need

sources.title: PostgreSQL 18: 9.28. System Administration Functions
supports: pg_drop_replication_slot(slot_name) drops a physical or logical replication slot

sources.title: PostgreSQL 18: REVOKE
supports: REVOKE removes previously granted privileges from one or more roles

sources.title: PostgreSQL 18: pg_stat_activity
supports: state 'idle in transaction' means the backend is in a transaction and not executing a query; xact_start is when the current transaction started

sources.title: AWS CLI 2.35.11: bundled service definition for dms (2016-01-01)
supports: start-replication requires --replication-config-arn and --start-replication-type; stop-replication requires --replication-config-arn
describe-replications filters by replication-config-arn or replication-config-id; describe-replication-table-statistics requires --replication-config-arn
StopReplication does not deprovision the stopped replication
TableStatistics carries FullLoadRows, the applied insert, update and delete counts, and ValidationState with its documented values

sources.title: PostgreSQL 18: pg_dump
supports: pg_dump makes consistent exports even if the database is being used concurrently and does not block readers or writers

sources.title: PostgreSQL 18: 9.17. Sequence Manipulation Functions
supports: setval(regclass, bigint, boolean): with is_called true the next nextval advances the sequence before returning a value

sources.title: Performing logical replication for Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL
supports: rds.logical_replication is a static parameter; setting it to 1 needs a reboot and can increase WAL generation

sources.title: Amazon CloudWatch metrics for Amazon RDS
supports: OldestReplicationSlotLag, TransactionLogsDiskUsage and ReplicationSlotDiskUsage are published for PostgreSQL, in bytes

sources.title: Overview of Amazon RDS Blue/Green Deployments
supports: Blue/green deployments are supported for RDS for PostgreSQL; the green environment is a copy that stays in sync, and switchover typically takes under a minute
The overview describes version upgrades and parameter changes, and no change of engine

sources.title: Limitations and considerations for Amazon RDS blue/green deployments
supports: During switchover Amazon RDS increments sequence values in the green environment to match the blue one

sources.title: Migrating data to Amazon Aurora with PostgreSQL compatibility
supports: For an RDS for PostgreSQL source the page lists migration from a snapshot and migration through an Aurora read replica, and names AWS DMS for sources that are not PostgreSQL-compatible

sources.title: Loading data into Aurora DSQL

supports: wrangler d1 export writes a D1 database to a .sql file
A running export blocks other database requests, and export is not supported for databases with virtual tables

sources.title: Cloudflare D1: Query a database
supports: D1 is reached through the Workers binding, the REST API, and Wrangler; the docs list no database wire protocol

sources.title: Vercel: Postgres on Vercel

sources.title: Vercel: Marketplace storage
