sources.title: What is AWS Health?
supports: The AWS Health Dashboard is available to all AWS customers at no additional cost and requires no setup
All AWS customers can receive AWS Health events through Amazon EventBridge at no additional cost

The AWS Health API needs an AWS Business Support+, AWS Enterprise Support, or AWS Unified Operations plan; in a Region that does not offer these plans, or for an account that has not transitioned, a Business, Enterprise On-Ramp, or Enterprise Support plan

sources.title: Concepts for AWS Health
supports: Health events are notifications that AWS Health sends on behalf of other AWS services; there are account-specific events and public events
A public event is reported even if the account does not use that service or has no resources in that Region
Public events are not available through AWS managed notifications in AWS User Notifications; an EventBridge rule or a user-configured notification is needed
Event type categories: account notification, issue, scheduled change; all scheduled change events are account-specific

Example event type codes, including AWS_EC2_OPERATIONAL_ISSUE, AWS_EBS_VOLUME_ATTACHMENT_ISSUE, AWS_ABUSE_PII_CONTENT_REMOVAL_REPORT (listed under issue), AWS_EC2_INSTANCE_RETIREMENT_SCHEDULED, AWS_RDS_PLANNED_LIFECYCLE_EVENT, AWS_S3_OPEN_ACCESS_BUCKET_NOTIFICATION, AWS_BILLING_SUSPENSION_NOTICE
Event status is open, closed, or upcoming; events can be viewed in the dashboard or the API for up to 90 days
Actionability is ACTION_REQUIRED, ACTION_MAY_BE_REQUIRED, or INFORMATIONAL; events about service issues carry no actionability label
Personas are OPERATIONS, SECURITY, and BILLING
Calling the AWS Health API without one of the required Support plans returns SubscriptionRequiredException
The public Service health page is https://health.aws.amazon.com/health/status and needs no account; the signed-in dashboard is https://health.aws.amazon.com/health/home

sources.title: Viewing your account events in the AWS Health Dashboard
supports: Your account health has the tabs Open and recent issues, Scheduled changes, Other notifications, and Event log; the event log shows the events of the past 90 days

sources.title: AWS Health Dashboard
supports: The Service health page shows only public events, for all services and Regions, without signing in; Service history covers the last 12 months
An RSS feed exists but its format is subject to change; AWS recommends EventBridge for ingesting events programmatically

sources.title: Monitoring events in AWS Health with Amazon EventBridge
supports: AWS Health delivers events on a durable basis and attempts to deliver each to EventBridge at least once
A rule receives events for its own account only; organizational view is needed for other accounts
Public events might take up to one hour to start arriving after a rule is created

sources.title: Creating EventBridge rules for AWS Region coverage
supports: A rule is created in each Region whose events are wanted

In the standard partition US West (Oregon) is the backup Region of every other Region and US East (N. Virginia) is the backup of US West (Oregon); events are sent to both the primary and the backup Region
A rule in a backup Region that should not receive copies filters on detail.backupEvent
Simplified integration: one rule in US West (Oregon) receives account-specific events of all standard-partition Regions, without public events and without high availability
Global events, such as those of IAM, require a rule in US East (N. Virginia)
For a highly available setup, rules in both Regions and de-duplication by detail.communicationId

sources.title: Monitoring account-specific and public events for AWS Health
supports: A rule with "source": ["aws.health"] delivers both account-specific and public events; a wildcard such as "aws.health*" matches nothing
eventScopeCode is PUBLIC or ACCOUNT_SPECIFIC and can be filtered on
Public events reach the backup Region only when a valid rule exists in the impacted Region; account-specific events reach both regardless of rules
AWS recommends de-duplicating by eventARN and communicationId

sources.title: Viewing paginated lists of AWS Health events on EventBridge
supports: An event whose resources or affectedEntities exceed EventBridge's 256 KB limit is split into pages published as separate messages with the same eventARN
For human-readable notifications a filter on detail.page keeps only the first page
The communicationId carries the page number after a hyphen even when there is one page

sources.title: Reference: AWS Health events Amazon EventBridge schema
supports: detail-type is AWS Health Event or AWS Health Abuse Event; source is aws.health
region is the Region the notification was delivered to; the impacted Region is detail.eventRegion
The fields of detail, their required flags, and the time format 'DoW, DD MMM YYYY HH:MM:SS TZ'
eventTypeCategory is issue, accountNotification, investigation, or scheduledChange; statusCode is open, closed, or upcoming
An event ARN is not unique to an account or Region; communicationId with the account ID helps de-duplicate
For public events latestDescription holds only the latest update, not the history
page, totalPages and backupEvent are strings in the sample payloads
The five sample payloads copied into examples/44-health/fixtures/documented.json
Events that include MAINTENANCE_SCHEDULED are generally pushed about two weeks before the start time
sources.note: The field table marks lastUpdatedTime as required, but two of the five samples leave it out; one sample leaves out resources. The table spells the persona OPERATIONAL while the samples and the concepts page say OPERATIONS. The samples' weekdays do not fit their dates. No sample and no field list is given for AWS Health Abuse Event.

sources.title: Configuring an EventBridge rule to send notifications about events in AWS Health
supports: Example patterns that filter on detail.service with the codes EC2, AUTOSCALING and VPC, on eventTypeCategory, and on actionability
For security use cases AWS suggests all AWS Health Abuse events and events with the SECURITY persona

sources.title: Aggregating AWS Health events using organizational view and delegated administrator access
supports: With organizational view on, the management account or a delegated administrator account receives one feed of events from all accounts of the organization on EventBridge; rules in other accounts keep working

sources.title: Aggregating AWS Health events across accounts
supports: Organizational view needs an organization with all features enabled and is turned on from the management account
AWS calls delegating the view to a member account a best practice
Organizational events are available for 90 days

sources.title: Enabling organizational view
supports: Organizational view is available in the AWS Health console for all AWS Support plans at no additional cost

sources.title: Registering a delegated administrator for your organizational view
supports: Up to five member accounts can be registered as delegated administrators, with aws organizations register-delegated-administrator and the service principal health.amazonaws.com

sources.title: Manage AWS Health notifications in AWS User Notifications
supports: Since December 15, 2025 AWS Health email is delivered by AWS managed notifications in AWS User Notifications, from health@aws.com, to the account contacts by default
Channels: email, chat, and push notifications to the AWS Console Mobile Application
The notifications are less detailed than the AWS Health API, the aws.health source in EventBridge, and the dashboard
Public service events are not available through AWS managed notifications

sources.title: Planned lifecycle events for AWS Health
supports: Planned lifecycle events are scheduled changes with the type code AWS_{SERVICE}_PLANNED_LIFECYCLE_EVENT
The start time is the soonest date resources are affected and is to be treated as the change date; an end time is not always given
Lead time is designed to be at least 180 days for major changes and 90 days for minor ones, where possible
Affected resources are PENDING until acted on, then RESOLVED; these updates can lag by up to 72 hours
An event with unresolved resources stays open for four years after its start or end date

sources.title: Running operations on EC2 instances automatically in response to events in AWS Health
supports: AWS_EC2_PERSISTENT_INSTANCE_RETIREMENT_SCHEDULED is sent for EBS-backed instances and AWS_EC2_INSTANCE_RETIREMENT_SCHEDULED for instance store-backed ones
The EventBridge console's rule builder lists the Health service codes and event type codes to choose from

sources.title: Integrating AWS Health with other systems using the AWS Health API
supports: The AWS Health API needs a Business Support+, Enterprise Support, or Unified Operations plan, or one of the older Business, Enterprise On-Ramp, or Enterprise Support plans where those still apply; otherwise SubscriptionRequiredException
The API has an active endpoint in us-east-1, a passive one in us-east-2, and the global endpoint global.health.amazonaws.com

sources.title: AWS Health API Reference: Welcome
supports: The API returns the information shown in the AWS Health Dashboard
The Event data type: service is a code such as EC2 or RDS; statusCode is open, closed, or upcoming; eventScopeCode is PUBLIC, ACCOUNT_SPECIFIC, or NONE
sources.note: On 2026-10-13 this page still names the Business, Enterprise On-Ramp, and Enterprise Support plans only, while the user guide names Business Support+, Enterprise Support, and Unified Operations first. The chapter follows the user guide and says so.

sources.title: AWS Health Dashboard: Service health
supports: On 2026-10-13 the data behind the page listed a public event whose ARN carried the service MULTIPLE_SERVICES and the type code AWS_MULTIPLE_SERVICES_OPERATIONAL_ISSUE
sources.note: Read from https://health.aws.amazon.com/public/currentevents, the JSON the page loads. That endpoint is not documented; it is used here only as an observation of one service code.

sources.title: Scheduled events for Amazon EC2 instances
supports: AWS notifies of a scheduled event in advance by email to the address associated with the account, and also sends an AWS Health event
The types of scheduled events: instance stop, instance retirement, instance reboot, system reboot, system maintenance
An instance in an Auto Scaling group is eventually replaced with no further action

sources.title: Instance retirement
supports: An instance is scheduled for retirement when AWS detects irreparable failure of the underlying hardware
An EBS-backed instance is stopped and can be started again, which moves it to new hardware; an instance store-backed instance is terminated
The primary contact and the operations contact of the account receive the email

sources.title: Lambda runtimes
supports: At least 180 days before a runtime is deprecated, Lambda sends email to the primary account contact and shows a notification in the Health Dashboard for accounts with functions on that runtime in $LATEST
Deprecation notifications are not available for functions that use container images

sources.title: What is AWS User Notifications?
supports: AWS managed notifications are generated by default by services such as AWS Health; user-configured notifications are built on EventBridge rules the user specifies
Channels: the Console Notifications Center, email, Amazon Q Developer in chat applications, and AWS Console Mobile App push notifications

sources.title: AWS User Notifications FAQs
supports: AWS User Notifications is offered free of charge

sources.title: Compare AWS Support Plans
supports: The plans listed are Basic Support, Business Support+, Enterprise Support, and Unified Operations; Basic Support is included for all AWS customers
The comparison lists the AWS Health API under health monitoring
sources.note: The page was read as text; which plan columns carry the check mark for the AWS Health API could not be read from it. The rule in the chapter comes from the AWS Health user guide.

sources.title: AWS Support Plan Pricing
supports: Business Support+: the greater of USD 29 a month per account or 9% of monthly AWS charges up to USD 10K, with lower percentages above
Enterprise Support starts at USD 5,000 a month and Unified Operations at USD 50,000 a month

sources.title: Amazon EventBridge Pricing
supports: AWS management events are ingested by the event bus for free
The page lists no charge for rules

sources.title: AWS Price List: Amazon SNS, ap-northeast-1
supports: Email and Email-JSON notifications: the first 1,000 a month are free, then USD 2.00 per 100,000 (SKU U7N84S2RCJJJKURJ, publication date 2026-09-15)

sources.title: Amazon SNS API Reference: Publish
supports: A subject must be UTF-8 text with no line breaks or control characters, and less than 100 characters long

sources.title: How Lambda handles errors and retries with asynchronous invocation
supports: A function error is retried twice by default, one minute after the first attempt and two minutes after the second
A function can receive the same event more than once even without an error
A dead-letter queue captures discarded events

sources.title: Sending events between event buses in the same account and Region
supports: Events sent from one event bus to another are charged as custom events
sources.note: Read while deciding against forwarding us-east-1's events to Tokyo's bus. The chapter does not build that.

sources.title: cdkd v0.296.28: register-providers.ts
supports: cdkd 0.296.28 registers its own providers for AWS::Events::Rule, AWS::Lambda::Function, AWS::Lambda::Permission, AWS::DynamoDB::Table, AWS::SNS::Topic, AWS::SNS::TopicPolicy, AWS::SNS::Subscription, AWS::SQS::Queue, AWS::SQS::QueuePolicy, AWS::Logs::LogGroup, AWS::IAM::Role and AWS::IAM::Policy

sources.title: Cloudflare Notifications
supports: Notifications are delivered by email and webhooks on all plans, and by PagerDuty on Business plans and higher

sources.title: Cloudflare: Available Notifications
supports: Incident Alerts tell an account when Cloudflare incidents are created, updated, and resolved, on all plans, and can be filtered by impact level and by affected component
Maintenance Notification tells when maintenance of a point of presence is scheduled, changed, or canceled, on all plans, and can be filtered by point of presence

sources.title: Vercel Status
supports: The status page offers subscriptions by email, SMS, Slack, webhook, and an Atom or RSS feed to incidents Vercel creates, updates, or resolves
The subscription forms offer no choice of component or region

sources.title: Vercel Alerts
supports: Alerts report usage and error anomalies of the account's own projects by email, Slack, or webhook, on Enterprise plans and on Pro plans with Observability Plus
The page does not mention incidents of the Vercel platform

sources.title: What is AWS Infrastructure Composer? - AWS Infrastructure Composer Developer Guide
supports: End of support notice at the top: the standalone console is unavailable from December 7, 2026; the embedded console experiences were replaced by a visual IaC editor; the full experience remains in the AWS Toolkit for Visual Studio Code
Infrastructure Composer can be used from its console, the AWS Toolkit for Visual Studio Code, and in CloudFormation console mode
It creates CloudFormation and AWS SAM templates and syncs changes between the canvas and the template code
Existing CloudFormation and AWS SAM templates can be imported to visualize and modify them
Any CloudFormation resource can be dragged onto the canvas

sources.title: AWS Infrastructure Composer end of support
supports: End of support is effective December 7, 2026; no new customers from October 29, 2026 (stated as a target date in the FAQ)
The standalone URL console.aws.amazon.com/composer is not accessible after December 7, 2026
The AWS Toolkit for Visual Studio Code keeps the visual authoring experience; no changes are planned
The embedded experience in the CloudFormation console is replaced by a visual editor integrated in that console
The Export to Infrastructure Composer entries in the Lambda and Step Functions consoles are removed
Infrastructure Composer exposes no customer-facing API, SDK or CLI
Templates saved locally or in Amazon S3, and existing stacks, are not affected
How to open a template in VS Code: the button in the editor, the context menu, or the Command Palette

sources.title: AWS Infrastructure Composer
supports: Notice: no longer available to new customers as of October 29, 2026; existing customers until December 7, 2026
sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetcher.

sources.title: Document history for Infrastructure Composer
supports: The end of support notice was added on September 29, 2026
Public release December 1, 2022; general availability March 7, 2023; all CloudFormation resources September 26, 2023; VS Code November 30, 2023; CloudFormation console mode March 28, 2024

sources.title: AWS Application Composer is now AWS Infrastructure Composer
supports: AWS Application Composer was renamed AWS Infrastructure Composer; posted October 4, 2024
sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetcher.

sources.title: Using Infrastructure Composer in CloudFormation console mode
supports: CloudFormation console mode has no local sync
Lambda Function and Lambda Layer cards need builds and packaging that are not available in that mode
sources.note: The page still describes the mode as the recommended tool to visualize templates; the end of support page says the embedded experience is being replaced.

sources.title: Configure and modify cards in Infrastructure Composer
supports: An enhanced component card is a collection of CloudFormation resources combined into one curated card
A standard IaC resource card represents a single CloudFormation resource

sources.title: Standard cards in Infrastructure Composer
supports: All CloudFormation resources are available as standard IaC resource cards
A standard card starts from a template with the type, required or common properties, and placeholders for their value types

sources.title: Card connections in Infrastructure Composer
supports: A line between cards represents an event-driven relationship
Lines between enhanced component cards are solid; connections of standard cards are detected from the template and drawn dotted
Standard cards have no connector ports
Connecting enhanced cards provisions, when necessary, IAM policies (through AWS SAM policy templates), environment variables, and events

sources.title: Group cards together on Infrastructure Composer's visual canvas
supports: Enhanced cards are grouped by hand; a standard card is grouped into another when the template references it, as a role referenced by a function
sources.note: The page does not say what grouping writes into the template.

sources.title: Locally sync and save your project in the Infrastructure Composer console
supports: By default the template is saved by hand; local sync saves it automatically to the local machine
Local sync writes the template, project folders, a backup directory named .aws-composer, and supported external files
Local sync is off by default

sources.title: Allow web page access to local files in Infrastructure Composer
supports: Local sync needs a browser with the File System Access API; recent Google Chrome and Microsoft Edge are named
Infrastructure Composer gets read and write access to the allowed project folder and its children; the data is not stored beyond the local file system

sources.title: Reference external files in Infrastructure Composer
supports: External files are supported for API Gateway REST APIs (OpenAPI) and Step Functions state machine definitions

sources.title: View code updates with the Change Inspector in Infrastructure Composer
supports: The Change Inspector shows the template code added and removed by the most recent interaction on the canvas

sources.title: Using Infrastructure Composer from the AWS Toolkit for Visual Studio Code
supports: Deployment from VS Code goes through sam sync of the AWS SAM CLI

sources.title: Visual overview of Infrastructure Composer from the AWS Toolkit for Visual Studio Code
supports: The parts of the canvas in VS Code: resource palette, list, arrange, sync, resource properties panel, card, line, group, port
Delete removes the card from the canvas and from the template

sources.title: Access Infrastructure Composer from the AWS Toolkit for Visual Studio Code
supports: The Toolkit for VS Code must be installed first; the canvas opens from a CloudFormation or AWS SAM template
sources.note: Neither this page nor the Toolkit guide says whether JSON templates open, or whether AWS credentials are needed to draw.

sources.title: Working with AWS Infrastructure Composer in the Toolkit - AWS Toolkit for VS Code
supports: Changes made on the canvas are stored persistently, so one can switch between the file in the editor and the canvas
Three ways to open: the button in the editor, the context menu, the Command Palette
sources.note: The context menu entry is written here as Open with App Composer, and on the end of support page as Open with Infrastructure Composer.

sources.title: AWS Infrastructure Composer FAQs
supports: There is no additional charge for using Infrastructure Composer; resources created with it are billed as usual
CloudFormation and AWS SAM templates can be imported and visualized
sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetcher. The page names neither YAML nor JSON, and does not mention the AWS CDK.

sources.title: Edit templates visually with template studio - AWS CloudFormation User Guide
supports: Template studio shows the template as text beside a diagram of its resources; the text is authoritative and the diagram cannot be edited
The diagram draws a connection wherever one resource refers to another through Ref, Fn::GetAtt, Fn::Sub, or DependsOn; a resource nothing references appears on its own
A role assumed by three functions is shown inside each function although the template declares one
It opens from the navigation pane, from Create stack, from an existing stack's update, and wherever the console shows a template
Edits are not saved automatically; saving writes to Amazon S3 at standard S3 rates, by default to the bucket CloudFormation manages for uploaded templates
It converts between YAML and JSON; YAML to JSON discards comments
Validate uses ValidateTemplate with TemplateBody, limited to 51,200 bytes
The diagram downloads as a PNG
Permissions: cloudformation:GetTemplate, s3:GetObject, cloudformation:ValidateTemplate, s3:PutObject, s3:CreateBucket, s3:ListBucket
sources.note: The older address infrastructure-composer-for-cloudformation.html in the same guide now serves this page. The page does not use the name Infrastructure Composer and does not say how a file on the local machine is opened.

sources.title: Ref - CloudFormation Template Reference Guide
supports: Ref takes the logical name of a resource or a parameter
With the AWS::LanguageExtensions transform the argument can be another intrinsic function

sources.title: Fn::GetAtt - CloudFormation Template Reference Guide
supports: JSON syntax is a pair [logicalNameOfResource, attributeName]; the dotted single string is the YAML short form
Without AWS::LanguageExtensions the logical name must be a string and the attribute name may only use Ref

sources.title: Fn::Sub - CloudFormation Template Reference Guide
supports: Fn::Sub takes a string, or a string and a map of variables
${Name} resolves like Ref and ${Name.Attribute} like Fn::GetAtt
${!Literal} is written out as ${Literal}

sources.title: DependsOn attribute - CloudFormation Template Reference Guide
supports: DependsOn takes a string or a list of strings; the resource is created after the ones it names
Ref, GetAtt and Sub create implicit dependencies: the referenced resource is created first and deleted last

sources.title: Troubleshooting CloudFormation
supports: Read to look for a statement on circular dependencies; the page has none
sources.note: How CloudFormation answers a template whose references form a cycle was not confirmed from a page read for this chapter.

sources.title: How AWS Shield and Shield Advanced work
supports: Shield Standard is provided automatically and at no extra charge when you use AWS; Shield Advanced is a subscription for higher levels of protection
Classes of attack: network volumetric (layer 3), network protocol (layer 4, such as a TCP SYN flood), and application layer (layer 7, such as web request floods)

sources.title: AWS Shield Standard overview
supports: Shield Standard defends against the most common, frequently occurring network and transport layer DDoS attacks, for all AWS customers, at no additional charge
Route 53 hosted zones, CloudFront distributions and Global Accelerator standard accelerators receive comprehensive availability protection against all known network and transport layer attacks
If the first point of entry is in an AWS Region the application perimeter is the VPC; with CloudFront or Global Accelerator it begins at the edge of the AWS network

sources.title: AWS Shield Advanced overview
supports: The subscription covers standard AWS WAF fees (web ACL, rule, and base request fee up to 1,500 WCUs and the default body size) for resources protected with Shield Advanced, up to 50 billion requests a calendar month
It does not cover AWS WAF for resources that are not protected with Shield Advanced, nor Bot Control, CAPTCHA and other non-standard costs
The subscription includes access to the Layer 7 Anti-DDoS managed rule group
For accounts in one AWS Organizations consolidated billing family, one subscription price covers all subscribed accounts

sources.title: List of AWS resources that AWS Shield Advanced protects
supports: Protection applies only to resources explicitly specified in Shield Advanced or through a Firewall Manager Shield Advanced policy; nothing is protected automatically

Resource types: CloudFront distributions, Route 53 hosted zones, Global Accelerator standard accelerators, EC2 Elastic IP addresses (and instances and Network Load Balancers through them), Application Load Balancers, Classic Load Balancers

sources.title: AWS Shield Advanced capabilities and options
supports: Capabilities: AWS WAF integration, automatic application layer DDoS mitigation, health-based detection, protection groups, enhanced visibility, Firewall Manager policies at no additional charge, the Shield Response Team (SRT), proactive engagement, cost protection
To use the services of the SRT you must also be subscribed to the Business Support plan or the Enterprise Support plan
Health-based detection is available for any resource type except Route 53 hosted zones; proactive engagement only for resources with health-based detection
Cost protection is provided in the form of Shield Advanced service credits

sources.title: Deciding whether to subscribe to AWS Shield Advanced and apply additional protections
supports: Consider Shield Advanced where you need guaranteed availability, rapid access to DDoS mitigation experts, awareness and notification by AWS, or predictability in cloud costs during an attack
You pay one monthly subscription fee for all accounts under a consolidated billing account, plus usage fees based on GB of data transferred out

sources.title: Managed DDoS event response with Shield Response Team (SRT) support
supports: The SRT can analyze AWS WAF logs and, with approval, change the web ACL; build custom network mitigations; engage AWS networking teams; and recommend architecture changes
To use the SRT you must be subscribed to the Business Support plan or the Enterprise Support plan

sources.title: Requesting a credit in AWS Shield Advanced after an attack
supports: Credits cover only: Shield Advanced data transfer out, CloudFront HTTP/HTTPS requests, CloudFront data transfer out, Route 53 queries, Global Accelerator data transfer, Application Load Balancer capacity units, and EC2 instances launched by auto scaling in response to the attack

Prerequisites: the resource had Shield Advanced protection before the attack began; for CloudFront and Application Load Balancers a web ACL with a rate-based rule in Block mode was associated; the DDoS resiliency best practices were implemented

The request is a billing case with 'DDoS Concession' in the subject, submitted within 15 days after the billing month of the attack; credits apply only to Shield Advanced usage and are valid for 12 months

sources.title: Health-based detection using health checks with Shield Advanced and Route 53
supports: You define a Route 53 health check, verify it reports healthy, and associate it with the protection; Shield Advanced does not manage health checks
With an unhealthy health check Shield Advanced requires smaller deviations to alert and reports events more quickly; with a healthy one it requires larger deviations
Health checks are required for proactive engagement

sources.title: Automating application layer DDoS mitigation with Shield Advanced
supports: Starting March 26, 2026, the Anti-DDoS Managed Rule Group for AWS WAF is the default solution against HTTP request floods and supersedes Layer 7 Auto Mitigation; a new Shield Advanced customer who needs the legacy solution contacts AWS Support
The Anti-DDoS Managed Rule Group detects and mitigates attacks within seconds rather than minutes
The legacy automatic mitigation needs between 24 hours and 30 days to establish a traffic baseline after a web ACL is associated

sources.title: Grouping your AWS Shield Advanced protections
supports: A protection group treats several protected resources as one unit for detection and mitigation; membership can be all protected resources, a resource type, or named resources
Automatic application layer mitigation does not interact with protection groups

sources.title: AWS Shield Advanced metrics
supports: Shield Advanced publishes detection, mitigation and top contributor metrics in the AWS/DDoSProtection namespace for the resources it protects
DDoSDetected has a non-zero value during an event and is posted with no dimension other than the resource; DDoSAttackRequestsPerSecond is reported only for the most significant layer 7 events
Metrics for CloudFront, Route 53 and protection groups are reported in us-east-1
Metrics are reported once a minute during an event and once a day otherwise
AWS recommends an alarm for each protected resource when DDoSDetected is non-zero, and says a non-zero value does not necessarily imply an attack

sources.title: Responding to DDoS events in AWS
supports: AWS automatically mitigates network and transport layer attacks

For application layer attacks AWS attempts to detect and notify Shield Advanced customers through CloudWatch alarms and by default does not automatically apply mitigations, to avoid blocking valid traffic
A Shield Advanced customer can contact the AWS Support Center; critical and urgent cases are routed directly to DDoS experts

sources.title: Subscribing to AWS Shield Advanced
supports: You subscribe each account in the AWS WAF & Shield console; you do not subscribe to Shield Standard
Once subscribed, to unsubscribe you must contact AWS Support; auto-renewal is disabled with the UpdateSubscription API
Subscribing does not protect any resource: you must specify the resources

sources.title: AWS Shield detection logic for infrastructure layer threats (layer 3 and layer 4)
supports: For CloudFront and Route 53 all packets are inspected by a fully inline DDoS mitigation system and attacks are mitigated in real time, regardless of whether you use Shield Advanced

For regional resources such as load balancers and Elastic IP addresses, traffic is evaluated every minute and a mitigation is placed when the resource's capacity is exceeded; mitigations reduce DDoS traffic but might not eliminate it
Shield Advanced adds lower detection thresholds (half the calculated capacity), intermittent attack protection, and health-based detection

sources.title: AWS Shield mitigation logic for CloudFront and Route 53
supports: CloudFront only lets traffic that is valid for web applications through; TCP SYN floods are mitigated by a SYN proxy and TLS is terminated at the edge, so the origin only receives well-formed web requests
Shield Advanced does not support CloudFront tenants

sources.title: Setting up proactive engagement for the SRT to contact you directly
supports: Proactive engagement needs the Business or Enterprise Support plan, a Route 53 health check on the protected resource, and at least one contact (up to ten)
Proactive engagement is not available for events detected by the Anti-DDoS managed rule group

sources.title: AWS Shield Pricing
supports: Shield Advanced requires a 1-year subscription commitment and charges a monthly fee plus a usage fee on data transfer out
Subscriptions auto-renew annually; the renewal can be cancelled through the Support Center between 30 and 5 days before the renewal date
All Shield Advanced benefits, including DDoS cost protection, are subject to fulfillment of the 1-year commitment
If CloudFront is in front of a load balancer that receives all its traffic from CloudFront, only CloudFront needs protection
To contact the Shield Response Team customers need the Enterprise or Business Support levels
sources.note: The monthly fee is filled in by script on the page; the amount was read from the Price List (shield-price-list).

sources.title: AWS Price List: AWSShield
supports: Shield-Monthly-Fee: USD 3,000 for the first subscription, USD 0 for additional subscriptions
Global-DataTransfer-Shield-Bytes out of CloudFront: USD 0.025 per GB for the first 100 TB
APN1-DataTransfer-Shield-Bytes out of ELB and of Elastic IP in Tokyo: USD 0.05 per GB for the first 100 TB

sources.title: Rate-based rule high-level settings in AWS WAF
supports: The evaluation window is 60, 120, 300 or 600 seconds, 300 by default; it sets how far back AWS WAF looks, not how often it checks
The lowest rate limit is 10
A rate-based rule that counts all requests together needs a scope-down statement

sources.title: Rate-based rule caveats in AWS WAF
supports: AWS WAF rate limiting is not intended for precise request-rate limiting and does not guarantee an exact limit match
Requests can come in at too high a rate for up to several minutes before AWS WAF detects and rate limits them; usually this delay is below 30 seconds
Changing a rate limit setting resets the rule's counts and can pause rate limiting for up to a minute

sources.title: Applying rate limiting to requests in AWS WAF
supports: The rule action applies to a request that belongs to an aggregation instance whose request count is currently over the limit
With the Count action the rule does not limit the rate of requests

sources.title: Listing IP addresses that are being rate limited by rate-based rules
supports: The list of rate-limited IP addresses is read with get-rate-based-statement-managed-keys; the console does not provide it
A single rate-based rule instance can rate limit at most 10,000 IP addresses; beyond that it limits those with the highest rates

sources.title: DDoS Simulation Testing Policy
supports: DDoS simulation testing must be performed by an AWS DDoS Test Partner pre-approved by AWS
The target must be a Protected Resource in an account you own that is subscribed to Shield Advanced, or an edge-optimized API Gateway endpoint in such an account
The request volume may not exceed 50,000 requests per second, and the test may not originate from an AWS resource

sources.title: AWS WAF Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) prevention
supports: AWSManagedRulesAntiDDoSRuleSet builds traffic baselines for the protected resource and manages requests during probable DDoS events, for CloudFront distributions, Application Load Balancers and other resources AWS WAF supports
The managed rule group is charged for in addition to standard AWS WAF fees

sources.title: AWS WAF metrics and dimensions
supports: BlockedRequests is in the AWS/WAFV2 namespace with the dimensions Rule and WebACL; the Region dimension is required for all protected resource types except CloudFront distributions

sources.title: AWS Price List: awswaf
supports: Global-AMR-AntiDDoS: USD 20.00 per month in CloudFront; Global-AMR-AntiDDoS-Request: USD 0.15 per million requests
Global-WebACLV2 USD 5.00 per web ACL per month, Global-RuleV2 USD 1.00 per rule per month, Global-RequestV2-Tier1 USD 0.60 per million requests
For Shield protected resources the web ACL, rule and tier-0 request SKUs are USD 0

sources.title: Amazon CloudFront no longer charges for requests blocked by AWS WAF
supports: Effective October 25, 2024, CloudFront requests blocked by AWS WAF incur no request fees or data transfer charges
AWS WAF continues billing for evaluating and blocking these requests

sources.title: Restrict access to Application Load Balancers
supports: An internal Application Load Balancer in private subnets can be used through VPC origins

For an internet-facing load balancer: CloudFront adds a secret custom header to origin requests and the listener forwards only requests that carry it, answering 403 otherwise; HTTPS is required for the header to stay secret
Optionally the load balancer's security group admits only the AWS-managed prefix list for CloudFront

sources.title: Restrict access with VPC origins
supports: Application Load Balancers, Network Load Balancers and EC2 instances in private subnets can be VPC origins, making CloudFront the single point of entry

The VPC needs an internet gateway although it is not used for routing to the origin; the origin's security group must admit the CloudFront managed prefix list or the service-managed security group CloudFront-VPCOrigins-Service-SG
Supported Regions include ap-northeast-1 except the Availability Zone apne1-az3
VPC origins do not support gRPC or Lambda@Edge origin request and origin response triggers

sources.title: Restrict access to an AWS Lambda function URL origin
supports: Origin access control for a function URL needs AuthType AWS_IAM and permissions for cloudfront.amazonaws.com on lambda:InvokeFunctionUrl and lambda:InvokeFunction, conditioned on the distribution's ARN
With PUT or POST the caller must send the SHA256 of the body in the x-amz-content-sha256 header; Lambda does not support unsigned payloads

sources.title: Locations and IP address ranges of CloudFront edge servers
supports: The managed prefix lists com.amazonaws.global.cloudfront.origin-facing (IPv4) and com.amazonaws.global.ipv6.cloudfront.origin-facing (IPv6) contain the ranges of CloudFront's origin-facing servers

sources.title: AWS-managed prefix lists
supports: The CloudFront managed prefix list has a weight of 55: in a security group, whose default quota is 60 rules, it leaves room for 5 more

sources.title: Use managed cache policies
supports: CachingOptimized includes no query strings or cookies in the cache key, only the normalized Accept-Encoding header; minimum TTL 1 second, default TTL 86,400 seconds
The ID of CachingOptimized is 658327ea-f89d-4fab-a63d-7e88639e58f6

sources.title: Request and response behavior for custom origins
supports: When simultaneous requests for the same object arrive at an edge location before the first response, CloudFront pauses and sends the response of the first request to all of them (request collapsing), only for requests that share a cache key
The CachingDisabled policy prevents request collapsing

sources.title: CloudFront flat-rate pricing plans
supports: Plans (Free, Pro, Business, Premium) have a monthly price with no overage charges regardless of traffic spikes or attacks; blocked DDoS attacks and requests blocked by AWS WAF never count against the usage allowance
Monthly allowances: 1 M requests and 100 GB (Free), 10 M and 50 TB (Pro), 125 M and 50 TB (Business), 500 M and 50 TB (Premium)
Usage above the allowance is not billed; sustained excess can lead to traffic being served from fewer or more distant edge locations
A distribution with Shield Advanced enabled is not eligible; an account using AWS Free Tier is not eligible; a web ACL must be associated; at most 3 Free plans per account
A plan covers one distribution; other costs, such as Lambda@Edge invocations, are billed separately

sources.title: AWS Price List: CloudFrontPlans

sources.title: Choosing workflow type in Step Functions
supports: The workflow type cannot be changed after a state machine is created

Standard: up to one year, exactly-once workflow execution unless Retry is specified in ASL, execution state persisted between state transitions, history retrievable through the API for 90 days after completion, billed by state transition

Express: up to five minutes, billed by number of executions, duration and memory; asynchronous Express is at-least-once, synchronous Express is at-most-once; execution state is not persisted between transitions and history is not captured by Step Functions
Express Workflows do not support the .sync and .waitForTaskToken integration patterns, Distributed Map, or activities
For Standard, starting an execution with the name of a running one returns an idempotent response; for Express, the same name results in concurrent executions

sources.title: Transforming data with JSONata in Step Functions
supports: Step Functions implements JSONata based on the 2.0.6 specification; $eval is not available, $parse replaces it
When creating a workflow in the console, AWS recommends JSONata as the top-level QueryLanguage; without the field the default is JSONPath
JSONata states use Arguments and Output in place of InputPath, Parameters, ResultSelector, ResultPath and OutputPath, and a string is an expression only when it starts with {% and ends with %}
$states holds input, result, errorOutput (in a Catch) and context
An expression that returns no value, a type error, an evaluation longer than one second, and exceeded memory all raise States.QueryEvaluationError, which Retry and Catch can name
Step Functions adds $partition, $range, $hash, $random, $uuid and $parse
A Choice rule in JSONata has a Condition

sources.title: Passing data between states with variables
supports: Assign is available on Pass, Task, Map, Parallel, Choice and Wait states, and inside Catch and Choice rules
All expressions in an Assign are evaluated with the values on state entry, then assigned; the new values are visible from the next state
Assign and Output are processed in parallel
A variable is at most 256 KiB, all variables in one Assign at most 256 KiB together, and all stored variables at most 10 MiB per execution
Parallel branches and Map iterations read outer variables and keep their own; a Distributed Map cannot reference outer variables

sources.title: Amazon States Language (specification)
supports: In JSONata states a Catcher may have Output and Assign, which may reference $states.errorOutput; without Output the state output is the Error Output, an object with Error and usually Cause
When a state reports an error, the matching Catcher's Assign is evaluated and the state's top-level Assign is not
ItemSelector overrides each item of a Map; $states.context.Map.Item.Value and .Index describe the item
A MaxConcurrency of 1 processes the items in order
sources.note: The specification states the default of a missing Output twice and differently: "the result in a Task, Map, and Parallel State" in the section on Arguments and Output, and "the Task State copies its input through to its output" in the section on the Task state. The chapter's definitions write Output in every Task and Map so that neither reading matters.

sources.title: Discover service integration patterns in Step Functions
supports: Three patterns: Request Response, Run a Job (.sync), Wait for a Callback with Task Token (.waitForTaskToken), chosen by the suffix of Resource
AWS SDK integrations: Request Response in Standard and Express, .waitForTaskToken in Standard, no .sync
Optimized DynamoDB supports Request Response only; SQS, SNS and Lambda support Request Response and, in Standard, the callback; Step Functions, ECS, and others support .sync
A task waiting for a token waits until the execution reaches one year unless HeartbeatSeconds or TimeoutSeconds is set
If a task using a callback token times out, a new random token is generated
Task tokens must be returned by principals in the same account
A .sync task that is aborted is cancelled on a best-effort basis; .sync polling consumes API quota

sources.title: Handling errors in Step Functions workflows
supports: Retrier fields and defaults: IntervalSeconds 1, MaxAttempts 3 (0 never retries), BackoffRate 2.0, MaxDelaySeconds, JitterStrategy FULL or NONE (default NONE; FULL randomizes each interval between 0 and its computed value)
A retrier's counters apply across all visits to it within one state execution (the page's complex retry scenario: ErrorA, ErrorB, ErrorC, ErrorB)
States.ALL matches every known error name except States.Runtime and States.DataLimitExceeded, must be alone and last; States.TaskFailed matches every error except States.Timeout
Retries are treated as state transitions
Catchers exist for Task, Parallel and Map states, not for the execution as a whole
The page lists States.HeartbeatTimeout as the error of a missed heartbeat

sources.title: Task workflow state
supports: TimeoutSeconds and HeartbeatSeconds both default to 99,999,999; HeartbeatSeconds must be smaller than TimeoutSeconds
The page says a missed heartbeat fails the task with States.Timeout
The optimized Lambda integration is arn:aws:states:::lambda:invoke; a function ARN as Resource is the legacy form
Arguments and Output are the JSONata fields of a Task
sources.note: Two pages name the error of a missed heartbeat differently (States.Timeout here and on the integration patterns page, States.HeartbeatTimeout on the error handling page). The chapter's Retry names both.

sources.title: Learning to use AWS service SDK integrations in Step Functions
supports: The Resource of an SDK integration is arn:aws:states:::aws-sdk:serviceName:apiAction, with parameters in PascalCase

The error name of an SDK integration is ServiceName.ErrorName with the suffix Exception added even when the service's own name lacks it (S3.BucketAlreadyExistsException); the exception prefix of Amazon S3 is S3
Step Functions cannot generate IAM policies for SDK integrations

sources.title: Retry behavior - AWS SDKs and Tools Reference Guide
supports: The behaviour the page describes requires opting in with AWS_NEW_RETRIES_2026=true until it becomes the default; without it the SDK uses pre-2026 retry behaviour
Retry modes standard and adaptive; legacy is not available in JavaScript; adaptive is not recommended as a general default
AWS_RETRY_MODE / retry_mode and AWS_MAX_ATTEMPTS / max_attempts, and the precedence code, environment, shared config file, default
Under the 2026 behaviour: base delay 50 ms for transient errors and 1,000 ms for throttling, cap 20 seconds, full jitter
Under the 2026 behaviour: retry quota of 500 tokens, 14 per transient retry, 5 per throttling retry, 1 restored by a success without retry
Under the 2026 behaviour: DynamoDB and DynamoDB Streams clients default to 4 max attempts with a 25 ms transient base delay
x-amz-retry-after is a delay in milliseconds, clamped between the computed backoff and that plus 5,000 ms
The token budget is typically scoped to a single client instance
sources.note: The page describes the opt-in behaviour only. The pre-2026 numbers in the chapter (100 ms, 500 ms, costs 10 and 5) are from the installed @smithy/core 3.35.2, not from this page.

submodules/retry/util-retry/StandardRetryStrategy.js: capacity 500, refusal by error type, attempts, then capacity; retry-after hint clamped to computed delay + 5,000 ms
submodules/retry/service-error-classification: the throttling codes, the transient codes and statuses 500, 502, 503, 504, and that 429 or $retryable.throttling is throttling

submodules/retry/middleware-retry/retryMiddleware.js: amz-sdk-invocation-id and amz-sdk-request headers, $metadata.attempts and totalRetryDelay, a streaming payload is not retried, step finalizeRequest with priority high
submodules/client/middleware-stack/MiddlewareStack.js: the five steps and three priorities
submodules/client/smithy-client/defaults-mode.js and config/defaults-mode: defaultsMode is legacy when unset and then sets no timeout
submodules/client/util-waiter: minDelay, maxDelay, maxWaitTime, exponential backoff with jitter between polls, TimeoutError and AbortError

sources.title: Considerations and limitations for CTAS queries
supports: If the workgroup overrides the client-side setting for the query results location, Athena creates a CTAS table under <results location>/tables/<query-id>/
external_location must be empty; CTAS never overwrites data
A failed CTAS or INSERT INTO can leave orphaned data files that later queries read; the data manifest file lists them; Iceberg is recommended for atomic transactions
CTAS ignores ORDER BY; Parquet is the default format with GZIP as the default compression; a partitioned CTAS writes at most 100 partitions

sources.title: CREATE TABLE AS
supports: A CTAS query that specifies external_location in a workgroup that enforces a query results location fails with an error
table_type is HIVE or ICEBERG, default HIVE; for Iceberg, is_external must be false and location is required; partitioned_by does not apply to Iceberg tables, partitioning does

sources.title: INSERT INTO
supports: Each INSERT operation creates a new file rather than appending to an existing one; Athena does not rewrite or modify existing files
INSERT INTO writes at most 100 partitions, is not supported on bucketed tables or for federated queries, and expects the partition column last in the SELECT list
Supported formats include Parquet with ParquetHiveSerDe and JSON with the Hive JsonSerDe
Athena writes a data manifest file for each INSERT query to the query result location

sources.title: UNLOAD
supports: UNLOAD writes the result of a SELECT as Parquet, ORC, Avro, JSON or text files without creating a table; SELECT itself only produces CSV
Except when writing to partitions, the TO location must hold no data; UNLOAD does not overwrite
Files are written in parallel with no ordering between them; orphaned data is not deleted on failure; at most 100 partitions; UNLOAD can be used with prepared statements

sources.title: Use parameterized queries (with the pages on execution parameters and prepared statements)
supports: Parameterized queries help prevent SQL injection; they are execution parameters in any DML query, or PREPARE and EXECUTE statements
Execution parameters are not workgroup specific; prepared statements are, and a workgroup holds at most 1,000 of them
Parameterized queries are supported only for SELECT, INSERT INTO, CTAS and UNLOAD statements
Parameters are positional question marks, cannot be placed in quotes, and a value to be treated as a string must be enclosed in single quotes; CAST can be used in a value
The CLI passes the values in --execution-parameters
sources.note: Also read: querying-with-prepared-statements-querying-using-execution-parameters.html, ...-using-the-aws-cli.html, querying-with-prepared-statements-querying.html and ...-sql-statements.html.

sources.title: Configure access to prepared statements
supports: PREPARE needs athena:CreatePreparedStatement, EXECUTE needs athena:GetPreparedStatement, each with athena:StartQueryExecution, on the workgroup

sources.title: SELECT (escaping single quotes)
supports: To escape a single quote, precede it with another single quote, as in 'O''Reilly'

sources.title: Escape reserved keywords in queries
supports: Reserved keywords are escaped with backticks in DDL statements and with double quotes in SELECT statements
AT is in neither list

sources.title: Reuse query results in Athena
supports: Reuse is enabled per query; Athena looks for a previous execution of the same query in the same workgroup and returns its result without running the query
The default maximum age is 60 minutes and the largest is 7 days; Athena does not check for changes in the source data within that age, so stale results can be returned
The caller must have access to the tables and to the S3 location of the stored result

Not reused: non-deterministic queries such as LIMIT without ORDER BY, statements other than SELECT and EXECUTE, federated catalogs, tables under Lake Formation, and workgroups with managed query results

sources.title: Managed query results
supports: A workgroup can store query results in Athena-managed storage instead of an S3 bucket of yours; results are kept 24 hours at no cost and then deleted
Managed query results do not support query result reuse; access is through GetQueryResults on the workgroup

sources.title: Query Apache Iceberg tables
supports: Athena performs read, time travel, write and DDL queries on Iceberg tables; it creates and operates on Iceberg v2 tables only
Only Iceberg tables in the AWS Glue catalog are supported, with AWS Glue optimistic locking only
Parquet, ORC and Avro files are supported; timestamps have millisecond precision in Athena

sources.title: Create Iceberg tables
supports: CREATE TABLE … PARTITIONED BY (col | transform) LOCATION … TBLPROPERTIES ('table_type'='ICEBERG'); CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE is an error for Iceberg
Partition columns are declared among the columns first and named in PARTITIONED BY without a type
Table properties and defaults: format parquet, vacuum_min_snapshots_to_keep 1, vacuum_max_snapshot_age_seconds 432000 (5 days), optimize_rewrite_delete_file_threshold 2

sources.title: Update Iceberg table data
supports: INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE each produce a new snapshot; UPDATE and DELETE write position delete files and enforce snapshot isolation
Athena always uses merge-on-read for UPDATE, MERGE INTO and DELETE FROM, whatever the table properties say

sources.title: MERGE INTO
supports: MERGE INTO target [AS alias] USING { source_table | query } [AS alias] ON condition, with WHEN MATCHED THEN DELETE or UPDATE and WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN INSERT (…) VALUES (…)
MERGE INTO is transactional and supported only for Iceberg tables in engine version 3
An error is raised when a single target row matches more than one source row

sources.title: Perform time travel and version travel queries
supports: SELECT … FROM table FOR TIMESTAMP AS OF timestamp reads a consistent snapshot as of that time; FOR VERSION AS OF takes a snapshot ID
The example uses FOR TIMESTAMP AS OF (current_timestamp - interval '1' day)

sources.title: Optimize Iceberg tables (with the OPTIMIZE and VACUUM statement pages)
supports: OPTIMIZE table REWRITE DATA USING BIN_PACK [WHERE predicate] rewrites data files by size and by the number of delete files; only partition columns are allowed in WHERE; it is charged by the data scanned during the rewrite
VACUUM table expires snapshots and removes orphan files; expired snapshots can no longer be reached by time travel; its S3 requests are charged
VACUUM needs s3:DeleteObject on the table's location; without it the query succeeds but the files are not deleted; it fails if the table sits at the root of a bucket
sources.note: Also read: optimize-statement.html and vacuum-statement.html.

sources.title: Evolve Iceberg table schema
supports: Iceberg schema updates are metadata-only changes: no data files are changed; add, drop, rename, reorder and some type promotions are supported

sources.title: Register S3 table bucket catalogs and query Tables from Athena
supports: S3 table buckets store Iceberg tables and automate compaction, snapshot management and garbage collection
From Athena, OPTIMIZE and VACUUM are not supported on S3 Tables: maintenance is managed in S3
The tables are reached through a Glue catalog named s3tablescatalog/<bucket>, with s3tables permissions or Lake Formation
sources.note: S3 Tables prices were not read for this chapter.

sources.title: Use Amazon Athena Federated Query
supports: Federated query runs SQL across sources other than S3 through data source connectors; Athena data catalog connectors need a Lambda function in your account
Starting April 21, 2026, certain newly created connectors are registered as Glue Data Catalogs and use no Lambda function in your account

sources.title: Manage query processing capacity
supports: A capacity reservation holds a number of DPUs for the workgroups assigned to it; the minimum is 4 DPUs
DML queries use between 4 and 124 DPUs and DDL queries 4

sources.title: Service Quotas (Athena)
supports: The maximum query string length is 262,144 bytes
Active DML and DDL query quotas count both running and queued queries; the DML query timeout can be raised to at most 240 minutes
sources.note: Quotas as read on 2026-10-13. The default values are in the Service Quotas console and were not copied.

sources.title: StartQueryExecution (Athena API Reference)
supports: ClientRequestToken makes the request idempotent: a repeated request returns the same response and creates no other query; an error is returned if a parameter such as QueryString changed; 32 to 128 characters; SDKs generate one when it is left out
ExecutionParameters is a list of strings of 1 to 1,024 characters applied in order; QueryString is at most 262,144 characters
ResultReuseConfiguration holds ResultReuseByAgeConfiguration with Enabled and MaxAgeInMinutes (0 to 10080, default 60)
sources.note: Also read: API_ResultReuseByAgeConfiguration.html and API_StopQueryExecution.html.

sources.title: QueryExecutionStatus and QueryExecutionStatistics (Athena API Reference)
supports: State is QUEUED, RUNNING, SUCCEEDED, FAILED or CANCELLED; for certain transient errors the state goes from RUNNING back to QUEUED; FAILED is always terminal
Statistics hold DataScannedInBytes, ResultReuseInformation and DataManifestLocation
sources.note: Also read: API_QueryExecutionStatistics.html and API_GetQueryExecution.html.

sources.title: GetQueryResults (Athena API Reference)
supports: GetQueryResults streams the results from the query results location and pages with NextToken, at most 1,000 rows a request
The caller also needs s3:GetObject on the results location; anyone with s3:GetObject there can read results from S3 without the Athena permission
sources.note: The page does not say that the first row of a SELECT result repeats the column names.

sources.title: Example workgroup policies
supports: Athena actions on queries, named queries and prepared statements are granted on the workgroup's ARN, arn:aws:athena:<region>:<account>:workgroup/<name>
The example for running queries in one workgroup notes that it does not deny access to other workgroups

sources.title: Configure access to databases and tables in the AWS Glue Data Catalog
supports: Access is limited at the database and table level, not per partition; an action on a table also needs permission on its database and on the catalog
The CREATE TABLE example grants glue:GetDatabase, glue:GetTables, glue:GetTable, glue:GetPartitions and glue:CreateTable

sources.title: Control access to Amazon S3 from Athena
supports: A user's permissions pass through Athena: the user must be allowed to read the S3 buckets to query them
aws:SourceIp, aws:SourceVpc and aws:SourceVpce cannot be used to restrict Athena's access to S3

sources.title: Partition your data
supports: Partitioning restricts the data each query scans; with a partition column in the WHERE clause Athena scans only that partition's data

sources.title: Optimize data (with Optimize queries)
supports: With a columnar format, reading fewer columns reduces the data read from S3; many small files hurt, columnar files most of all
Most compression formats must be read from the beginning, so compressed text files cannot in general be processed in parallel
ORDER BY with LIMIT is run as a top N query
sources.note: Also read: performance-tuning-query-optimization-techniques.html. Neither page says that LIMIT reduces the bytes scanned, or that it does not.

sources.title: Identify query output files
supports: A query leaves <QueryID>.csv and <QueryID>.csv.metadata in the result location, and statements that write data leave <QueryID>-manifest.csv

sources.title: Create the table for CloudTrail logs in Athena using partition projection
supports: The CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE statement stored in examples/49-athena/sql/cloudtrail.sql, with the placeholders amzn-s3-demo-bucket, account-id, aws-region and the start date

sources.title: Create the table for ALB access logs
supports: The CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE statement stored in examples/49-athena/sql/alb.sql; the trailing ?( .*)? of the regular expression should stay so that new fields do not break the table

sources.title: Create a table for CloudFront standard logs (legacy)
supports: The CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE statement stored in examples/49-athena/sql/cloudfront.sql, for tab-separated standard logs with two header lines
sources.note: The same guide has separate pages for CloudFront logs delivered as Parquet; they were not read.

sources.title: Using Amazon S3 server access logs to identify requests
supports: The CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE statement with date-based partitioning stored in examples/49-athena/sql/s3-access.sql

sources.title: Cloudflare Basin SQL (formerly R2 SQL): overview and SQL reference
supports: Basin SQL, formerly R2 SQL, is generally available and queries Apache Iceberg tables managed by Basin Catalog

Its SQL reference documents SELECT with joins and set operations, SHOW, DESCRIBE and EXPLAIN, and no INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, MERGE or CREATE TABLE AS; it mentions no query parameters; the default LIMIT is 500 rows

sources.title: Vercel Query
supports: Query builds metric queries from form fields or an AI assistant, over Vercel's own observability events, and exports results as CSV or JSON; full access requires Observability Plus on Pro or Enterprise
The page describes no SQL interface and no way to query files of your own

sources.title: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore: Overview
supports: The page lists these services by name: Harness, Runtime, Memory, Gateway, Identity, Code Interpreter, Browser, Observability, Payments, Evaluations, Optimization, Policy, Registry
Runtime is described as a secure, serverless runtime environment purpose-built for deploying and scaling dynamic AI agents and tools, with true session isolation and built-in identity
Gateway converts APIs, Lambda functions, and existing services into MCP-compatible tools and connects to pre-existing MCP servers
AgentCore offers consumption-based pricing with no upfront commitments or minimum fees
AgentCore services work together or independently with any open-source framework and with any foundation model

sources.title: AgentCore: Supported AWS Regions
supports: Asia Pacific (Tokyo) is listed as supported for harness, Runtime microVMs, Runtime Instances, Memory, Gateway, Identity, Built-in Tools, Observability, Policy, Evaluations, optimization, AWS Agent Registry and the Web Search Tool
AgentCore payments is not listed as supported in Asia Pacific (Tokyo)

sources.title: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore pricing
supports: Runtime microVMs: v1 USD 0.0895 per vCPU-hour and USD 0.00945 per GB-hour; v2 USD 0.1276 per vCPU-hour and USD 0.0169 per GB-hour (consumption)

CPU is not charged during I/O wait; billing is per second with a 1-second minimum and a 128 MB memory minimum, over the whole session from microVM ready until session termination, idle periods included
With v2, idle memory is reclaimed after 120 seconds
Gateway: USD 0.005 per 1,000 API invocations, USD 0.025 per 1,000 search invocations, USD 0.02 per 100 tools indexed per month
Identity: USD 0.010 per 1,000 tokens or API keys requested for non-AWS resources, and no additional charge when used through Runtime or Gateway

Short-term memory: USD 0.25 per 1,000 new events through 2026-10-05; from 2026-10-06 USD 1.00 per GB ingested, USD 0.20 per GB retrieved, USD 0.10 per GB-month stored, each event billed at a minimum of 12 KB
Observability is charged under Amazon CloudWatch pricing

sources.title: Quotas for Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
supports: Active session workloads per account: 5,000 in us-east-1 and us-west-2, 2,500 in other Regions, adjustable
Maximum hardware allocation per session 2 vCPU / 8 GB; request timeout 15 minutes; maximum payload 100 MB; streaming maximum duration 60 minutes
Direct code deployment package: 250 MB compressed, 750 MB uncompressed; Docker image 2 GB
Data plane API request rate 1,000 TPS per account; new Runtime session creation rate 25 TPS per account
Idle session timeout 15 minutes and maximum session duration 8 hours, both adjustable through LifecycleConfiguration
Memory: 100 messages per CreateEvent, 5 CreateEvent requests per second per actor per session with conversational payloads, minimum EventExpirationDuration 7 days and maximum 365
sources.note: The CreateMemory API reference gives 3 as the minimum of eventExpiryDuration; this page says 7. The stack uses 30.

sources.title: Host agent or tools with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Runtime
supports: Each user session runs in a dedicated microVM with isolated CPU, memory, and filesystem; after session completion the microVM is terminated and memory is sanitized
Two compute types: microVMs and Instances; sessions run up to 8 hours on microVMs and up to 14 days on Instances
Works with frameworks such as LangGraph, Strands and CrewAI, and with custom agents that do not use a specific framework
A newer platform version, V2, starts the agent from a snapshot

sources.title: AgentCore Runtime: microVMs (key components, platform versions)
supports: A runtime has immutable versions; a DEFAULT endpoint is created with the runtime and follows the latest version
platformVersion is V1 or V2 and V1 is the default; V2 is available in us-east-1, us-east-2, us-west-2, eu-west-1 and ap-northeast-1
On V2 create and update take minutes and the container must report healthy within 120 seconds
AWS CloudFormation and the AWS CDK do not currently support setting platformVersion
sources.note: aws-cdk-lib 2.273.0 does declare a platformVersion property on CfnRuntime. The stack leaves it unset.

sources.title: AgentCore Runtime: HTTP protocol contract
supports: The agent listens on host 0.0.0.0, port 8080
POST /invocations takes JSON and answers JSON or text/event-stream
GET /ping answers a JSON body whose status is Healthy or HealthyBusy; while HealthyBusy the session is considered active
A 4xx or 5xx from the agent is returned to the caller as 424 RuntimeClientError
Without an Authorization header an OAuth-configured runtime answers 401 with a WWW-Authenticate header

sources.title: AgentCore Runtime service contract
supports: Supported protocols are HTTP (port 8080), MCP (port 8000, /mcp), A2A (port 9000) and AG-UI (port 8080)

sources.title: Use isolated sessions for agents
supports: AgentCore does not enforce session-to-user mappings; the client backend should maintain the relationship between users and their session IDs
A session is created on the first invoke with a runtimeSessionId provided by the application, of at least 33 characters
A session's compute stops after inactivity (default 15 minutes) or at the maximum lifetime (default 8 hours); the next invocation with the same ID provisions new compute
Data in memory or on disk persists only for the compute lifecycle; AgentCore Memory is the documented place for what must outlive it
The session header for HTTP is X-Amzn-Bedrock-AgentCore-Runtime-Session-Id

sources.title: Authenticate and authorize with Inbound Auth and Outbound Auth
supports: A runtime supports either IAM SigV4 or JWT bearer token inbound auth, not both at once
The JWT authorizer takes a discovery URL, allowed audiences, allowed clients, allowed scopes and required custom claims; allowedClients is checked against the client_id claim
The X-Amzn-Bedrock-AgentCore-Runtime-User-Id header is not verified against an authenticated identity and needs bedrock-agentcore:InvokeAgentRuntimeForUser
The Authorization header can be passed to the agent through the request header allowlist, and the agent may skip signature validation because the runtime has already validated the token
The invoke URL for a bearer token is https://bedrock-agentcore.<region>.amazonaws.com/runtimes/<escaped ARN>/invocations?qualifier=DEFAULT
Agents created on or after 2025-10-13 get workload identity permissions from a service-linked role

sources.title: Pass custom headers to Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Runtime
supports: Up to 20 headers per runtime, each value at most 4 KB
The Authorization header can be allowlisted only when the runtime has a customJWTAuthorizer; it is then validated and forwarded to the agent code

sources.title: Security best practices for AgentCore Runtime
supports: Any code running inside the microVM can obtain the execution role's credentials from the metadata service
Session-to-user mapping, input validation and prompt injection prevention are the customer's responsibility
The prompt field should be enforced to be a string, because a framework may dispatch a toolUse block found in the input
Add aws:SourceArn and aws:SourceAccount conditions to the execution role's trust policy

sources.title: IAM Permissions for AgentCore Runtime
supports: The execution role trusts bedrock-agentcore.amazonaws.com with aws:SourceAccount and aws:SourceArn conditions
The listed execution role statements include logs actions on /aws/bedrock-agentcore/runtimes/*, X-Ray actions on *, and cloudwatch:PutMetricData limited to the bedrock-agentcore namespace
sources.note: The stack omits the X-Ray statements and logs:PutResourcePolicy, because it enables neither tracing nor log delivery. Whether a runtime starts without them was not tried.

sources.title: API reference: CreateAgentRuntime
supports: agentRuntimeName matches [a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9_]{0,47}
environmentVariables: at most 50 entries
requestHeaderConfiguration and platformVersion are request fields

sources.title: API reference: LifecycleConfiguration
supports: idleRuntimeSessionTimeout and maxLifetime are seconds, minimum 60 and maximum 1,209,600, defaults 900 and 28,800

sources.title: API reference: CreateMemory
supports: name and eventExpiryDuration are required; memoryStrategies is optional; eventExpiryDuration ranges from 3 to 365

sources.title: AgentCore Runtime: direct code deployment
supports: Direct code deployment packages are limited to 250 MB where container images can be up to 2 GB
With direct code deployment AWS patches the language runtime; with containers only the compute kernel

sources.title: AgentCore Runtime: direct code deployment for Node.js
supports: The entry point is a .js file that implements the /invocations POST and /ping GET endpoints; dependencies may be vendored or bundled into a single .js file with esbuild
AgentCore Runtime does not run TypeScript files natively
AgentCore Runtime only supports the arm64 instruction set architecture
ADOT instrumentation is only compatible with CommonJS module output

sources.title: Supported runtimes for code deployment
supports: Supported runtimes are Python 3.10 to 3.14 and Node.js 22 (NODE_22) on Amazon Linux 2023

sources.title: AgentCore CLI reference
supports: The CLI creates agents in Python or TypeScript, and builds a CodeZip or a Container

sources.title: AgentCore Memory: memory types
supports: Short-term memory is the events of a session, read back with ListEvents
Long-term memory generation is an asynchronous process that runs in the background

sources.title: AgentCore Memory: terminology
supports: An event is the fundamental unit of short-term memory, organized by actorId and sessionId, immutable and timestamped

sources.title: AgentCore Memory: built-in strategies
supports: The built-in strategies are user preferences, semantic, session summaries and episodic

sources.title: AgentCore Memory: fine-grained access control through a gateway
supports: IAM controls on Memory match the IAM principal that calls Memory and cannot express a rule keyed on an OAuth or JWT identity
The documented way to bind actorId to the JWT sub claim is Memory behind a Gateway with a policy

sources.title: Service Authorization Reference: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
supports: Condition keys bedrock-agentcore:actorId, sessionId, namespace and strategyId exist; CreateEvent and ListEvents support actorId and sessionId
CreateEvent, ListEvents, InvokeAgentRuntime and InvokeAgentRuntimeForUser are separate actions

sources.title: AgentCore Gateway: supported targets
supports: Targets are grouped as MCP targets (Lambda functions, API Gateway REST API stages, OpenAPI schemas, Smithy models, MCP servers, integration templates, connectors), HTTP targets (AgentCore Runtime, HTTP passthrough) and inference targets

sources.title: AgentCore Gateway: Lambda function targets
supports: The Lambda event is a map of the tool's input properties, and context.client_context.custom carries bedrockAgentCoreToolName, bedrockAgentCoreGatewayId, bedrockAgentCoreTargetId and message IDs
No key that identifies the end user is listed

sources.title: AgentCore Gateway: header propagation
supports: The Authorization header cannot be allowlisted on a target, and is forwarded to the target only when an interceptor Lambda provides it

sources.title: AgentCore Gateway: tool naming
supports: A tool is exposed as <target name>___<tool name>

sources.title: AgentCore Gateway: inbound authorization
supports: Inbound authorization is a JWT, an IAM identity, or offloaded (authenticate only, or no authorization)

sources.title: AgentCore Gateway: outbound authorization
supports: Lambda, API Gateway and Smithy targets support only the gateway service role (GATEWAY_IAM_ROLE) for outbound authorization

sources.title: AgentCore Identity: get a workload access token
supports: A workload access token is an AWS-signed opaque token for AgentCore's own services, such as outbound credential providers, and cannot be used for external services
GetWorkloadAccessTokenForJWT validates the token and identifies the user by its iss and sub claims; GetWorkloadAccessTokenForUserId treats the user ID as an opaque string it cannot verify

sources.title: AgentCore Identity: terminology
supports: A workload identity represents a logical application or workload; the token vault releases a credential only to the agent and user combination that obtained it

sources.title: AgentCore Observability: service-provided data
supports: Metrics are provided by default; spans and logs for an agent require explicit enablement
Viewing service-generated spans and traces needs CloudWatch Transaction Search turned on once; fuller data needs the code instrumented with the ADOT SDK

sources.title: AgentCore Observability: view data
supports: Standard output of a runtime goes to the log group /aws/bedrock-agentcore/runtimes/<agent_id>-<endpoint_name>

sources.title: What is the Amazon Chime SDK?
supports: The Amazon Chime SDK is a set of real-time communications components for messaging, audio, video, and screen sharing in web or mobile applications
Pay-for-use pricing with no upfront fees; messaging, media pipelines, speech enhancement and PSTN audio are priced separately

sources.title: Using the Amazon Chime SDK (prerequisites, concepts, architecture)
supports: The SDK works independently of any Amazon Chime administrator account
A server application manages meeting and attendee resources; a client application uses them to make media connections

A meeting is an ephemeral resource; an attendee is identified by an AttendeeId; a join token is an opaque secret the server must transfer securely to the client authorized to join on behalf of the attendee
Clients signal over secure WebSockets and DTLS; audio is mixed by the service; video is forwarded by an SFU, up to 25 simultaneous videos per meeting
Data messages of up to 2 KB; quotas are per API endpoint
Supported browsers for the JavaScript client library

sources.title: Creating meetings using the Amazon Chime SDK
supports: The server calls CreateMeeting with a MediaRegion and CreateAttendee, and transfers both to the client
A meeting ends on DeleteMeeting, when it exceeds 24 hours, or when no attendees are connected for five continuous minutes

sources.title: Using meeting Regions for Amazon Chime SDK meetings
supports: Control Regions have the API endpoint; media Regions host the meetings; a control Region can create a meeting in any media Region of the same partition
A meeting can be updated only in the control Region that created it, and its events are delivered there
AWS recommends always specifying MediaRegion; https://nearest-media-region.l.chime.aws returns the nearest one

sources.title: Available AWS Regions for the Amazon Chime SDK
supports: Asia Pacific (Tokyo) is both a meeting control Region and a meeting media Region

sources.title: Amazon Chime SDK endpoints and quotas
supports: meetings-chime.ap-northeast-1.amazonaws.com is an endpoint
Defaults: 250 concurrent meetings (adjustable), 250 attendees per meeting (not adjustable), 25 published video streams per meeting
CreateMeeting, CreateAttendee, DeleteAttendee, DeleteMeeting and GetMeeting each default to 10 requests per second

sources.title: Amazon Chime SDK API: CreateMeeting
supports: ClientRequestToken, ExternalMeetingId and MediaRegion are required; the list of media Regions
'Use a different token for different meetings'

sources.title: Amazon Chime SDK API: CreateAttendee
supports: ExternalUserId is 2 to 64 characters of a fixed pattern, may not begin with aws:, and 'links the attendee to an identity managed by a builder application'
NotFoundException when the meeting does not exist; ThrottlingException is HTTP 429

sources.title: Amazon Chime SDK API: Attendee
supports: The JoinToken lets a client authenticate and join as the attendee
The JoinToken expires when the meeting ends or when DeleteAttendee is called
AWS recommends transferring each JoinToken so that no client but the authorized one has it

sources.title: Amazon Chime SDK API: DeleteAttendee
supports: Deletes the attendee and their JoinToken; attendees are deleted automatically when the meeting is deleted

sources.title: Amazon Chime SDK API: DeleteMeeting
supports: Deletes all attendees, disconnects all clients, and prevents new clients from joining

sources.title: Amazon Chime SDK API: GetMeeting
supports: Returns the meeting details by MeetingId; NotFoundException is among its errors

The Meetings namespace is the one to use when starting today; its endpoint is https://meetings-chime.<region>.amazonaws.com

sources.title: Understanding Amazon Chime SDK meeting lifecycle events
supports: Events go to EventBridge, SNS or SQS with source aws.chime and detail-type 'Chime Meeting State Change'
chime:AttendeeAuthorized is sent when a user already in the meeting joins again with the same join token: the meeting is handed off to the new device
chime:AttendeeDropped is sent when the service receives no packets for 10 to 15 seconds; AttendeeLeft and AttendeeDropped are never both sent for one leave
chime:MeetingEnded is also sent on DeleteMeeting

The IAM action prefix is chime: for the meetings namespace as well
