sources.title: Cloudflare R2: Bucket locks
supports: Bucket lock rules prevent the deletion and overwriting of objects for a number of days, until a date, or indefinitely
A rule can be removed from the dashboard, with wrangler r2 bucket lock remove, or by leaving it out of an updated configuration; the page describes no mode that the bucket's owner cannot remove

sources.title: Vercel Blob
supports: put() refuses an existing pathname unless allowOverwrite is set; del() deletes; the overview page describes no retention lock
Vercel Blob stores its data in Amazon S3
sources.note: Only the overview page (last updated 2026-08-26) was read.

sources.title: Multi-AZ DB instance deployments for Amazon RDS
supports: A Multi-AZ DB instance deployment keeps a synchronous standby replica in another Availability Zone
The standby cannot serve read traffic
Synchronous replication can raise write and commit latency compared with Single-AZ

sources.title: Failing over a Multi-AZ DB instance for Amazon RDS
supports: Failover times are typically 60-120 seconds, longer with large transactions or a lengthy recovery
Failover changes the DNS record of the DB instance to point to the standby, and existing connections must be re-established
The listed reasons for a failover include OS patching, an unhealthy or unreachable primary host, a customer modification, a storage failure, and a reboot with failover

sources.title: Best practices for Amazon RDS
supports: A client that caches DNS should use a TTL of less than 30 seconds, because the address of a DB instance can change after a failover
Test failover to learn how long it takes for your use case

sources.title: Multi-AZ DB cluster deployments for Amazon RDS
supports: A Multi-AZ DB cluster has one writer and two readable DB instances in three Availability Zones
Replication is semisynchronous: a commit needs the acknowledgment of at least one reader
Supported instance classes are db.c6gd, db.m5d, db.m6gd, db.m6id, db.m6idn, db.m8gd, db.r5d, db.r6gd, db.r6id, db.r6idn, db.r8gd and db.x2iedn
Multi-AZ DB clusters are not Aurora DB clusters

sources.title: Failing over a Multi-AZ DB cluster for Amazon RDS
supports: Failover times are typically under 35 seconds

sources.title: Limitations of Multi-AZ DB clusters for Amazon RDS
supports: Multi-AZ DB clusters cannot be stopped and started, and do not support storage autoscaling by a maximum allocated storage

sources.title: Working with DB instance read replicas
supports: Updates to the primary DB instance are copied asynchronously to a read replica
RDS does not autoscale read replicas

sources.title: Creating a read replica
supports: Automatic backups must be enabled on the source DB instance (a backup retention period other than 0) before a read replica can be created
The same or a larger instance class and storage type than the source is recommended for a replica

sources.title: Working with read replicas for Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL
supports: PostgreSQL read replicas are read-only, and a promotion cannot be reversed
Point-in-time recovery is not supported for read replicas
With no transactions on the source, a PostgreSQL replica reports a lag of up to five minutes

sources.title: Read replica configuration with PostgreSQL
supports: A PostgreSQL read replica is an asynchronously created physical replica that uses native streaming replication
Up to 15 read replicas per source DB instance in the same Region
A read replica can itself be a Multi-AZ DB instance

sources.title: Monitoring and tuning the replication process
supports: The ReplicaLag metric is the result of SELECT extract(epoch from now() - pg_last_xact_replay_timestamp())

sources.title: Amazon CloudWatch metrics for Amazon RDS
supports: ReplicaLag is reported in seconds; FreeStorageSpace and DatabaseConnections are instance metrics in the AWS/RDS namespace
The T DB instance classes are recommended only for development, test and other non-production servers
Surplus CPU credits beyond what an instance can earn in 24 hours incur an additional charge

sources.title: DB instance class types
supports: The families are general purpose (db.m), memory optimized (db.r, db.x, db.z), compute optimized (db.c6gd, Multi-AZ DB clusters only), and burstable (db.t)
db.t4g instances are configured for Unlimited mode and can burst beyond the baseline for an additional charge

sources.title: Amazon RDS DB instance storage
supports: gp3 gives a baseline of 3,000 IOPS and 125 MiB/s; for PostgreSQL the baseline rises to 12,000 IOPS and 500 MiB/s from 400 GiB
gp3 storage for PostgreSQL ranges from 20 to 65,536 GiB
Magnetic storage is deprecated and new DB instances cannot use it

sources.title: Managing capacity automatically with Amazon RDS storage autoscaling
supports: Autoscaling starts when free space is at most 10 percent of allocated storage for at least five minutes, and fewer than four storage modifications happened in the past 24 hours
The increment is the greatest of 10 GiB, 10 percent of allocated storage, and the growth predicted for the next 7 hours
Allocated storage cannot be reduced after it has been allocated
The maximum storage threshold must be at least 10 percent above the allocated storage

sources.title: Overview of parameter groups
supports: The settings of a default parameter group cannot be modified
A static parameter takes effect only after a manual reboot; a dynamic parameter takes effect immediately by default
A pending-reboot status does not cause an automatic reboot in the next maintenance window

sources.title: Maintaining a DB instance
supports: Every DB instance has a weekly maintenance window; an unspecified one is a 30-minute window on a random day inside an 8-hour block per Region (13:00-21:00 UTC for Tokyo)
The window decides when pending operations start and does not limit how long they run
With Multi-AZ, operating system updates are applied to the standby first, then the standby is promoted
For an engine upgrade of a Multi-AZ DB instance, primary and standby are upgraded at the same time and both are unavailable

sources.title: Upgrading a DB instance engine version
supports: Major version upgrades must be started manually; minor version upgrades can be automatic
Database engine upgrades require downtime
RDS applies a minor version upgrade even with auto minor version upgrade off for critical security issues or an end of support

sources.title: Upgrades of the RDS for PostgreSQL DB engine
supports: RDS uses pg_upgrade for major version upgrades, and an upgrade cannot be reverted
With a backup retention above 0, RDS takes two DB snapshots during a major upgrade
In-Region read replicas are upgraded together with the source in a major version upgrade

sources.title: How to perform a major version upgrade for RDS for PostgreSQL
supports: A major upgrade does not upgrade extensions, and optimizer statistics must be regenerated with ANALYZE afterwards
A version-compatible parameter group must be ready before the upgrade

sources.title: Performing a minor version upgrade for RDS for PostgreSQL
supports: One minor version per major version is designated as the automatic upgrade version and is applied in the maintenance window

sources.title: Release calendars for Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL
supports: PostgreSQL 18 is the newest major version on RDS; its RDS end of standard support is 28 February 2031
RDS end of standard support: 17 on 28 February 2030, 16 on 28 February 2029, 15 on 29 February 2028, 14 on 28 February 2027; 13 ended on 28 February 2026
Each major version has dates for the start of Extended Support year 1 pricing, year 3 pricing, and the end of Extended Support

sources.title: Amazon RDS Extended Support with Amazon RDS
supports: RDS Extended Support keeps a database on a major version past the RDS end of standard support date for an additional cost, for up to 3 years
After Extended Support ends, RDS upgrades the major version automatically

sources.title: Creating a DB instance with Amazon RDS Extended Support
supports: Through the AWS CLI or the RDS API, an unspecified setting defaults to open-source-rds-extended-support (enabled); in the console the option is not selected by default
With open-source-rds-extended-support-disabled, RDS upgrades the instance to a supported version on or shortly after the end of standard support

sources.title: Amazon RDS Extended Support charges
supports: Charges begin the day after the RDS end of standard support date and apply to standby instances in Multi-AZ deployments too

sources.title: Overview of Amazon RDS Blue/Green Deployments
supports: A blue/green deployment creates a staging (green) environment that stays in sync with production
The switchover causes downtime, usually under one minute

sources.title: Limitations and considerations for Amazon RDS blue/green deployments
supports: Blue/green deployments do not support managing master user passwords with AWS Secrets Manager
Blue/green deployments are not supported with CloudFormation
Point-in-time recovery history does not carry over to the new production instance after a switchover

sources.title: PostgreSQL replication methods for blue/green deployments
supports: RDS for PostgreSQL uses physical replication for blue/green deployments, and logical replication when a major version upgrade is requested

sources.title: Introduction to backups
supports: Automated backups are storage volume snapshots of the whole DB instance, and the instance can be recovered to any point in the retention period
Automated backups are deleted with the DB instance unless retained; final and manual snapshots are not
Automated backups do not occur while the instance is in a state other than available, such as storage_full

sources.title: Backup retention period
supports: The retention period is 0 to 35 days; 0 disables automated backups; the default is one day through the API or CLI and seven days in the console
Changing the retention between 0 and a nonzero value causes an outage

sources.title: Managing automated backups
supports: During the backup window storage I/O might be suspended briefly while the backup initializes, typically under a few seconds
For PostgreSQL Multi-AZ deployments I/O is not suspended on the primary, because the backup is taken from the standby
The backup window cannot overlap with the weekly maintenance window

sources.title: Quotas and constraints for Amazon RDS
supports: The default of max_connections for PostgreSQL is LEAST({DBInstanceClassMemory/9531392}, 5000)

sources.title: Restoring a DB instance to a specified time for Amazon RDS
supports: A point-in-time restore creates a new DB instance and does not modify the source
RDS uploads transaction logs to Amazon S3 every five minutes; LatestRestorableTime shows how recent a restore can be
A restored DB instance gets the default DB parameter group unless one is specified

sources.title: Deleting a DB instance
supports: Deletion protection must be off before a DB instance can be deleted, and it is on by default for instances created in the console
A final snapshot and retained automated backups are the two ways to restore a deleted instance

sources.title: Stopping an Amazon RDS DB instance temporarily
supports: A stopped DB instance is started automatically after seven consecutive days
While stopped, provisioned storage and backup storage are charged and DB instance hours are not
A DB instance that has a read replica, or is one, cannot be stopped
Starting an instance requires instance recovery and can take from minutes to hours

sources.title: Encrypting Amazon RDS resources
supports: A DB instance can be encrypted only when it is created, not afterwards

sources.title: Working with a DB instance in a VPC
supports: A DB subnet group should have subnets in at least two Availability Zones

sources.title: Password management with Amazon RDS and AWS Secrets Manager
supports: RDS generates the master user password, stores it in Secrets Manager, and rotates it every seven days by default
The secret is deleted when the DB instance is deleted
Not supported: creating a read replica when the source manages credentials with Secrets Manager, and Blue/Green Deployments

sources.title: IAM database authentication for MariaDB, MySQL, and PostgreSQL
supports: An authentication token is generated with Signature Version 4 and has a lifetime of 15 minutes; it does not affect a session once established
For PostgreSQL, a user with the rds_iam role must log in as an IAM user: IAM authentication takes precedence over the password
IAM database authentication needs between 300 and 1000 MiB of extra memory on the DB instance
CloudWatch and CloudTrail do not log IAM authentication

sources.title: Creating and using an IAM policy for IAM database access
supports: The action is rds-db:connect and the resource is arn:aws:rds-db:region:account-id:dbuser:DbiResourceId/db-user-name

sources.title: Creating a database account using IAM authentication
supports: For PostgreSQL the user is created and then granted the rds_iam role: GRANT rds_iam TO db_userx

sources.title: Using SSL/TLS to encrypt a connection to a DB instance or cluster
supports: The certificate authorities are rds-ca-rsa2048-g1 (the default), rds-ca-rsa4096-g1 and rds-ca-ecc384-g1
With these CAs RDS rotates the DB server certificate automatically before it expires
The certificate bundles are published as global-bundle.pem and one bundle per Region

sources.title: Using SSL with a PostgreSQL DB instance
supports: rds.force_ssl defaults to 1 (on) for RDS for PostgreSQL 15 and later, and to 0 for 14 and older

sources.title: Building Lambda functions with Node.js
supports: Starting with Node.js 20, Lambda no longer loads additional CA certificates by default; NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS=/var/runtime/ca-cert.pem restores the earlier behaviour, which included the Amazon RDS certificates

sources.title: Using AWS Lambda with Amazon RDS
supports: Direct connections are useful in simple scenarios, and proxies are recommended for production

sources.title: Giving Lambda functions access to resources in an Amazon VPC
supports: The execution role needs six ec2 network interface actions, allowed on all resources

sources.title: Amazon RDS Proxy
supports: RDS Proxy pools and shares database connections, and queues or rejects connections it cannot serve
A proxy must be in the same VPC as the database and cannot be publicly accessible
For DB instances in replication configurations, a proxy can be associated only with the writer DB instance, not a read replica
Each account is limited to 20 proxies by default

sources.title: Planning where to use RDS Proxy
supports: Lambda functions and DB instances that hit too many connections are good candidates for a proxy
RDS Proxy bypasses DNS caches to reduce failover times by up to 66% for RDS Multi-AZ DB instances

sources.title: Avoiding pinning an RDS Proxy
supports: A pinned client connection keeps one database connection until the session ends

For PostgreSQL, SET commands, PREPARE/DEALLOCATE/EXECUTE, temporary objects, cursors, LISTEN, session-level advisory locks and sequence functions cause pinning; transaction-level advisory locks do not
Any statement larger than 16 KB pins the session
DatabaseConnectionsCurrentlySessionPinned shows how often pinning occurs

sources.title: Working with Amazon RDS Proxy endpoints
supports: Read-only proxy endpoints are described for proxies associated with a Multi-AZ DB cluster

sources.title: Amazon RDS Proxy pricing
supports: For provisioned instances RDS Proxy is priced per vCPU per hour of the database instance, with a minimum charge of 2 vCPUs

sources.title: Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL pricing
supports: There is no additional charge for backup storage up to 100% of the total database storage for a Region
T4g and T3 instances run in Unlimited mode and are charged when average CPU over a rolling 24 hours exceeds the baseline
The page describes a free tier of 750 hours for one year for new customers

sources.title: Amazon RDS Free Tier
supports: The page describes credits of up to USD 200 and a Free plan of up to 6 months for new customers, not hours of a named instance class

sources.title: CloudWatch Database Insights
supports: The end-of-life date for Performance Insights was July 31, 2026, and its users were migrated to Database Insights
Database Insights has a Standard mode (the default) and an Advanced mode

sources.title: Monitoring Amazon RDS databases with CloudWatch Database Insights
supports: By default RDS enables the Standard mode of Database Insights for RDS databases

sources.title: RDS for PostgreSQL database log files
supports: The PostgreSQL log, the upgrade log and the IAM database authentication error log can be published to CloudWatch Logs
The PostgreSQL log goes to the log group /aws/rds/instance/<instance>/postgresql

sources.title: Parameters for logging in RDS for PostgreSQL
supports: rds.log_retention_period defaults to 4320 minutes: log files on the instance are deleted after 3 days

sources.title: Turning on query logging for your RDS for PostgreSQL DB instance
supports: log_min_duration_statement logs any statement that runs at least the given number of milliseconds

sources.title: AWS::RDS::DBInstance
supports: The properties ManageMasterUserPassword, EngineLifecycleSupport, EnableIAMDatabaseAuthentication, MaxAllocatedStorage and AutoMinorVersionUpgrade exist on the resource

sources.title: Resource types that support Cloud Control API
supports: AWS::RDS::DBParameterGroup is in the list of supported resource types

supports: rds.DatabaseInstance has manageMasterUserPassword, iamAuthentication, engineLifecycleSupport and maxAllocatedStorage; rds.PostgresEngineVersion lists versions up to 18.3

sources.title: @aws-sdk/rds-signer 3.1149.0 (installed types)
supports: Signer takes hostname, port, username and region, and getAuthToken() returns the token

sources.title: AWS Price List: Amazon RDS, ap-northeast-1
supports: Unit prices of db.t4g.micro (Single-AZ and Multi-AZ, 2 vCPUs), gp3 storage, RDS Proxy, backup storage beyond the free allocation, RDS Extended Support for PostgreSQL, and the db.c6gd.medium Multi-AZ DB cluster

sources.title: PostgreSQL 18: System Administration Functions
supports: pg_current_wal_lsn() returns the current write-ahead log write location and cannot be executed during recovery
pg_last_wal_replay_lsn() returns the last write-ahead log location replayed during recovery

sources.title: PostgreSQL 18: Hot Standby
supports: Connections to a hot standby are strictly read-only, and data on the standby is eventually consistent with the primary

sources.title: PostgreSQL 18: ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES
supports: ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES sets the privileges applied to objects created in the future by the role that runs it

sources.title: Cloudflare Hyperdrive
supports: Hyperdrive accelerates queries from Workers to an existing Postgres or MySQL database, including ones hosted on AWS

sources.title: Cloudflare Hyperdrive: Pricing
supports: Hyperdrive is included in the Workers Free and Paid plans; connection pooling and query caching incur no additional charge on the Paid plan

sources.title: Cloudflare Hyperdrive: Connect to a private database using Tunnel
supports: Hyperdrive reaches a database in a private network through Cloudflare Tunnel

sources.title: Cloudflare D1: Global read replication
supports: The D1 Sessions API gives sequential consistency within a session, carried between requests by a bookmark

sources.title: Vercel Postgres
supports: Vercel Postgres is no longer available; existing databases were moved to Neon in December 2024, and new projects install a Postgres integration from the Marketplace

sources.title: Vercel Storage
supports: Relational databases on Vercel come through Marketplace providers such as Neon and Supabase

sources.title: Amazon Aurora storage
supports: Aurora data is stored in the cluster volume, a single virtual volume with copies of the data across three Availability Zones in one Region
The amount of replication is independent of the number of DB instances in the cluster
Adding a DB instance does not copy the table data; removing one removes no data; only deleting the cluster removes the data
Two storage configurations: Aurora Standard (pay per 1 million I/O requests) and Aurora I/O-Optimized (no I/O charge)
AWS's guidance: I/O-Optimized when I/O spending is 25% or more of total Aurora spending
Switching from Standard to I/O-Optimized is possible once every 30 days; back to Standard at any time; no downtime for serverless instances
The volume grows automatically and you are charged for the space used; freed space reduces the charge

sources.title: Amazon Aurora endpoint connections
supports: The four endpoint types: cluster, reader, instance, custom, plus the Global Database writer endpoint
Up to 15 Aurora Replicas handle read-only traffic
Cluster and reader endpoints change which instance they connect to when an instance becomes unavailable; instance endpoints do not
During a failover the reader endpoint might direct connections to the new primary for a short time

sources.title: Cluster endpoints for Amazon Aurora
supports: The IP address behind the cluster endpoint changes when a failover promotes a new primary

With connection pooling, be prepared to flush or shorten the time-to-live of cached DNS information, so as not to open a read/write connection to an instance that is unavailable or is now read-only after a failover

sources.title: Reader endpoints for Amazon Aurora
supports: The reader endpoint balances connections, not individual queries
With only a primary instance and no replicas, the reader endpoint connects to the primary, and writes go through

sources.title: Custom endpoints for Amazon Aurora
supports: A custom endpoint is a set of instances you choose; up to five per cluster
Custom endpoints distribute connections passively, using DNS to return the address of one of the instances at random

sources.title: High availability for Amazon Aurora
supports: Writes are replicated synchronously across Availability Zones to six storage nodes; replicas use asynchronous replication
With a replica, failover promotes it: read and write operations fail with an exception meanwhile; service is typically restored in less than 60 seconds, often less than 30
Without a replica, the primary is recreated in the same AZ, which typically takes less than 10 minutes
If an AZ outage takes a single-instance cluster's primary, you must create a new instance in another AZ yourself
Promotion tiers 0 to 15 decide which replica is promoted
RDS Proxy bypasses DNS caches and can reduce failover times by up to 66%

sources.title: Fast failover with Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL
supports: Recommended TCP keepalive settings: idle 1 second, interval 1 second, count 5
Updating the DNS record of an endpoint typically takes less than 30 seconds
After connecting, SHOW transaction_read_only tells a writer (OFF) from a reader (ON)
FailoverDBCluster promotes another instance and is the API for testing a failover; the cluster needs two or more instances
The page's examples are for the JDBC driver; nothing in it is about node-postgres

sources.title: Replication with Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL
supports: Replicas read the same cluster volume as the writer, so no copy of the data is made per replica
ReplicaLag for Aurora PostgreSQL is the lag of the replica's page cache behind the writer's

sources.title: How Aurora serverless works
supports: One ACU is approximately 2 GiB of memory with corresponding CPU and networking; capacity ranges from 0 to 256 ACUs
A minimum of 0 ACUs needs Aurora PostgreSQL 13.15, 14.12, 15.7, 16.3 or higher
Scaling happens in increments as small as 0.5 ACU, while connections are open and transactions are in progress, without disrupting them
The larger the current capacity, the larger the scaling increment
Readers in promotion tiers 0 and 1 are kept at least as large as the writer; tiers 2 to 15 scale on their own
A cluster with n instances consumes about n times the minimum ACUs when idle
The page now calls the feature 'Aurora serverless' and says Serverless v1 is a deprecated product

sources.title: Scaling to Zero ACUs with automatic pause and resume for Aurora serverless
supports: With a minimum of 0 ACUs an instance pauses after a period with no user connections; the instance charge is zero while paused; storage is still charged
The interval is 300 seconds (the default) to 86,400 seconds
Resuming typically takes about 15 seconds; after more than 24 hours paused it can take 30 seconds or longer
An open user connection, an RDS Proxy, logical replication, a zero-ETL integration, and membership of a global database prevent pausing
A request through the RDS Data API resumes a paused writer
Aurora resumes paused instances for some maintenance, and then waits at least 20 minutes before pausing again
An instance resumes at a relatively small capacity whatever it had before
AWS recommends retry logic for connections, and timeouts longer than 15 seconds (30 or more if idle for over a day)

sources.title: Performance and scaling for Aurora serverless
supports: The scaling rate depends on current capacity: the higher it is, the faster the instance scales up
With a minimum of 0 or 0.5 ACUs on PostgreSQL, max_connections is capped at 2,000

sources.title: Supported Regions and Aurora DB engines for Aurora serverless
supports: In Asia Pacific (Tokyo), Aurora serverless with Aurora PostgreSQL: 18.3, 17.4, 16.1, 15.2, 14.3, 13.6 and higher

sources.title: Supported Regions and Aurora DB engines for cluster storage configurations
supports: Aurora I/O-Optimized is available in all Regions for Aurora PostgreSQL 17.4, 16.1, 15.2, 14.7, 13.10 and higher

sources.title: Quotas and constraints for Amazon Aurora
supports: The cluster volume's maximum size is 256 TiB for Aurora PostgreSQL 17.5, 16.9, 15.13 and higher, and 128 TiB for earlier versions

sources.title: Cloning a volume for an Amazon Aurora DB cluster
supports: A clone is a new cluster that initially shares the source's data pages (copy-on-write); storage is added only as either side changes pages
Shared pages are billed to the source cluster only
Up to 15 copy-on-write clones; the next one is a full copy
A clone cannot be created in another Region

sources.title: Backtracking an Aurora DB cluster
supports: Backtrack rewinds an Aurora MySQL cluster to a time without restoring from a backup
Backtrack is not available for Aurora PostgreSQL

sources.title: Using Amazon Aurora Global Database
supports: One primary Region where data is written and up to 10 read-only secondary Regions
Replication uses the storage layer, with latency typically under a second
Switchover moves the primary with no data loss when healthy; failover is for an outage of the primary Region

sources.title: Aurora zero-ETL integrations
supports: A zero-ETL integration makes the cluster's data available in Amazon Redshift or an Amazon SageMaker AI lakehouse in near real time

sources.title: Using the Amazon RDS Data API
supports: The Data API is an HTTP endpoint for running SQL without a persistent connection
It uses database credentials stored in Secrets Manager; the caller passes none
A Lambda function can use it without being configured for access to a VPC

sources.title: Limitations for the Amazon RDS Data API
supports: Queries run on the writer instance only
Not supported on T DB instance classes
The response size limit is 1 MiB

sources.title: Supported Regions and Aurora DB engines for RDS Data API
supports: In Asia Pacific (Tokyo), the Data API with Aurora PostgreSQL serverless and provisioned: 17.4, 16.1, 15.3, 14.8, 13.11 and higher

sources.title: Amazon RDS Data API operations reference
supports: ExecuteStatement, BatchExecuteStatement, BeginTransaction, CommitTransaction, RollbackTransaction
Every call takes resourceArn (the cluster) and secretArn
Parameters are name-value pairs (SqlParameter) with a Field value
Supported Aurora PostgreSQL types include UUID, TIMESTAMP, JSONB, TEXT, INT, BOOL

sources.title: Controlling Data API timeout behavior
supports: A call is cancelled with a timeout error after 45 seconds by default
If the SDK reports a timeout while the operation still completes, retrying might insert duplicate data; the SDK might retry automatically

sources.title: Session management with Amazon RDS Data API
supports: The Data API keeps a pool of database connections and resets session state (DISCARD ALL on PostgreSQL) before reusing one

sources.title: Authorizing access to the Amazon RDS Data API
supports: The minimum policy: the five rds-data actions on the cluster's ARN, and secretsmanager:GetSecretValue on the secret
AWS recommends a specific ARN and not a wildcard

sources.title: Troubleshooting Amazon RDS Data API
supports: 'Transaction is not found': each call of a transaction must come within three minutes of the previous one
A row in a result set is limited to 64 KB
Multi-statements are not supported

supports: formatRecordsAs JSON returns the result set as one JSON string in formattedRecords
sources.note: The installed client's types add that this applies to SELECT statements only and is ignored for others, which is why the chapter reads `records` with column metadata instead.

sources.title: Password management with Amazon Aurora and AWS Secrets Manager
supports: Aurora can create the master user password, keep it in Secrets Manager, and rotate it every seven days by default
Deleting the cluster deletes the secret it manages
Secrets stored in Secrets Manager incur charges

sources.title: Working with Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL
supports: AWS describes Aurora PostgreSQL as a drop-in replacement for PostgreSQL

sources.title: Extension versions for Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL
supports: Aurora PostgreSQL supports a published list of extensions per engine version; the list includes pgvector, pg_cron, and plpgsql

sources.title: Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL updates
supports: Aurora PostgreSQL 17.9 was released on 2026-04-06, and 17.11 on 2026-09-29
PostgreSQL 18 versions exist (18.3 from 2026-06-11)
sources.note: The page lists releases. It does not say which versions a new cluster can be created with in a given Region today; that needs `aws rds describe-db-engine-versions`, which was not run.

sources.title: What is Amazon Aurora DSQL?
supports: Aurora DSQL is serverless and distributed, with no instances and, in AWS's words, no traditional database failover
Compatible with PostgreSQL version 16
Available in Asia Pacific (Tokyo) and (Osaka)
Multi-Region peered clusters accept reads and writes in each Region with strong consistency

sources.title: Migrating from PostgreSQL to Aurora DSQL
supports: No temporary tables, no triggers, no PL/pgSQL; the isolation level is fixed at Repeatable Read
A transaction can modify up to 3,000 rows
Connections time out after 1 hour
sources.note: Neither this page nor the others read for chapter 60 mention CREATE EXTENSION. Whether Aurora DSQL supports any extension was not confirmed.

sources.title: Cluster quotas and database limits in Amazon Aurora DSQL
supports: 10,000 connections per cluster (adjustable); 100 new connections per second
A write transaction is limited to 10 MiB of modified data, 3,000 rows, and 5 minutes

sources.title: Concurrency control in Aurora DSQL
supports: Aurora DSQL takes no locks and checks for conflicts at commit; the loser gets SQLSTATE 40001
AWS states that this eliminates deadlocks

sources.title: PostgreSQL 17: Appendix A. PostgreSQL Error Codes
supports: Class 08 is connection exceptions (08000, 08003, 08006)
25006 read_only_sql_transaction, 40001 serialization_failure, 40P01 deadlock_detected
57P01 admin_shutdown, 57P02 crash_shutdown, 57P03 cannot_connect_now
sources.note: Which of these Aurora PostgreSQL actually sends to a session during a failover was not observed.

supports: A transaction can run for at most 24 hours, and times out when no call uses its ID for three minutes
DatabaseResumingException: the request was cancelled because the Aurora Serverless instance was paused; wait and try again
DatabaseUnavailableException: the writer instance is not available; TransactionNotFoundException; ServiceUnavailableError

formatRecordsAs applies to SELECT statements only
TypeHint values: DATE, DECIMAL, JSON, TIME, TIMESTAMP, UUID

sources.title: Cloudflare Hyperdrive
supports: Hyperdrive pools connections and caches queries between Workers and an existing Postgres or MySQL database, including databases hosted on AWS
Available on Free and Paid plans; the page was last updated 2026-06-22

sources.title: Postgres on Vercel
supports: Vercel Postgres is no longer available; existing databases were moved to Neon in December 2024
New projects install a Postgres integration from the Marketplace

sources.title: Vercel Marketplace: AWS
supports: The AWS integration on the Vercel Marketplace lists Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL, Amazon Aurora DSQL, and Amazon DynamoDB
sources.note: Read through a page summary. How the integration provisions and bills was not read.

sources.title: Amazon SQS queue types
supports: Standard queues: at-least-once delivery and best-effort ordering; FIFO queues: order preserved and no duplicates introduced
With batching a FIFO queue handles up to 3,000 messages per second per API method, from 300 API calls per second
sources.note: This page says high throughput mode scales to 30,000 TPS 'with relaxed ordering within message groups'. The message quotas page gives per-Region figures (9,000 TPS in Tokyo) and the high throughput page does not mention relaxed ordering. The chapter quotes the quotas page and says the two differ.

sources.title: Amazon SQS FIFO queues
supports: The order in which messages are sent and received is preserved, and a message is delivered once and remains unavailable until a consumer processes and deletes it
A FIFO queue can hold many ordered message groups, with no quota on their number
FIFO queues are available in all Regions where SQS is

sources.title: FIFO queue delivery logic in Amazon SQS
supports: A send without a message group ID fails
Ordering holds within a message group; messages of different groups may be processed out of order relative to each other
One receive may return several messages of the same group, up to 10, and may add messages of other groups
No more messages of a group are returned by later receives until the received ones are deleted or become visible again
A consumer cannot ask for a particular message group
A producer may retry SendMessage with the same deduplication ID without introducing duplicates, as long as an acknowledgment arrives before the deduplication interval expires

sources.title: Exactly-once processing in Amazon SQS
supports: A SendMessage retried within the 5-minute deduplication interval introduces no duplicate
Content-based deduplication uses a SHA-256 hash of the message body, not of its attributes
Deduplication needs either content-based deduplication or an explicit deduplication ID

sources.title: Using the message deduplication ID in Amazon SQS
supports: A message whose deduplication ID was already accepted is acknowledged and not delivered
SQS keeps tracking the deduplication ID after the message has been received and deleted

sources.title: When to provide a message deduplication ID in Amazon SQS
supports: A producer should give an explicit ID when identical bodies must count as different messages, or different bodies as the same message

sources.title: Using the message group ID with Amazon SQS FIFO Queues
supports: Messages of one message group are processed one at a time, in strict order
On a standard queue a MessageGroupId enables fair queues and does not order anything

sources.title: FIFO queue and message identifiers in Amazon SQS
supports: A FIFO queue's name ends in .fifo, and the suffix counts toward the 80 characters of a name
Each receive returns a different receipt handle, and a delete needs the most recent one
The sequence number is a large, non-consecutive number SQS assigns to each message

sources.title: Moving from a standard queue to a FIFO queue in Amazon SQS
supports: A standard queue cannot be converted to a FIFO queue
FIFO queues support a delay per queue, not per message

sources.title: Amazon SQS FIFO queue and Lambda concurrency behavior
supports: At any time only one Lambda instance processes messages of a given message group; different groups are processed concurrently

sources.title: High throughput for FIFO queues in Amazon SQS
supports: A FIFO queue is stored in partitions, and the hash of the message group ID decides the partition
SQS recommends message group IDs with many distinct values

sources.title: Enabling high throughput for FIFO queues in Amazon SQS
supports: High throughput needs the deduplication scope set to the message group and the throughput limit set per message group ID

sources.title: Amazon SQS message quotas
supports: A message is at most 1,048,576 bytes (1 MiB) and at least 1 byte
Retention defaults to 4 days and ranges from 60 seconds to 14 days
The visibility timeout defaults to 30 seconds and ranges from 0 seconds to 12 hours
A batch holds at most 10 messages, a message at most 10 attributes, and a message timer at most 15 minutes
Without high throughput a FIFO queue allows 300 transactions per second per API action, 3,000 messages with batching
With high throughput the limit in Asia Pacific (Tokyo) is 9,000 transactions per second, 90,000 messages with batching
A message group ID is at most 128 characters of alphanumerics and punctuation

sources.title: Amazon SQS FIFO queue quotas
supports: A FIFO queue supports at most 120,000 in-flight messages; no error is returned when the limit is reached
The longest long polling wait is 20 seconds, and the longest queue delay 15 minutes

sources.title: Amazon SQS visibility timeout
supports: A received message stays in the queue, hidden for the visibility timeout, and becomes visible again unless deleted
While a message of a FIFO message group is in flight, later messages of the group are not made available until it is deleted or its timeout expires
ChangeMessageVisibility extends or shortens the timeout of one message; 0 makes it available at once
The limit is 12 hours from when the message was first received, and extending does not reset it
The guide suggests a heartbeat that keeps extending the timeout when the processing time is not known

sources.title: Processing messages in a timely manner in Amazon SQS
supports: A visibility timeout shorter than the processing time lets another consumer receive the message while the first still works on it
A heartbeat can start with 2 minutes and add 2 minutes every minute
A consumer that needs longer than 12 hours should use Step Functions

sources.title: Configuring visibility timeouts in Amazon SQS
supports: The visibility timeout should be longer than the SDK's read timeout for ReceiveMessage

sources.title: Amazon SQS short and long polling
supports: Short polling asks a subset of servers and answers at once, even with nothing; long polling asks all servers and answers when a message is available or the wait time ends
The longest wait is 20 seconds
Long polling is in effect when the receive's WaitTimeSeconds, or else the queue's ReceiveMessageWaitTimeSeconds, is greater than 0

sources.title: Amazon SQS batch actions
supports: SendMessageBatch, DeleteMessageBatch, and ChangeMessageVisibilityBatch each take up to 10 messages
The messages of one SendMessageBatch may not exceed 1 MiB in total
Permission for a batch action is the permission for the single action

sources.title: Managing large Amazon SQS messages with Extended Client Library and Amazon S3
supports: The Extended Client Libraries for Java and Python store the payload in S3 and send a reference in the message
The libraries work with standard and FIFO queues
sources.note: The page still says 'payloads between 256 KB and 2 GB'. The quotas page and the API reference give 1 MiB as the message limit; the chapter uses 1 MiB.

sources.title: Amazon SQS delay queues
supports: A delay queue hides every new message for up to 15 minutes
Changing the delay of a FIFO queue affects messages already in it; for a standard queue it does not
For longer or more flexible delays the guide points to EventBridge Scheduler

sources.title: Amazon SQS message timers
supports: A message timer hides one message for up to 15 minutes and overrides the queue's delay
FIFO queues do not support timers on individual messages

sources.title: Message metadata for Amazon SQS
supports: A message can carry up to 10 attributes, each with a name, a type (String, Number, Binary), and a value
All parts of an attribute count toward the 1 MiB size limit

sources.title: Using dead-letter queues in Amazon SQS
supports: A dead-letter queue must be in the same account and Region as its source queue
The guide warns against a dead-letter queue on a FIFO queue when the exact order of operations must not be broken
For a FIFO queue the enqueue timestamp resets when a message moves to the dead-letter queue; for a standard queue it does not
A redrive allow policy can restrict which source queues may use a queue as their dead-letter queue

sources.title: Learn how to configure a dead-letter queue redrive in Amazon SQS
supports: A redrive moves messages to the source queue or another queue of the same type, oldest first
Redriven messages are new messages with a new message ID and enqueue time, and they interleave with what producers are sending
When a message moves from a FIFO queue to its FIFO dead-letter queue, its deduplication ID is replaced by its message ID
Messages cannot be filtered or changed while redriving; a task runs at most 36 hours

sources.title: Encryption at rest in Amazon SQS
supports: A queue is encrypted with SQS-managed keys (SSE-SQS) or with a KMS key (SSE-KMS)
SSE encrypts the body; not the queue metadata, the message metadata including attributes, or the metrics
The data key reuse period is 60 seconds to 24 hours, 5 minutes by default
A queue encrypted with the AWS managed key for SQS cannot invoke a Lambda function in another account

sources.title: Amazon SQS Key management
supports: A producer to an SSE-KMS queue needs kms:GenerateDataKey and kms:Decrypt; a consumer needs kms:Decrypt
Calls to KMS per queue are estimated as R = (B / D) * (2 * P + C)
An AWS service that sends to an encrypted queue needs a customer managed key whose policy allows that service

sources.title: Available CloudWatch metrics for Amazon SQS
supports: ApproximateAgeOfOldestMessage: a standard queue moves a message received three or more times to the back, so the metric skips it; a FIFO queue does not reorder, and a failed message blocks its group until it is deleted or expires
NumberOfEmptyReceives counts ReceiveMessage calls that returned nothing
NumberOfDeduplicatedSentMessages and ApproximateNumberOfGroupsWithInflightMessages exist for FIFO queues
NumberOfMessagesSent does not count messages SQS moves to a dead-letter queue itself

sources.title: Creating alarms for dead-letter queues using Amazon CloudWatch
supports: The guide alarms on the dead-letter queue's ApproximateNumberOfMessagesVisible

sources.title: Amazon SQS fair queues
supports: On a standard queue, messages sent with a MessageGroupId are treated as tenants, and delivery to quiet tenants is prioritized when one tenant builds a backlog
A MessageGroupId on a standard queue does not enforce ordering

sources.title: Basic examples of Amazon SQS policies
supports: A queue policy grants another account sqs:SendMessage by naming the account as principal and the queue as resource

sources.title: SendMessage
supports: A message sent with a deduplication ID that was accepted before is accepted and not delivered during the 5-minute deduplication interval
If the acknowledgment is lost and the message is resent with the same deduplication ID after the interval, SQS cannot detect the duplicate
DelaySeconds cannot be set per message on a FIFO queue
A body may contain only the characters #x9, #xA, #xD, #x20 to #xD7FF, #xE000 to #xFFFD, #x10000 to #x10FFFF; anything else is rejected with InvalidMessageContents
A deduplication ID is at most 128 characters; the sequence number keeps increasing within a message group

sources.title: SendMessageBatch
supports: For a FIFO queue, the messages of one batch are enqueued in the order they are sent
Each entry's result is reported individually, so a call that returns HTTP 200 can contain failures

sources.title: ReceiveMessage
supports: A receive returns at most 10 messages
If a consumer is still processing when the visibility timeout expires, another worker can receive the same messages and process duplicates, and the first consumer's delete fails
ReceiveRequestAttemptId lets a FIFO consumer retry a receive whose answer was lost and get the same messages, for 5 minutes
The system attributes include ApproximateReceiveCount, MessageGroupId, MessageDeduplicationId, and SequenceNumber

sources.title: ChangeMessageVisibility
supports: The new timeout counts from the moment of the call
Asking for more than the time left of the 12 hours is an error; SQS does not shorten the request
The changed timeout applies to this receive only; the next receive uses the queue's value again

sources.title: DeleteMessage
supports: A delete with an old receipt handle succeeds as a request, and the message might not be deleted

sources.title: CreateQueue
supports: The dead-letter queue of a FIFO queue must be a FIFO queue, and that of a standard queue a standard queue
maxReceiveCount defaults to 10; a message moves when its receive count exceeds it
DeduplicationScope is messageGroup or queue; FifoThroughputLimit is perQueue or perMessageGroupId
MaximumMessageSize ranges from 1,024 bytes to 1,048,576 bytes

sources.title: StartMessageMoveTask
supports: A message move task works only from a queue that is the dead-letter queue of another SQS queue
With no destination, messages go back to the queues they came from; one task per queue at a time

sources.title: Using Lambda with Amazon SQS
supports: Lambda polls the queue and invokes the function synchronously with a batch; it deletes the messages when the function succeeds
An event source mapping processes each event at least once, and the documentation strongly recommends idempotent function code
A FIFO record carries SequenceNumber, MessageGroupId, and MessageDeduplicationId among its attributes
Provisioned mode gives an event source mapping dedicated pollers, at extra cost
sources.note: The page gives the maximum number of provisioned pollers as 10,000 in one place and the parameters page says 2,000. The chapter does not use provisioned mode and quotes neither.

sources.title: Creating and configuring an Amazon SQS event source mapping
supports: The queue's visibility timeout should be at least six times the function's timeout, plus the batch window if there is one
Lambda refuses an event source mapping whose function timeout exceeds the queue's visibility timeout
The batch size is at most 10 for a FIFO queue and 10,000 for a standard queue
maxReceiveCount of at least 5 is recommended
An encrypted queue needs kms:Decrypt in the execution role

sources.title: Configuring scaling behavior for SQS event source mappings
supports: Maximum concurrency is a setting of the event source, from 2 to 1,000, and cannot be combined with provisioned mode
For a FIFO queue, concurrent invocations are capped by the number of message group IDs or by maximum concurrency, whichever is lower
When the function returns an error, all retries on the affected messages happen before Lambda receives more messages of the same group
At low traffic Lambda scales back to five concurrent invokes, and the further reduction to two is not available when maximum concurrency is set

sources.title: Handling errors for an SQS event source in Lambda
supports: With partial batch responses on a FIFO queue, the function should stop at the first failure and return the failed and all unprocessed messages
An exception fails the whole batch; an empty or null list is a complete success; an unknown or empty itemIdentifier fails the whole batch

sources.title: Lambda parameters for Amazon SQS event source mappings
supports: A batching window is not supported for FIFO queues

sources.title: Subscribing an Amazon SQS queue to an Amazon SNS topic
supports: The queue's policy must give the topic sqs:SendMessage before the subscription delivers

sources.title: Amazon SNS message delivery for FIFO topics
supports: An SNS FIFO topic delivers to SQS FIFO queues, keeping order and deduplication, and to SQS standard queues with best-effort ordering

sources.title: Using IAM with DynamoDB transactions
supports: Put and Update inside a transaction are authorized by the PutItem and UpdateItem permissions

sources.title: TransactWriteItems
supports: The actions of a transaction all succeed or all fail
CancellationReasons lists one reason per item in request order; a failed condition has the code ConditionalCheckFailed and an item without error the code None

sources.title: Using time to live (TTL) in DynamoDB
supports: The TTL attribute is a Number in Unix epoch seconds; expired items are deleted typically within a few days, without consuming write throughput

sources.title: Policy evaluation logic
supports: Within one account, the permissions of identity-based and resource-based policies are evaluated together and the result is their union; an explicit deny in either overrides an allow

sources.title: Cross-account policy evaluation logic
supports: Cross-account access needs a resource-based policy on the resource that names the other account or its principals, and an identity-based policy on the principal that allows the access

sources.title: Amazon SQS pricing
supports: Every SQS action is a request; all customers get 1 million requests a month free, for standard and FIFO queues alike
Each 64 KB chunk of a payload is billed as one request, so a 1 MiB payload is 16 requests
Fair queue requests are charged the fair queue rate on top of the standard rate
Calls SQS makes to KMS for a queue encrypted with a KMS key are charged by KMS

sources.title: AWS Price List: Amazon SQS, Asia Pacific (Tokyo)
supports: FIFO requests: USD 0.50 per million (SKU SQUU378BX6EJ8NEF); standard: USD 0.40; fair queue requests: USD 0.10 per million
Global-Requests, queue type Any: the first 1,000,000 requests a month are USD 0
sources.note: Publication date 2026-09-11T12:46:07Z.

sources.title: AWS Price List: AWS KMS, Asia Pacific (Tokyo)
supports: USD 0.03 per 10,000 requests and USD 1 per customer managed key a month
sources.note: Publication date 2026-09-11T12:46:01Z.

sources.title: Cloudflare Queues: How Queues Works
supports: Queues does not guarantee that messages are delivered in the order they were published

sources.title: Cloudflare Queues: Delivery guarantees
supports: Queues delivers at least once by default

sources.title: Cloudflare Queues: Limits
supports: A message is at most 128 KB, a delay at most 24 hours, and a pull consumer's visibility timeout at most 12 hours

sources.title: Cloudflare Queues: Batching, Retries and Delays
supports: A message can be delayed when it is sent and when it is retried, by up to 24 hours

sources.title: Vercel Queues
supports: Vercel Queues is in beta on all plans; a topic is a durable append-only log read by consumer groups, delivered at least once
A publish can carry an idempotency key that drops repeated publishes during the message's retention period
sources.note: The overview page does not state an ordering guarantee. The chapter says so.

sources.title: @go-to-k/cdkd 0.296.28
supports: The package registers dedicated providers for AWS::SQS::Queue, AWS::SQS::QueuePolicy, AWS::Lambda::EventSourceMapping, AWS::Lambda::Function, AWS::CloudWatch::Alarm, AWS::DynamoDB::Table, AWS::Logs::LogGroup, AWS::IAM::Role, and AWS::IAM::Policy
Its SQS provider names a queue that has no QueueName with generateResourceName(logicalId) and adds no .fifo suffix, so a FIFO queue needs an explicit name
sources.note: Read from the dist files of the installed package, not from the repository.

sources.title: REST API endpoints for self-hosted runners
supports: POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/runners/generate-jitconfig: 'Generates a configuration that can be passed to the runner application at startup'; body name, runner_group_id, labels (1 to 100) are required, work_folder defaults to _work; answers 201, 404, 409, 422; the response has runner.id and encoded_jit_config
A registration token for a repository 'expires after one hour'
DELETE /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/runners/{runner_id} 'Forces the removal of a self-hosted runner from a repository' and answers 204
sources.note: The page does not say what a 409 from generate-jitconfig means, nor how long encoded_jit_config is.

sources.title: Secure use reference (GitHub Actions)
supports: Self-hosted runners 'do not have guarantees around running in ephemeral clean virtual machines, and can be persistently compromised by untrusted code in a workflow'
Self-hosted runners 'should almost never be used for public repositories'; for private repositories anyone who can fork and open a pull request can compromise the runner environment

Just-in-time runners 'perform at most one job before being automatically removed'; 're-using hardware to host JIT runners can risk exposing information from the environment'; started with ./run.sh --jitconfig
'there is no way to guarantee that a self-hosted runner only runs one job' is said of runners destroyed by automation after each job, before the JIT section
pull_request_target and workflow_run are privileged triggers and must not check out untrusted code

sources.title: Self-hosted runners reference
supports: 'The host machine must be able to make outbound HTTPS connections over port 443'; the hosts include github.com, api.github.com, *.actions.githubusercontent.com and codeload.github.com
A new runner version must be installed within 30 days
'GitHub recommends implementing autoscaling with ephemeral self-hosted runners; autoscaling with persistent self-hosted runners is not recommended'
'You can create your own autoscaling environment by using payloads received from the workflow_job webhook'
ARC is recommended for teams with Kubernetes; the Scale Set Client 'orchestrates GitHub API interactions for scale sets while leaving infrastructure provisioning to you'
Docker container actions and service containers need a Linux machine with Docker installed

sources.title: Removing self-hosted runners
supports: A self-hosted runner that has not connected for more than 14 days is removed automatically; an ephemeral one after 1 day

sources.title: Actions Runner Controller
supports: ARC is a Kubernetes operator; its listener holds an HTTPS long poll to the Actions service and the controller requests a just-in-time configuration for each ephemeral runner pod
The actions-runner image 'contains the least amount of packages necessary for the container runtime and the runner binaries'; the runner is launched with /home/runner/run.sh

sources.title: actions/scaleset
supports: A standalone Go client for the Runner Scale Set APIs, in public preview; starting and managing the runners is left to the user

sources.title: Webhook events and payloads
supports: Delivery headers X-GitHub-Event, X-GitHub-Delivery (a GUID), X-Hub-Signature-256 (sent when the webhook has a secret); payloads are capped at 25 MB
workflow_job has the actions queued, in_progress, completed, waiting; a GitHub App needs read access to the Actions repository permission to subscribe

sources.title: github/rest-api-description: api.github.com.yaml
supports: webhook-workflow-job-queued: action, repository, sender, workflow_job are required; workflow_job has id, run_id, run_attempt, labels (array of strings), head_branch, runner_id (nullable) and no field naming the head repository
repository has full_name, private (boolean), fork, visibility; installation (id, node_id) is present when the event is sent to a GitHub App
workflow-run requires head_repository, repository, event and head_branch
sources.note: Read from the main branch on 2026-10-13. The schema lists head_repository as required and not nullable; the receiver accepts null and refuses it.

sources.title: Validating webhook deliveries
supports: X-Hub-Signature-256 is an HMAC hex digest of the payload, keyed with the webhook secret, and always starts with sha256=
Compare with a constant-time comparison, not ==
The test values: secret "It's a Secret to Everybody", payload "Hello, World!", signature sha256=757107ea0eb2509fc211221cce984b8a37570b6d7586c22c46f4379c8b043e17

sources.title: Handling failed webhook deliveries
supports: 'GitHub does not automatically redeliver failed deliveries'; a delivery fails when the server is down or takes longer than 10 seconds

sources.title: Best practices for using webhooks
supports: Answer with a 2XX within 10 seconds; a redelivery carries the same X-GitHub-Delivery value as the original

sources.title: Generating a JSON Web Token (JWT) for a GitHub App
supports: RS256; iat (60 seconds in the past is recommended), exp no more than 10 minutes ahead, iss the client ID or app ID; sent as Authorization: Bearer

sources.title: REST API endpoints for GitHub Apps

sources.title: Securely deploying AI agents (Claude Code docs)
supports: Agents can take unintended actions due to prompt injection (instructions embedded in content they process) or model error
Isolation technologies compared: sandbox runtime, containers (setup dependent), gVisor, VMs such as Firecracker

Cloud deployments: private subnet with no internet gateway, firewall rules that block all egress except to a proxy, a proxy that enforces domain allowlists, minimal IAM permissions, traffic logged at the proxy
The recommended credential pattern is a proxy outside the agent's boundary that injects credentials; the agent never sees them
With HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY the proxy sees only an opaque CONNECT tunnel for HTTPS unless it terminates TLS
Not all programs respect HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY

sources.title: Choose a sandbox environment (Claude Code docs)
supports: Sandbox isolation reduces the impact of a breach but does not eliminate risk; any approach that allows network egress can still leak data the agent can read
A custom container can run Claude Code with your own network policies; unprivileged containers need enableWeakerNestedSandbox for the built-in Bash sandbox
A dedicated virtual machine provides the strongest separation, with its own kernel; options include microVMs such as Firecracker
A cloud session runs in an isolated, Anthropic-managed virtual machine; a proxy holds the GitHub token outside the sandbox

sources.title: Configure the sandboxed Bash tool (Claude Code docs)
supports: The Bash sandbox covers shell commands only; Read, Edit, Write, WebFetch and WebSearch, MCP servers and hooks run outside it
Linux uses bubblewrap and socat; network connections go through a proxy that checks each host against the allowed domains
The proxy decides from the client-supplied hostname without inspecting TLS, so domain fronting can reach hosts outside the allowlist
sandbox.failIfUnavailable makes Claude Code exit when the sandbox cannot start; allowUnsandboxedCommands false disables the unsandboxed retry

In an unprivileged container bubblewrap cannot mount a fresh /proc; enableWeakerNestedSandbox bind-mounts the container's /proc, weakens security, and should be used only when the outer container is the boundary
A tool that ignores the proxy environment variables cannot connect from inside the sandbox

sources.title: Run Claude Code programmatically (Claude Code docs)

--bare skips hooks, skills, plugins, MCP servers, auto memory and CLAUDE.md; Amazon Bedrock credentials are still read as usual
--output-format stream-json emits newline-delimited JSON; the last line is a result message with cost and session metadata
dontAsk denies every call that would otherwise prompt
On SIGTERM Claude Code terminates the process tree of a running Bash command and exits with code 143

sources.title: workerd, Cloudflare's JavaScript/Wasm Runtime (README at v1.20261012.1)
supports: workerd is a JavaScript / Wasm server runtime based on the same code that powers Cloudflare Workers
Its stated uses: an application server to self-host applications designed for Cloudflare Workers, a development tool, and a programmable HTTP proxy

WARNING: workerd is not a hardened sandbox. It tries to isolate each Worker, but on its own does not contain suitable defense-in-depth against implementation bugs; to run possibly-malicious code you must run it inside an appropriate secure sandbox, such as a virtual machine
When one nanoservice calls another, the callee runs in the same thread and process
Updating workerd never breaks existing code; the version number is a date, the maximum compatibility date that version supports
Configuration is a file in Cap'n Proto text format; `workerd serve my-config.capnp` serves it
Prebuilt binaries are distributed via npm; on Linux they need glibc 2.35 or higher (Ubuntu 22.04, Debian Bookworm), on macOS 13.5 or higher
Tested on Linux and macOS (x86-64 and arm64) and Windows (x86-64)
For production the README suggests systemd, with sockets inherited through --socket-fd, and Restart=always

sources.title: workerd.capnp: the configuration schema (v1.20261012.1)
supports: A Config has services, sockets, v8Flags, extensions, autogates, and logging; a Service is a worker, a network, an external server, or a disk directory
A Worker has modules or a serviceWorkerScript, a required compatibilityDate, compatibilityFlags, bindings, globalOutbound, Durable Object namespaces and storage
Binding kinds include text, data, json, cryptoKey, service, durableObjectNamespace, kvNamespace, r2Bucket, queue, analyticsEngine, hyperdrive, fromEnvironment, memoryCache, and workerLoader
kvNamespace, r2Bucket, and queue bindings turn operations into HTTP requests aimed at a service named in the configuration; workerd does not contain the stores
fromEnvironment takes the value from getenv() of the named variable; the binding is null if the variable is not set
Durable Object storage is none, inMemory (for local testing), or localDisk (marked EXPERIMENTAL); objects are always local to one instance of the runtime
A worker that inherits another runs in the same isolate as the base worker
The default globalOutbound is the service `internet`, which allows publicly routable addresses only
HttpOptions.forwardedProtoHeader names the header that tells the worker which protocol the original client used
The schema has no field that limits a worker's CPU time or memory (the only limits struct is MemoryCacheLimits)
`workerd compile` builds a self-contained binary from the workerd binary, a configuration, and its source code

sources.title: Cloudflare Workers: How Workers works
supports: V8 isolates are lightweight contexts; one instance of the runtime runs hundreds or thousands of them, and each isolate's memory is completely isolated
An isolate is created within an existing environment instead of a virtual machine per function, which eliminates the cold starts of the virtual machine model
Any given isolate can start around a hundred times faster than a Node process on a container or virtual machine, and on startup consumes an order of magnitude less memory
A single Workers instance may handle multiple requests, including concurrent requests, in a single-threaded event loop; Cloudflare recommends you do not use or mutate global state
Isolates may be evicted for resource limits on the machine, suspicious scripts, or individual resource limits
sources.note: Page last updated 2026-09-18.

sources.title: Cloudflare Workers: Security model
supports: V8 isolates prevent code from accessing memory outside the isolate, even within the same process, which lets Cloudflare run many isolates in a single process

Around the isolates Cloudflare adds: a process-level sandbox built from Linux namespaces and seccomp that prohibits all filesystem and network access, a supervisor process that mediates everything else, cordons that separate Workers by trust level into different processes, and process isolation for some Workers
Date.now() is locked in place while code executes, no other timers are provided, and there is no multi-threading, as defenses against Spectre
Cloudflare builds and deploys a new runtime after a V8 security patch within 24 hours
V8 creates a wider attack surface than virtual machines
sources.note: Page last updated 2026-09-18.

sources.title: Manual deployment: Start YB-Masters
supports: yb-master is started with --master_addresses, --rpc_bind_addresses, --fs_data_dirs and the --placement_cloud, --placement_region, --placement_zone flags, or with --flagfile
The number of nodes running YB-Masters, and of addresses in --master_addresses, must equal the replication factor
The masters discover each other and elect a Raft leader; the page tells you to add the start command to cron so the process is restarted if it goes down

sources.title: Manual deployment: System configuration
supports: chrony is the preferred NTP implementation; a YB-TServer or YB-Master shuts down when it detects clock skew larger than --max_clock_skew_usec (500 ms by default)
On cloud providers the provider's link-local time service should be used
Recommended limits include 1048576 open files and 12000 user processes; transparent hugepages should be enabled; on virtual machines vm.swappiness=0 and vm.max_map_count=262144
ClockBound is supported on AWS and optional; PTP is currently available only for AWS

sources.title: Deployment checklist
supports: The default replication factor is 3; with it a cluster tolerates one node failure, and needs at least as many nodes, YB-Masters and YB-TServers as the RF
Minimum 2 cores and 2 GB RAM; for production YSQL 16+ cores and 64 GB+ RAM
x86 and ARM (aarch64) are supported; SSDs are required, XFS recommended, noatime on data drives
On AWS use the M instance family and gp3 volumes of at least 250 GB; avoid T2 instance types
Nodes communicate on 7100 (YB-Master RPC) and 9100 (YB-TServer RPC); 5433 serves YSQL clients; 7000 is the YB-Master admin UI

sources.title: Operating system support
supports: Amazon Linux 2023 is supported in v2024.2.3 and later; AlmaLinux 8 is the default for YugabyteDB Anywhere-deployed nodes

sources.title: Create server certificates
supports: Each node needs ca.crt, node.<commonName>.crt and node.<commonName>.key, where the common name is the node's address
The example issues the root and the node certificates with openssl for 3650 days; the page does not describe rotation

sources.title: Enable server-to-server encryption
supports: use_node_to_node_encryption and use_client_to_server_encryption default to false; allow_insecure_connections defaults to true and, set to false, keeps any service with unencrypted communication from joining
certs_dir names the directory with the certificates

sources.title: Transaction isolation levels
supports: YSQL supports Serializable, Snapshot and Read Committed; Snapshot maps to the SQL Repeatable Read level
For manually deployed universes yb_enable_read_committed_isolation defaults to false, and Read Committed falls back to the stricter Snapshot isolation

sources.title: Concurrency control
supports: With wait queues a transaction waits for the conflicting ones to finish, then proceeds only if they made no conflicting permanent change, and otherwise aborts
A statement that is the first of its transaction is retried internally with a later snapshot

sources.title: Transaction retries in YSQL
supports: 40001 (serialization failure) and 40P01 (deadlock detected) are to be handled by rolling back and retrying the whole transaction with backoff
A COMMIT must not be retried blindly, because it is unclear whether the commit happened

sources.title: Synchronous replication in DocDB
supports: A tablet has as many peers as the replication factor; they form a Raft group and elect a leader
A write is applied after its Raft log entry is replicated to and persisted on a majority of the peers
Tolerating f fault domains needs a replication factor of at least 2f + 1
Only the tablet leader processes user-facing reads and writes by default; the stated recovery time after a zone outage is 3 seconds

sources.title: Transactions overview
supports: Every update is a transaction; timestamps come from hybrid logical clocks that combine physical time and a logical counter, and nodes exchange them on every RPC
Conflict resolution between concurrent transactions depends on the maximum clock skew in the cluster

sources.title: Hash and range sharding
supports: Tables are split into shards called tablets; the primary key of a row decides its tablet
Hash sharding spreads rows evenly over the 2-byte hash space 0x0000 to 0xFFFF; range sharding keeps rows in primary key order

sources.title: YB-Master service
supports: YB-Master keeps the system metadata, the map from tablets to servers, balances load and re-replicates the data of a failed server; it is not in the I/O path
The masters form a Raft group of their own

sources.title: YugabyteDB node-postgres smart driver
supports: @yugabytedb/pg is built on node-postgres and adds cluster-aware and topology-aware connection load balancing (loadBalance, topologyKeys, ybServersRefreshInterval)

sources.title: Change cluster configuration
supports: Moving to new nodes uses change_blacklist ADD, get_load_move_completion, and change_master_config ADD_SERVER / REMOVE_SERVER one master at a time
A new master is started without master_addresses and joins through ADD_SERVER; tserver_master_addrs must then be updated on every tablet server

sources.title: Replace a failed YB-Master
supports: The replacement is started with an empty --master_addresses; if the failed master is already dead, REMOVE_SERVER comes before ADD_SERVER
--tserver_master_addrs has to be updated on every YB-TServer to the new set of masters

sources.title: Replace a failed YB-TServer
supports: Start a new YB-TServer in the same placement, blacklist the failed one, wait for get_load_move_completion to reach 100, then remove the blacklist entry
The master leader marks a server DEAD after it has not responded for one minute

sources.title: Upgrade YugabyteDB
supports: A rolling upgrade restarts the YB-Masters one at a time, then the YB-TServers one at a time, pausing at least 60 seconds between nodes
It is finalized with `yb-admin promote_auto_flags` and `yb-admin upgrade_ysql`; after finalizing there is no rollback, and the monitoring phase should not exceed two days
post_install.sh is run after the archive is extracted

sources.title: Distributed snapshots for YSQL
supports: Snapshots are per database and use hard links on the cluster's own volumes; they do not protect against file system corruption or hardware failure
Moving a snapshot off the cluster is manual: the schema with ysql_dump, the metadata with export_snapshot, and the snapshot directories of every tablet copied by hand

sources.title: Firecracker README (v1.17.0)
supports: Firecracker is a virtual machine monitor that uses KVM to create and run microVMs, and excludes unnecessary devices and guest-facing functionality
It was developed at Amazon Web Services to accelerate the speed and efficiency of services like AWS Lambda and AWS Fargate, and is open source under Apache 2.0
One Firecracker process exposes an API endpoint; the defaults are 1 vCPU and 128 MiB
What the API can configure, including rate limiters for virtio devices, a vsock, an entropy device, pmem, memory hotplug
The jailer applies a cgroup and namespace barrier and drops privileges
Tested platforms are EC2 .metal instances of Intel, AMD and Graviton generations with host kernels 5.10, 6.1 and 6.18; 8th generation Intel only with 6.1 or 6.18
The security of microVMs depends on a well configured Linux host

sources.title: Firecracker Specification (v1.17.0)
supports: On M5D.metal and M6G.metal: the VMM starts within 8 CPU ms, with wall-clock from 6 ms to 60 ms
For 1 vCPU and 128 MiB with the Firecracker-tuned kernel: VMM memory overhead <= 5 MiB, depending on workload and configuration
<= 125 ms from the InstanceStart call to the start of /sbin/init, measured with the serial console disabled and a minimal kernel and root file system
Guest CPU performance > 95% of bare metal, marked integration test pending
The API conforms to the in-tree OpenAPI specification

sources.title: Firecracker Design (v1.17.0)
supports: Each Firecracker process encapsulates one and only one microVM; threads are API, VMM and one per vCPU
Up to 32 vCPUs; 5 microVMs per host core per second with a minimal kernel, one vCPU and 128 MiB
Network devices are backed by TAP devices and block devices by files on the host
All vCPU threads are considered to run malicious code once started; Firecracker does not filter network traffic
Rate limiters are two token buckets, operations per second and bandwidth
Seccomp filters are installed by Firecracker; the jailer sets up cgroups and chroot, drops privileges, and execs Firecracker
In production builds the serial console is not exposed

sources.title: Firecracker FAQ (v1.17.0)
supports: Lambda launched in November 2014 with per-customer EC2 instances for isolation
Firecracker started from crosvm and is written in Rust
Only 6 emulated devices are named: virtio-net, virtio-balloon, virtio-block, virtio-vsock, serial console, and a minimal keyboard controller
Guest and host must have the same CPU architecture
Firecracker does not support guest reboot; on x86 `reboot` with reboot=k ends the process
The serial console is disabled by default for boot time
sources.note: The FAQ's list of six devices is shorter than the README's feature list of the same tag, which also names an entropy device and pmem.

sources.title: Firecracker Charter (v1.17.0)
supports: Mission: secure, multi-tenant, minimal-overhead execution of container and function workloads
Tenets: built-in security, light-weight virtualization, minimalist in features, compute oversubscription

sources.title: Firecracker LICENSE and NOTICE (v1.17.0)

sources.title: Getting Started with Firecracker (v1.17.0)
supports: Firecracker requires read/write access to /dev/kvm and supports x86_64 and aarch64 Linux
The guide suggests an EC2 c5.metal instance and says EC2 only supports KVM on .metal instance types
The commands that fetch a kernel and an Ubuntu rootfs from the project's CI bucket, add an SSH key, and build an ext4 image
The TAP device, 172.16.0.1/30, NAT, the guest MAC 06:00:AC:10:00:02 and the guest address 172.16.0.2
The API calls of a boot: logger, boot-source, drives, network-interfaces, actions InstanceStart; requests are handled asynchronously
--config-file configures and starts a microVM without API requests
The integration tests enforce the specification as measured on EC2 .metal instances
sources.note: The statement about .metal conflicts with the EC2 user guide's nested virtualization page read the same day.

sources.title: Firecracker development machine setup (v1.17.0)
supports: Development needs a bare-metal machine or a virtual machine with nested virtualization; the AWS section uses bare metal instances

sources.title: The Firecracker Jailer (v1.17.0)
supports: The jailer's arguments and its steps: close file descriptors, clean the environment, copy the binary into a chroot, set resource limits, create cgroups, pivot_root, mknod /dev/net/tun and /dev/kvm, join a network namespace, drop privileges, exec
Copying the binary ensures the process shares no memory with another Firecracker process

sources.title: Production Host Setup Recommendations (v1.17.0)
supports: Firecracker should be started with the jailer in production, or under constraints at least as restrictive
Each Firecracker process should correspond to a workload of a single tenant
Firecracker cannot mitigate the host's hardware vulnerabilities; SMT and kernel samepage merging should be disabled for tenant separation
Firecracker does not filter guest traffic; a rule dropping packets from TAP devices to 169.254.169.254 is given
The serial device should not be enabled in production

sources.title: Firecracker Snapshotting (v1.17.0)
supports: A snapshot is a guest memory file and a microVM state file; disk files are managed by the user
Loading maps the memory file MAP_PRIVATE, so pages load on demand and writes go to anonymous memory
Pause, Resume and CreateSnapshot only after boot; LoadSnapshot only before configuration
Diff snapshots are in developer preview
Resuming the same snapshot more than once is considered insecure without a mechanism for uniqueness; VMGenID reseeds the guest kernel's PRNG on Linux 5.18 and later
Network connectivity is not guaranteed after resume

sources.title: Firecracker kernel support policy (v1.17.0)

sources.title: Firecracker: Lightweight Virtualization for Serverless Applications (NSDI '20)
supports: Lambda first isolated functions with Linux containers and customers with virtual machines
Containers trade security against compatibility through the syscalls they allow; language VM isolation was unsuitable because Lambda and Fargate run arbitrary binaries
Firecracker has no BIOS, cannot boot arbitrary kernels, emulates no legacy devices nor PCI, and supports no VM migration (as of the paper)
Each Lambda worker runs hundreds or thousands of microVMs, each a slot for one function and one concurrent invocation, reused for serial invocations
A pool of pre-booted microVMs hides boot latency; slots lived at most 12 hours
Measured with Firecracker v0.20.0 on m5d.metal: memory overhead around 3 MB; boot figures; block and network throughput
The seccomp profile then allowed 24 syscalls and 30 ioctls
Lambda migrated to Firecracker on EC2 bare metal instances starting in 2018

The isolation technologies listed: cgroups, namespaces, seccomp-bpf, iptables, chroot, Firecracker rate limiting
